globals.name: nf
globals.doc: The NetherForge API: events, timers, tasks and saved data, and a namespace under it for each part of the server (`nf.players`, `nf.worlds`, …; see `nf` for them all).

globals.name: require
globals.doc: Loads a project module or one of its files, or a file beside a resource's script, and returns what it returned. `require("greeter")` is `modules/greeter/init.lua`; `require("greeter.messages")` is `modules/greeter/messages.lua`. The caller's own files come first: inside a module, its own (`require("util")`); in a centity's, menu's, dialog's or item's script, the `.lua` files in the script's folder (`require("helpers")` in `centities/tower/script.lua` is `centities/tower/helpers.lua`, or `helpers/init.lua`). A module runs once: everyone who requires it gets the running one, state and all. A file beside a script runs as part of it, once per copy of the script, with its globals and its `this`: each centity instance, menu window and dialog has its own. Requiring the script's own file, a circular require, or anything outside the project's Lua is an error.

globals.name: log
globals.doc: Writes a line to the server console (and the editor's, with the file and line it came from). Arguments are converted with `tostring` and joined with tabs.

globals.name: vec3
globals.doc: Builds a `Vec3`: `vec3(x, y, z)`. Also holds the common vectors (`vec3.zero`, `vec3.up`, `vec3.north`, …) and `vec3.from_yaw_pitch`.

classes.name: nf
classes.doc: Everything outside the script itself. The core verbs (events, timers, tasks and waiting, saved data, the budget) are on `nf`; everything else is grouped into namespaces under it: `nf.server`, `nf.commands`, `nf.players`, `nf.worlds`, `nf.structures`, `nf.centities`, `nf.menus`, `nf.dialogs`, `nf.items`, `nf.blocks`, `nf.recipes`, `nf.loot`, `nf.bossbars`, `nf.teams`, `nf.schedule`, `nf.economy`, `nf.placeholders`, `nf.particles`, `nf.cutscenes`, `nf.files`, `nf.text`, `nf.json`, `nf.http`, `nf.time`, `nf.random`, `nf.math` and `nf.test`. Plain functions on tables, so call them with a dot: `nf.players.online()`.

fields.name: server
fields.doc: The server itself: its clock, its performance, its version, its settings (players, message of the day, whitelist), and saying or running things as the console.

fields.name: commands
fields.doc: Slash commands a module adds to the server for as long as it runs, with typed arguments, tab completion and usage messages from their declaration.

fields.name: players
fields.doc: Players: everyone online, or anyone who has ever joined.

fields.name: worlds
fields.doc: The server's worlds: finding them, and making, loading and copying them.

fields.name: structures
fields.doc: Structures: saved boxes of blocks that `world:place_structure` places. The project's are `structures/<id>.nbt`; scripts save more with `world:save_structure`.

fields.name: centities
fields.doc: Centity instances: spawning new ones and finding live ones.

fields.name: menus
fields.doc: The project's menus (`menus/<id>/`), and menus scripts make.

fields.name: dialogs
fields.doc: The project's dialogs (`dialogs/<id>/`), and dialogs scripts make.

fields.name: items
fields.doc: The project's items (`items/<id>/`): item kinds of its own, whose stacks the server can always tell apart from any other stack of the same Minecraft kind.

fields.name: blocks
fields.doc: The project's blocks (`blocks/<id>/`): blocks of its own, drawn by its resource pack, with their own hardness, drops and sounds, held in the world as note block states. A player places one with an item whose `block` names it, or a script with `ProjectBlock:place`.

fields.name: recipes
fields.doc: The project's recipes: those in `recipes/<id>.json`, and those scripts register. A recipe can take the project's own items as ingredients (`{ item = "ruby" }`), which only a stack of that item fits, however it looks; and a recipe takes a project item only where it names it, so a ruby built on paper never crafts as paper. Players see a recipe in their recipe book once they've discovered it (`player:discover_recipe`), but can craft it either way.

fields.name: loot
fields.doc: Loot tables: the project's own (`loot/<id>.json`) and the game's. A roll picks from each of a table's pools, weighing its entries against each other, and gives the items it picked. The same `seed` always gives the same items (the editor rolls the same way). A table the project doesn't have, or that the game doesn't, is an error; so is a game table that needs something the roll doesn't say (a mob's table needs the mob, as `looted`).

fields.name: bossbars
fields.doc: Boss bars: bars across the top of players' screens.

fields.name: teams
fields.doc: The project's scoreboard teams: prefixes and suffixes on names, name colours and glow colours, friendly fire, name tags and collision.

fields.name: schedule
fields.doc: Runs a function at a time of day, every day or week, or by a cron expression: real time, as opposed to ticks (`nf.after`, `nf.every`). Times are in the server owner's time zone (`schedules.time-zone` in `config.yml`, the server's own zone by default), not the player's. Daylight saving follows the zone's rules. A daily or weekly time the clocks skip runs the same distance after the gap begins (`"02:30"` runs at 03:30 on the day clocks jump from 02:00 to 03:00), and one that happens twice runs the first time only. A cron expression matches the clock as it reads: a time the clocks skip doesn't happen that day, one for a single time of day that happens twice (`"30 1 * * *"`) runs the first time only, and one that matches every half hour keeps matching through an hour that repeats. A schedule belongs to the script that made it and ends when that script unloads (a reload, the server stopping), so the script's body makes it again. It's checked once a tick, so a callback runs within a tick (50 ms) of its time. A run the server missed (it was off at the time) is skipped, unless the schedule has `catch_up = true` and an `id`: then it runs once, on start. What a schedule last ran is kept in the server's store by `id`, per package.

fields.name: economy
fields.doc: Players' money, as the server's economy plugin keeps it, through [Vault](https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/vault.34315/): whichever economy is registered with it (EssentialsX, CMI, …) answers, so a project never names one. Needs Vault and an economy plugin. The plugin has to be on the server and enabled: a package that declares it (`requires`) while it isn't is a problem on the project's problem list until it is, and calling without it is an error. A plugin that is enabled after NetherForge counts from then on. The economy is looked up when it's asked, so one that registers late (after NetherForge starts) works from then on. Amounts are plain numbers in the economy's own currency; a player who is offline works as well as one who is online.

fields.name: placeholders
fields.doc: Placeholders, through [PlaceholderAPI](https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/placeholderapi.6245/): fill in the `%player_name%`-style placeholders every plugin offers, and offer your own as `%<namespace>_<key>%` to every plugin that reads them (scoreboards, chat formats, holograms). Needs PlaceholderAPI. The plugin has to be on the server and enabled: a package that declares it (`requires`) while it isn't is a problem on the project's problem list until it is, and calling without it is an error. A plugin that is enabled after NetherForge counts from then on.

fields.name: particles
fields.doc: The project's particle effects (`particles/<id>/effect.json`): timelines of particles authored in the editor, played at a place by scripts.

fields.name: cutscenes
fields.doc: The project's cutscenes (`cutscenes/<id>.json`): camera paths keyed in the editor, played for one player at a time.

fields.name: files
fields.doc: Files in the one directory scripts may keep things in: the only state a script has that survives a restart.

fields.name: text
fields.doc: Helpers for the MiniMessage text players see: escaping what players typed, stripping tags, resource pack glyphs, and measuring.

fields.name: json
fields.doc: JSON text to and from Lua values.

fields.name: http
fields.doc: Requests to web services (a Discord webhook, a status API). A package declares the hosts it talks to in `netherforge.json`'s `requires` (`"http": ["discord.com"]`, or `"*.discord.com"` for every name under it), and the server owner sees every host the project and its packages declare when it starts (`/nf requires`); a request to any other host is an error. Every request is held to the package whose code makes it. The server looks a name up once, checks the addresses it leads to and connects to exactly the address it checked: a loopback, private, link-local, shared (`100.64.0.0/10`), unique-local or IPv4-mapped address is refused even when its name is declared, unless the server owner turned on `http.allow-private-addresses` in `config.yml` (for a service on the same machine or network). Redirects (at most 5) are followed, and each one is held to the same rules, host declaration included. The server's proxy settings are never used. Only `http` and `https` URLs work. The server owner also limits requests in `config.yml`'s `http:` section: how large a request and a response may be, how long a request may take, and how many a package may make a minute.

fields.name: time
fields.doc: Dates and durations as text, in the same unit as `nf.server.unix_time()`: milliseconds. For timers, use ticks (`nf.after`, `nf.wait`); this is for showing and reading clock times and lengths of time.

fields.name: random
fields.doc: Randomness `math.random` doesn't give: generators of your own that repeat for a seed, smooth noise, and random ids.

fields.name: math
fields.doc: Small arithmetic `math` doesn't have, for animating by hand: blending, clamping, rescaling and easing.

fields.name: test
fields.doc: What a test file runs on. A project's tests are the `*_test.lua` files anywhere in it (`tests/shop_test.lua`), run by `netherforge test` (or the editor's Run tests) on a fake server: no Minecraft, no network, a world that holds only what the test puts in it. A test file runs like a module (it can `require` the project's modules, and files beside it) and registers its tests with `nf.test.case`; each test runs alone, on a fresh server with the project loaded and its scripts started, so one can never leave something behind for the next. The file's own code runs once for every test, before it, so it's where to `require` and build what the tests share. Nothing here exists on a real server: `nf.test` is `nil` there.

events.name: tick
events.doc: Every server tick, twenty times a second. Keep handlers cheap, or listen less often with `{ every = n }`.

events.name: unload
events.doc: This script is about to stop: a reload, the server stopping, its centity being removed, or its menu window going. Delivered only to the script that registered it, last of all. Put back anything it changed outside itself.

events.name: player_join
events.doc: A player joined the server. Assign `event.message` to change what everyone is told, or `nil` to say nothing.

events.name: player_quit
events.doc: A player left. Assign `event.message` to change what everyone is told, or `nil` to say nothing.

events.name: player_chat
events.doc: A player is saying something in chat. `event:cancel()` stops anyone seeing it; assign `event.message` to change what they said, or `event.format` to change how the line looks. Handlers run on the main thread while the chat waits for them, so keep them quick.

events.name: player_interact
events.doc: A player clicked a block or the air (not an entity), once for each hand the game asks about. `event:cancel()` stops it: no door opens, nothing is placed or used. A right click with an item goes on to `player_use_item` unless it was cancelled.

events.name: player_interact_entity
events.doc: A player right-clicked an entity that isn't part of a centity (those are `centity_click`): after the entity's `interact` and the player's `interact_entity`. `event:cancel()` stops what the click would do.

events.name: player_move
events.doc: A player moved into another block: walking, swimming, flying, falling, riding. Only moves that change block are heard, not every step or turn of the head, and teleports are `player_teleport` instead. `event:cancel()` puts them back where they were. The server only watches moves while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise.
events.example:
nf.on("player_move", function(event)
  if event.to.position.y < 0 then
    event:cancel()
  end
end)

events.name: player_teleport
events.doc: A player is being teleported: a command, a script, an ender pearl, a portal. `event:cancel()` keeps them where they are; assign `event.to` to send them somewhere else.

events.name: player_change_world
events.doc: A player arrived in another world: through a portal, or teleported there.

events.name: player_death
events.doc: A player died: before `nf.on("entity_death")` hears the same death. Assign `event.message` to change what everyone is told (or `nil` for nothing), `event.keep_inventory` to let them keep what they carry, and `event.drops` to change what falls.
events.example:
nf.on("player_death", function(event)
  event.keep_inventory = true
  event.message = "<red>" .. nf.text.escape(event.player:name()) .. " will be back"
end)

events.name: player_respawn
events.doc: A player is coming back after dying, or after leaving the end. Assign `event.location` to bring them back somewhere else.

events.name: player_drop_item
events.doc: A player is dropping an item from their inventory. `event:cancel()` keeps it in their inventory.

events.name: player_pickup_item
events.doc: A player is picking up a dropped item. `event:cancel()` leaves it lying there (it is asked again while they stand on it).

events.name: player_use_item
events.doc: A player right-clicked with an item, on a block or the air, after `player_interact`: starting to eat or drink, drawing a bow, throwing a pearl, emptying a bucket, placing a block. `event:cancel()` stops the item being used, but not what the click does to the block (a door still opens).

events.name: player_consume_item
events.doc: A player finished eating or drinking something. `event:cancel()` stops it: the item stays and does nothing.

events.name: player_swap_hands
events.doc: A player pressed the key that swaps the items in their hands. `event:cancel()` leaves them where they are, so the key can be used for something else.

events.name: player_sneak
events.doc: A player started or stopped sneaking.

events.name: player_command
events.doc: A player typed a command (any command: Minecraft's, a plugin's or a script's), before it runs. `event:cancel()` stops it running.

events.name: block_break
events.doc: A player is breaking a block: after the world's own `block_break` handlers. `event:cancel()` stops it; assign `event.drops` and `event.experience` to change what it drops.
events.example:
nf.on("block_break", function(event)
  if event.block:kind() == "minecraft:diamond_ore" then
    event:cancel()
  end
end)

events.name: block_place
events.doc: A player is placing a block: after the world's own `block_place` handlers. `event:cancel()` stops it.

events.name: entity_damage
events.doc: Something is hurting an entity (a player included): after the entity's own `damage` handlers. `event:cancel()` stops it; assign `event.amount` to change how much it takes.
events.example:
nf.on("entity_damage", function(event)
  if event.cause == "fall" and event.entity:is_player() then
    event.amount = event.amount / 2
  end
end)

events.name: entity_death
events.doc: An entity died (a player included): after the entity's own `death` handlers, and for a player after `player_death`. Assign `event.drops` and `event.experience` to change what it drops.

events.name: entity_spawn
events.doc: An entity is coming into a world (not a player joining, and never the entities centities are drawn with): after the world's own `entity_spawn` handlers. `event:cancel()` stops it.

events.name: player_input
events.doc: A player's movement keys changed: what they hold down now, as their game sends it (forward, back, left, right, jump, sneak, sprint), whether or not they can move. For steering something they ride or controlling a centity. The server only watches input while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise.
events.example:
nf.on("player_input", function(event)
  if event.jump and event.sneak then
    event.player:send_message("<gray>dash!")
  end
end)

events.name: player_change_slot
events.doc: A player picked another hotbar slot: a number key or the scroll wheel. `event:cancel()` keeps the slot they had.

events.name: player_swing
events.doc: A player swung an arm: every left click, on a block, an entity or the air, and some right clicks. The one way to hear a left click on the air. `event:cancel()` stops others seeing the swing, but not what the click does.

events.name: player_sprint
events.doc: A player started or stopped sprinting.

events.name: player_fly
events.doc: A player started or stopped flying (in creative, or where `set_can_fly` lets them). `event:cancel()` keeps them as they were.

events.name: player_jump
events.doc: A player jumped. `event:cancel()` puts them back where they jumped from.

events.name: player_change_game_mode
events.doc: A player's game mode is changing: a command, a script, or the server. `event:cancel()` keeps the one they have.

events.name: player_change_food
events.doc: A player's food level is changing: going down as they get hungry, up as they eat. `event:cancel()` keeps it as it is; assign `event.food` to set it to another level.

events.name: player_gain_experience
events.doc: A player is getting experience points: picking up orbs, or from a script or command. Assign `event.amount` to give another amount (0 for none).

events.name: player_change_level
events.doc: A player's experience level changed, up or down.

events.name: player_kick
events.doc: A player is being kicked: by a command, a plugin or a script, or by the server (flying, timing out, a bad packet). `event:cancel()` keeps them on the server; assign `event.text` to change what their screen says, or `event.message` to change what everyone is told (`nil` for nothing). Leaving then goes on to `player_quit`.

events.name: player_complete_advancement
events.doc: A player completed an advancement (or a recipe was unlocked for them: those are advancements too, under `minecraft:recipes/`). Assign `event.message` to change what everyone is told, or `nil` to say nothing.

events.name: player_stop_using_item
events.doc: A player let go of an item they were using before it finished: a bow or crossbow drawn, a shield raised, a spyglass, food or a potion part-eaten. `event.ticks` says how long they held it.

events.name: player_break_item
events.doc: A tool, weapon or piece of armour a player was using wore out and broke. `event.item` is what it was, before it went.

events.name: entity_heal
events.doc: It is getting health back: eating, regenerating, a potion, a beacon. `event:cancel()` stops it; assign `event.amount` to change how much. After the entity's own `heal` handlers.

events.name: projectile_launch
events.doc: It launched a projectile: an arrow, a trident, a snowball, an egg, an ender pearl, a potion, a fireball. `event:cancel()` stops the projectile coming into the world. A dispenser's projectile has no shooter, so only `nf` hears it. After the entity's own `launch_projectile` handlers.

events.name: projectile_hit
events.doc: This projectile hit an entity or a block. `event:cancel()` lets it pass through as if nothing were there (an arrow flies on; a snowball doesn't break). After the entity's own `hit` handlers.

events.name: entity_shoot_bow
events.doc: It shot a bow or a crossbow (a skeleton, a pillager, a player). `event:cancel()` stops the shot: nothing is fired or used up. After the entity's own `shoot_bow` handlers.

events.name: entity_target
events.doc: This mob is picking a target to go after, or forgetting the one it had (`event.target` is `nil`). `event:cancel()` keeps the target it had. The server only reports targets while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. After the entity's own `target` handlers.

events.name: entity_explode
events.doc: It exploded: a creeper, TNT, a fireball, an end crystal, a wither skull. `event:cancel()` stops the explosion breaking anything; assign `event.breaks_blocks = false` to keep every block standing but still hurt what is near, or `event.yield` to change how much of what breaks drops. After the entity's own `explode` handlers.

events.name: block_explode
events.doc: A block exploded: a bed in the nether or the end, a respawn anchor charged away from the overworld. `event:cancel()` stops the explosion breaking anything; assign `event.breaks_blocks = false` to keep every block standing but still hurt what is near, or `event.yield` to change how much of what breaks drops. After the world's own `block_explode` handlers.

events.name: entity_combust
events.doc: It is catching fire: from lava or fire, sunlight (a zombie, a skeleton), a flaming arrow or a fire aspect sword. `event:cancel()` keeps it from burning; assign `event.ticks` to make it burn for that long instead. After the entity's own `combust` handlers.

events.name: entity_change_effect
events.doc: One of its status effects is being added, changed, run out or taken away: a potion, a beacon, milk, a command or a script. `event:cancel()` stops the change. After the entity's own `change_effect` handlers.

events.name: block_ignite
events.doc: A block is catching fire: flint and steel, a fire charge, lava, lightning, fire spreading, an explosion. `event:cancel()` keeps it from burning. After the world's own `block_ignite` handlers.

events.name: block_burn
events.doc: A block is burning away in a fire. `event:cancel()` keeps it there (it may still catch fire again). After the world's own `block_burn` handlers.

events.name: block_spread
events.doc: A block is spreading to another: grass, mycelium, moss, vines, mushrooms, fire, sculk. `event.block` is where it spreads to, `event.source` where from. `event:cancel()` stops it. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. After the world's own `block_spread` handlers.

events.name: block_flow
events.doc: Water or lava is flowing into another block (or a dragon egg teleporting there). `event:cancel()` stops it. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. After the world's own `block_flow` handlers.

events.name: block_grow
events.doc: A crop, sapling stage, sugar cane, cactus, bamboo, pumpkin or melon is growing by itself (bone meal included). `event:cancel()` stops it. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. After the world's own `block_grow` handlers.

events.name: block_fade
events.doc: A block is fading by itself: ice or snow melting, coral dying, fire burning out, farmland drying. `event:cancel()` keeps it as it is. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. After the world's own `block_fade` handlers.

events.name: block_form
events.doc: A block is forming by itself: snow falling, ice freezing, concrete setting, obsidian or cobblestone from lava, frost walker ice or a snow golem's trail (`event.entity` says which). `event:cancel()` stops it. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. After the world's own `block_form` handlers.

events.name: leaves_decay
events.doc: Leaves are decaying, far from any log. `event:cancel()` keeps them. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. After the world's own `leaves_decay` handlers.

events.name: piston_extend
events.doc: A piston is pushing out. `event:cancel()` keeps it in, and everything it would push where it is. After the world's own `piston_extend` handlers.

events.name: piston_retract
events.doc: A piston is pulling back. `event:cancel()` keeps it out, and (for a sticky one) the block it would pull where it is. After the world's own `piston_retract` handlers.

events.name: block_redstone
events.doc: A block's redstone power is changing: a lever, a button, a pressure plate, a redstone lamp or wire. Assign `event.to` to give it another power. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. After the world's own `block_redstone` handlers.

events.name: sign_change
events.doc: A player finished writing on a sign. `event:cancel()` keeps the sign as it was. After the world's own `sign_change` handlers.

events.name: block_start_break
events.doc: A player started hitting a block to break it. `event:cancel()` stops them breaking it; assign `event.instant = true` to break it at once, or `false` to make them wait for it. After the world's own `block_start_break` handlers.

events.name: block_drop_item
events.doc: A block a player broke is dropping its items, its contents included (a chest's, a furnace's): after `block_break`, once it has gone. `event:cancel()` drops nothing. After the world's own `block_drop_item` handlers.

events.name: weather_change
events.doc: It is starting or stopping raining (or snowing) in a world. `event:cancel()` keeps the weather it has. After the world's own `weather_change` handlers.

events.name: thunder_change
events.doc: A thunderstorm is starting or stopping in a world. `event:cancel()` keeps the weather it has. After the world's own `thunder_change` handlers.

events.name: lightning_strike
events.doc: Lightning is striking: a storm, a trident with channeling, a command or a script. `event:cancel()` stops it. After the world's own `lightning_strike` handlers.

events.name: chunk_load
events.doc: A chunk came into memory: someone came near, or it was generated for the first time (`event.generated`). The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. After the world's own `chunk_load` handlers.

events.name: chunk_generated
events.doc: A chunk was generated, the first time it was loaded: its terrain, structures and the game's decorations are in place, so a script can add its own (a centity in a grove, a shrine on a hill). Its blocks are `event.x * 16` to `event.x * 16 + 15` across, the same along `z`, and can be read and changed in the handler; the chunks beside it may not be generated yet, so keep what you place inside it. Once per chunk, ever: one generated while no script listened isn't heard later. It happens for every new chunk a player explores, so keep handlers quick and leave most chunks alone. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. After the world's own `chunk_generated` handlers.

events.name: chunk_unload
events.doc: A chunk is leaving memory, as everyone has gone away. Its blocks can still be read and changed in the handler. After the world's own `chunk_unload` handlers.

events.name: world_load
events.doc: A world was loaded: at startup, or by a plugin or a script later.

events.name: world_unload
events.doc: A world is being unloaded. Its handle answers `nil` or `false` afterwards; handlers on it stay, for when it's loaded again.

events.name: entity_mount
events.doc: It is getting on something to ride it: a horse, a pig with a saddle, a boat, a minecart, another mob (a spider jockey). `event:cancel()` keeps it off. After the entity's own `mount` handlers.

events.name: entity_dismount
events.doc: It is getting off what it rides: sneaking, the vehicle breaking, a teleport, dying. `event:cancel()` keeps it on, except where it can't stay (it died, or what it rode has gone). After the entity's own `dismount` handlers.

events.name: vehicle_move
events.doc: A boat or minecart moved into another block, with or without a rider. Only moves that change block are heard. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise.

events.name: vehicle_damage
events.doc: Something is hitting a boat or minecart. `event:cancel()` stops it; assign `event.amount` to change how much it takes.

events.name: vehicle_destroy
events.doc: A boat or minecart is being broken: it will drop as an item. `event:cancel()` keeps it there.

events.name: player_open_inventory
events.doc: A player is opening a vanilla inventory: a chest, a furnace, a crafting table, a villager's trades, a horse's. Not one of the project's menus: those are `menu_open`. `event:cancel()` keeps it closed.

events.name: player_close_inventory
events.doc: A player closed a vanilla inventory (not one of the project's menus: those are `menu_close`), or left the server with it open.

events.name: player_craft
events.doc: A player is taking what they crafted out of the result slot (with shift, as many as they can make). `event:cancel()` leaves it there and keeps the ingredients.

events.name: player_prepare_craft
events.doc: What's in a crafting grid changed (a crafting table's, or the 2×2 in a player's inventory), and the game is working out what it makes. Assign `event.result` to make something else, or `nil` for nothing: a recipe of your own.

events.name: player_prepare_anvil
events.doc: What is in an anvil changed (or the name typed into it), and the game is working out the result. Assign `event.result` to make something else (or `nil` for nothing), and `event.cost` to change how many levels it takes.

events.name: player_prepare_smithing
events.doc: What is in a smithing table changed, and the game is working out the result. Assign `event.result` to make something else, or `nil` for nothing.

events.name: player_prepare_grindstone
events.doc: What is in a grindstone changed, and the game is working out the result. Assign `event.result` to make something else, or `nil` for nothing.

events.name: player_enchant_item
events.doc: A player is enchanting an item at an enchanting table. `event:cancel()` stops it: nothing is enchanted or spent. Assign `event.cost` to change how many levels it takes.

events.name: furnace_smelt
events.doc: A furnace, smoker or blast furnace finished smelting one item. `event:cancel()` stops it: the item stays unsmelted. Assign `event.result` to make something else. After the world's own `furnace_smelt` handlers.

events.name: server_list_ping
events.doc: Someone's server list is asking about the server: what it says, how many are on and how many fit. `event:cancel()` doesn't answer, so the server shows as offline to them. The ping waits on the main thread for the handlers (at most two seconds, then it's answered as it was), so keep them quick. The server only waits while something listens.
events.example:
nf.on("server_list_ping", function(event)
  event.description = "<gold>Arena night</gold>\n<gray>" .. event.online .. " playing"
  event.max_players = event.online + 1
end)

events.name: centity_click
events.doc: A player clicked any centity: the end of a click's path, after the clicked node, the nodes above it and the centity itself, unless one of them called `event:stop()`.

events.name: centity_natural_spawn
events.doc: A centity is about to appear by itself, from the `spawning` block of its `centity.json`: once for each one of a group, before it exists. `event:cancel()` refuses it (it doesn't count against anything, and the spawner tries again later); assign `event.location` to move it. It is asked after the spawner has checked the place against the centity's rules, and before the centity's own `spawn`.
events.example:
nf.on("centity_natural_spawn", function(event)
  if event.centity == "wisp" and event.player:name() == "Notch" then
    event:cancel()
  end
end)

events.name: menu_open
events.doc: Someone opened any menu window: after that window's own `open` handlers.

events.name: menu_close
events.doc: Someone closed any menu window: after that window's own `close` handlers.

events.name: menu_click
events.doc: Someone clicked in any menu window: the end of a click's path, after the slot's and the menu's handlers, unless one of them called `event:stop()`. `event:cancel()` stops the click moving anything.

events.name: dialog_press
events.doc: Someone pressed any dialog's button: the end of a press's path, after the button's and the dialog's handlers, unless one of them called `event:stop()`.

events.name: setting_changed
events.doc: Whoever runs the server changed one of this package's settings (see `nf.config`): from the editor, with `/nf settings` or its dialog, or by editing the settings file and running `/nf settings reload`. Only the package's own scripts hear it. A script that listens keeps running and takes the new value from here; one that read a setting without listening is restarted instead, so what it set up with the old value is set up again.
events.example:
local greeting = nf.config("greeting")
nf.on("setting_changed", function(event)
  if event.setting == "greeting" then
    greeting = event.value
  end
end)

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this table doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: A built-in event's name, or a custom event's: any name with a `:` in it, like `"shop:purchased"`.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `nf.on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: A built-in event's name, or a custom event's: any name with a `:` in it, like `"shop:purchased"`.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

functions.name: emit
functions.doc: Raises a custom event for every script: every `nf.on(event)` handler hears it now, in the order they were registered, before this returns. The payload is handed to them as it is, not copied, so a field a handler assigns is there for the caller to read afterwards. A name without a `:` is an error: built-in events are the server's to raise.

params.name: event
params.doc: A custom event's name, with a `:`: `"shop:purchased"`.

params.name: payload
params.doc: The event's fields. Leave it out for none.

returns.doc: Whether a handler cancelled it (`event:cancel()`), so a custom event can be vetoed.

functions.example:
if not nf.emit("shop:purchased", { player = player, item = "ruby" }) then
  player:send_message("<green>Bought!")
end

functions.name: after
functions.doc: Calls `callback` once, `ticks` server ticks from now (20 ticks are a second). Timers stop when the script unloads. One that errors is logged. To do several things with pauses in between, start a task (`nf.task`) and `nf.wait` in it.

params.name: ticks
params.doc: How long to wait. 0 runs on the next tick.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop it first.

functions.name: every
functions.doc: Calls `callback` every `ticks` server ticks, starting `ticks` from now, until cancelled or the script unloads. One that errors is logged, and stops after 20 errors in a row.

params.name: ticks
params.doc: At least 1.

functions.name: task
functions.doc: Starts a task: `callback` runs now, with the extra arguments, until it first waits (`nf.wait`, `nf.wait_until`, `nf.wait_for`, `dialog:ask` or an asynchronous function like `nf.worlds.copy`, `nf.http.request`, `world:locate_biome`, `database:query`, `database:execute` or `database:transaction` called without its callback), and carries on from there when the wait is over. Only a task can wait; event handlers can't, because whether an event is cancelled or stopped has to be known when it returns, so a handler that needs to wait starts a task. Each time a task carries on it gets the script's whole instruction budget again. A task belongs to the script that started it and ends when that script unloads, when `cancel()` is called, or when the handle it waits on goes. One that errors is logged with its file and line and ends; the code that started it carries on either way.

params.name: callback
params.doc: The task: plain Lua that may wait.
Passed to `callback`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to end it early.

functions.example:
this:on("click", function(event)
  nf.task(function()
    this:play_animation("open")
    nf.wait_for(this, "animation_end")
    nf.wait(40)
    this:play_animation("close")
  end)
end)

functions.name: wait
functions.doc: Pauses the task for `ticks` server ticks (20 are a second). It can't wait inside a function the server or Lua itself calls back (a `complete` function, `table.sort`'s comparator), nor inside a coroutine of your own; inside `pcall` is fine.

params.name: ticks
params.doc: How long. 0 waits for the next tick, like 1.

functions.example:
nf.task(function()
  for i = 3, 1, -1 do
    nf.server.broadcast(tostring(i))
    nf.wait(20)
  end
  nf.server.broadcast("<green>Go!")
end)

functions.name: wait_until
functions.doc: Pauses the task until `predicate()` returns something other than `false` or `nil`. It's called once straight away and then once every tick, as the task's code.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Ticks to give up after. Leave it out to wait for as long as it takes.

returns.doc: `true` once `predicate` held, `false` when the timeout ran out first.

functions.example:
nf.task(function()
  if nf.wait_until(function() return #nf.players.online() >= 2 end, 20 * 60) then
    nf.server.broadcast("<green>Starting!")
  end
end)

functions.name: wait_for
functions.doc: Pauses the task until `event` next happens on `handle` (or, for `nf`, anywhere on the server) and returns that event. The task carries on straight away, while the event is still being delivered, so until its next wait it can still `cancel()` or `stop()` the event or set its writable fields. If the handle goes first (a removed centity, a closed window, a dialog taken away by a reload), the task ends. An event the handle doesn't have is an error.

params.name: handle
params.doc: What the event happens to, as for `handle:on`; `nf` for a server-wide event.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name, as `handle:on` takes it.

params.name: filter
params.doc: Waits for the first event this returns `true` for; the others pass by. Run as the task's code, so an error in it ends the task.

returns.doc: The event: its payload and its methods.

functions.example:
nf.task(function()
  local event = nf.wait_for(nf, "player_chat", function(e) return e.player == player end)
  player:send_message("You said " .. nf.text.escape(event.message))
end)

functions.name: data
functions.doc: A saved table for the whole project, by name: `nf.data("shop")` is the same table in every script, so a module keeps its own under its own name and two modules never collide. Each name is its own file in the data directory, kept across restarts. It may hold strings, numbers, booleans, tables of them (keyed by strings, or a list numbered from 1), and the API's own values: `Vec3`s, `Location`s, `Item` tables, and `Player`, `Entity`, `Centity` and `World` handles, which come back as the same types (a handle to something gone answers `nil` or `false`, as handles do). Anything else (a function, a `Menu` window, a `Subscription`) is skipped when it's saved, with a line in the log naming where it was (`data.inventory[3]: a function can't be saved`). The table is live: change it and the change is saved, at the next autosave (every five minutes), when the project reloads and when the server stops. It stays in memory across hot reloads rather than being read again, so a script that reloads finds it as it left it. A table that would take more than 1 MiB isn't saved (the last save stands), and the log says so. A name that isn't lowercase letters, digits and `_` (starting with a letter or digit, at most 64 characters) is an error.

params.name: name
params.doc: Which table, like `"shop"`.

functions.example:
local shop = nf.data("shop")
shop.sales = (shop.sales or 0) + 1
shop.last_buyer = event.player

functions.name: db
functions.doc: A database. With no name it is this package's own: a SQLite file that belongs to it alone (each package, a dependency included, has its own, under the server's `plugins/NetherForge/databases/`), whose tables come from the package's `migrations/NNN_name.sql`, run in order when the project loads. With a name it is one of the MySQL or PostgreSQL connections the server's owner set up under `databases:` in the plugin's `config.yml`: the script names it and never sees a host, a user or a password, and the connection opens only to the packages the owner lists for it. Either way it's the same `Database`, so the same calls work (the SQL is the server's own dialect; see `Database` for what differs). A name that isn't set up, or isn't open to this package, is an error.

params.name: name
params.doc: The connection, as the server owner named it in `config.yml`, like `"network"`. Leave it out for the package's own SQLite database.

functions.example:
local db = nf.db()
nf.task(function()
  local rows, err = db:query("SELECT count(*) AS total FROM scores")
  if rows then
    log("scores: " .. rows[1].total)
  else
    log("no scores: " .. err)
  end
end)

-- The same, on the shared MySQL or PostgreSQL server the owner called "network":
local network = nf.db("network")

functions.name: config
functions.doc: One of this package's settings: what whoever runs the server set it to, or its default when they haven't. Settings are declared in `netherforge.json`'s `settings` (each with a type, a default and a description) and changed by the server's owner, never by scripts; a package reads only its own. The value is a `boolean`, an `integer`, a `number` or a `string`, by the setting's type. A script that reads a setting and doesn't listen for `setting_changed` is restarted when that setting changes; one that listens hears the change instead. A name the package doesn't declare is an error.

params.name: name
params.doc: The setting's name, as `netherforge.json` declares it.

functions.example: local rolls = nf.config("treasure_rolls")

functions.name: instructions_left
functions.doc: Lua instructions this call may still run before it's stopped. A loop over a lot of work can check it and leave the rest for the next tick. Coarse: it's updated every hundred instructions or so.

classes.name: nf.server
classes.doc: The server itself: its clock, its performance, its version, its settings (players, message of the day, whitelist), and saying or running things as the console.

functions.name: tick
functions.doc: Server ticks since NetherForge started (20 a second): the clock to measure durations with. Use `nf.server.unix_time()` only for timestamps that must mean something after a restart.

functions.name: unix_time
functions.doc: The wall clock: milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC. For timestamps that outlive a restart (daily rewards, cooldowns saved to a file); measure durations in ticks.
functions.example:
local save = assert(nf.files.get("last_reward.json"))
save:write_json({ at = nf.server.unix_time() })

functions.name: ticks_per_second
functions.doc: How many ticks the server managed in the last second or so: 20 when it keeps up, less when it lags.

functions.name: tick_milliseconds
functions.doc: How long a tick has been taking lately, in milliseconds, averaged over the last few seconds. Over 50 means the server is lagging.

functions.name: minecraft_version
functions.doc: The running server's Minecraft version, like `"26.3"`.

functions.name: broadcast
functions.doc: Sends a line to everyone online and the console, as the server.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage, like `"<gold>The gate opens"`.

functions.name: run
functions.doc: Runs a server command as the console, with the console's permissions. The leading slash is optional.

params.name: command
params.doc: One command line.

returns.doc: Whether the server ran it.

functions.example: nf.server.run("time set day")

functions.name: max_players
functions.doc: How many players the server lets in at once: what the server list shows as its maximum.

functions.name: set_max_players
functions.doc: Changes how many players the server lets in at once, until it restarts (`server.properties` is left alone). Nobody online is kicked when it drops below how many there are.

params.name: count
params.doc: At least 0.

functions.name: motd
functions.doc: The message of the day: the text under the server's name in the server list, as MiniMessage.

functions.name: set_motd
functions.doc: Changes the message of the day, until the server restarts (`server.properties` is left alone). To change it for one ping only, listen to `server_list_ping`.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage; a line break starts the second line.

functions.example: nf.server.set_motd("<gold>Event tonight at 8!")

functions.name: is_whitelist_enabled
functions.doc: Whether the whitelist is on: only players on it (`player:is_whitelisted()`) and operators can join.

functions.name: set_whitelist_enabled
functions.doc: Turns the whitelist on or off. Turning it on doesn't kick anyone online who isn't on it.

classes.name: nf.commands
classes.doc: Slash commands a module adds to the server for as long as it runs, with typed arguments, tab completion and usage messages from their declaration.

functions.name: register
functions.doc: Adds `/name` to the server for as long as the module runs. Only modules can register commands, because a command outlives any one centity. The definition declares its arguments and subcommands; NetherForge checks what's typed against them, answers mistakes with a usage message, completes them as players type, and hands the handler typed values. Returns `false` when the name is already a command, the server's or another module's. A handler that errors is logged and whoever typed the command is told; the command stays. A name that isn't usable, or a definition with a mistake in it (an unknown key, an unknown argument type, an optional argument before a required one), is an error.

params.name: name
params.doc: Lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`, starting with a letter. Without the slash.

params.name: definition
params.doc: Description, permission, aliases, arguments and subcommands. Can be left out, with the handler in its place: `nf.commands.register(name, handler)`.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Runs when someone types the command (with no subcommand). Can be left out when the definition has subcommands: typing the bare command then shows its usage.

returns.doc: `true` once the command is registered.

classes.name: nf.players
classes.doc: Players: everyone online, or anyone who has ever joined.

functions.name: online
functions.doc: Everyone online.

functions.name: get
functions.doc: A player by name (any case) or UUID: anyone who has ever joined this server, online or not, or `nil` for someone who never has. For someone offline, `exists()` is `false` and what needs them in the world (`position()`, `send_message`) answers `nil` or `false` until they come back.

params.name: name_or_id
params.doc: A name, or a UUID like `player:id()`.

functions.example:
local owner = nf.players.get(saved.owner)
if owner and owner:exists() then
  owner:send_message("<gold>Your crop is ready")
end

functions.name: known
functions.doc: Everyone who has ever joined this server, online or not, in no particular order. On a server that's been running a long time that's a lot of players, so call it when you need it (building a leaderboard) rather than every tick.

functions.name: banned
functions.doc: Everyone who's banned, whose ban hasn't run out.

functions.name: whitelisted
functions.doc: Everyone on the server's whitelist, whether it's on or not.

classes.name: nf.worlds
classes.doc: The server's worlds: finding them, and making, loading and copying them.

functions.name: all
functions.doc: Every loaded world, the default one first.

functions.name: get
functions.doc: A world by name, or `nil` when the server has none by that name loaded.

params.name: name
params.doc: Its name: `"world_nether"`.

functions.name: create
functions.doc: Makes a new world, and loads it: from then on it's the project's, so it can unload it (`world:unload`), and it stays the project's across reloads and restarts. A name that isn't an id (lowercase letters, digits and `_`), or that a world already has (loaded, or saved on the server), is an error: `nf.worlds.load` loads a saved one. A `terrain` that isn't one of the project's terrains is an error, and so are both a `generator` and a `terrain`, a `terrain` with another environment than `"normal"`, and a `dimension_type` that isn't one of the project's dimension types or that the server didn't start with. Making a world takes the server a moment.

params.name: name
params.doc: Its name, which is also its folder: `"arena_1"`.

returns.doc: The new world, or `nil` when the server couldn't make it.

functions.example:
local arena = nf.worlds.get("arena_1")
  or nf.worlds.load("arena_1")
  or nf.worlds.create("arena_1", { generator = "void", structures = false })
local realm = nf.worlds.create("realm", { terrain = "ruby_hills", seed = 42 })

functions.name: load
functions.doc: Loads a world the server has saved but not loaded (one a script created and unloaded, or any other world the server has), and returns it; one already loaded is just returned. `nil` when the server has no world saved by that name. A name with characters a world's can't have is an error.

params.name: name
params.doc: Its name: `"lobby"`.

functions.name: copy
functions.doc: Makes a new world from one of the project's maps (`maps/<map>/`): its files are copied, then the server loads the copy as a world named `name`, the project's from then on (as for `nf.worlds.create`). A map there's none of, or a `name` that isn't an id or that a world already has (or that another copy is being made into), is an error at once. A copy that can't be made (the disk, or the server refusing it) fails, and the server's log says so too. It works off the main thread, so its world arrives later: give `callback`, which is called with `world, err` once it's done, or call it inside a task (`nf.task`) without one, and it waits and returns `world, err`. Without a callback outside a task, it's an error. When it fails, `world` is `nil` and `err` says why.

params.name: map
params.doc: Which map.

params.name: name
params.doc: The new world's name: `"arena_2"`.

params.name: callback
params.doc: Called on the main thread once it's done, as this script's code, with the new world (or `nil` and why not). Not called if the script has stopped by then.

functions.example:
nf.task(function()
  local arena, err = nf.worlds.copy("arena", "arena_2")
  if not arena then
    log("no arena: " .. err)
    return
  end
  local spawn = arena:spawn_location()
  if spawn then
    player:teleport(spawn)
  end
end)

returns.doc: Only without a callback, in a task: the new world, or `nil`.
Why it failed, when it did; `nil` when it worked.

functions.name: default
functions.doc: The server's main world: where things go when nothing says which.
functions.example:
local world = nf.worlds.default()
world:set_time_of_day(6000)

classes.name: nf.structures
classes.doc: Structures: saved boxes of blocks that `world:place_structure` places. The project's are `structures/<id>.nbt`; scripts save more with `world:save_structure`.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether there's a structure by that id: one of the project's, or one a script saved.

functions.name: size
functions.doc: How big a structure is, in blocks along x, y and z (before it's turned), or `nil` when there's none by that id. One whose file can't be read is an error.
functions.example:
local size = nf.structures.size("house")
if size then
  world:place_structure("house", here - vec3(size.x / 2, 0, size.z / 2))
end

classes.name: nf.centities
classes.doc: Centity instances: spawning new ones and finding live ones.

functions.name: spawn
functions.doc: Puts a new instance of a centity into the world. Its entities exist, its script's body has run and its `spawn` handlers have heard it by the time this returns. A centity the project doesn't have is an error.

params.name: kind
params.doc: Which centity: its folder name under `centities/`.

params.name: location_or_position
params.doc: Where its position (the anchor) goes: a `Location` (it faces the location's `yaw`, when it has one), or a position in the calling centity's world (the server's first world, in a module). Without a yaw it faces south (yaw 0).

returns.doc: The new instance, or `nil` when the world doesn't exist.

functions.example: local tower = nf.centities.spawn("tower", player:location():offset(vec3(2, 0, 0)))

functions.name: get
functions.doc: The live centity instance with this id, or `nil` once it's gone. Ids come from `centity:id()` and are fine to keep.

params.name: id
params.doc: An instance id.

functions.name: all
functions.doc: Every live centity instance, or those the filter picks. Includes the caller's own instance. A filter key that isn't one of `CentityFilter`'s is an error.

params.name: filter
params.doc: Only instances of one kind, in one world, or near a point.

functions.example:
for _, crate in ipairs(nf.centities.all({ kind = "crate", world = nf.worlds.default() })) do
  crate:remove()
end

classes.name: nf.menus
classes.doc: The project's menus (`menus/<id>/`), and menus scripts make.

functions.name: shared
functions.doc: The window of a menu whose file says `"shared": true`: the one every player sees. A menu that isn't shared has a window per player and no one to hand back, so this is `nil`; open one with `player:open_menu`. A menu the project doesn't have is an error.

params.name: menu
params.doc: Its folder name under `menus/`.

functions.example:
local stock = nf.menus.shared("bank")
if stock then
  stock:add_item({ kind = "minecraft:gold_ingot", count = 3 })
end

functions.name: create
functions.doc: Makes a menu from a table instead of a file: a `MenuTemplate`, which `player:open_menu(template)` opens a new window of, as often as you like. The table says what `menu.json` would, in Lua spelling: `type` (`"chest"`, the default, `"barrel"`, `"shulker_box"`, `"hopper"`, `"dispenser"`, `"dropper"` or `"crafter"`), `rows` (a chest's 1 to 6, default 3), `title` (MiniMessage), `skin` (`<pack>/<key>`), `locked` (default `true`) and `slots`, items by slot number from 0. A template has no script of its own: put handlers on it (`template:on("click", ...)`), and they hear every window made from it. It lasts as long as the script that created it. A key it doesn't take, a value of the wrong type, a slot outside the window, an item the server doesn't have or a skin the project's resource packs don't have is an error, checked by the same rules as `menu.json`.

params.name: definition
params.doc: `{ type?, rows?, title?, skin?, locked?, slots? }`: what the menu is, as `menu.json` would say it, with `slots` as `{ [index] = item }`.

classes.name: nf.dialogs
classes.doc: The project's dialogs (`dialogs/<id>/`), and dialogs scripts make.

functions.name: get
functions.doc: A dialog by id. There's one of each, so this always finds it; a dialog the project doesn't have is an error.

params.name: dialog
params.doc: Its folder name under `dialogs/`.

functions.example: nf.dialogs.get("welcome"):open_for(event.player)

functions.name: create
functions.doc: Makes a dialog from a table instead of a file. The table says what `dialog.json` would, in Lua spelling (`after_action`, `can_close_with_escape`, an input's `max_length`, items as `Item` tables): `title` (required), `type`, `body`, `inputs`, `buttons`, `columns`, `dialogs`, and the rest of the file's fields except `script`. The `Dialog` it returns works like any other: `open_for`, `ask`, `button(key)`, and `press` and `close` handlers on it and its buttons. Its id is made up and never names a folder under `dialogs/`. It lasts as long as the script that created it; after that its methods answer `nil` or `false` and its handlers are gone. A key it doesn't take, a value of the wrong type, or anything `dialog.json` would have an error for (two buttons with one key, a `dialog_list` naming a dialog there isn't) is an error.

params.name: definition
params.doc: What the dialog is, as `dialog.json` would say it, with its keys in snake_case.

classes.name: nf.items
classes.doc: The project's items (`items/<id>/`): item kinds of its own, whose stacks the server can always tell apart from any other stack of the same Minecraft kind.

functions.name: create
functions.doc: A stack of a project item, as an `Item` table with every field its file sets, `item` naming it, and `count` 1: hand it to `player:give_item`, `menu:set_item` or anything else that takes an item. `overrides` sets fields of this stack: its `count`, its own `data`, or any other field. A field the file sets too is the stack's only until the file changes: then the stack takes the file's look again, keeping its count, damage and `data` (see the item format). A project item the project doesn't have is an error.

params.name: item
params.doc: Its folder name under `items/`, or `namespace:id` for one a package it depends on exports (see [Names across packages](packages.md)).

params.name: overrides
params.doc: `Item` fields for this stack, like `{ count = 3 }`. Any `Item` field but `kind` and `item`.

functions.example: event.player:give_item(nf.items.create("ruby", { count = 3, data = { found = "cave" } }))

functions.name: id
functions.doc: Which project item a stack is (its `item` field), or `nil` for a stack that isn't one. A stack carries its project item wherever it goes, so this tells a ruby from any other paper.

params.name: stack
params.doc: An item table, as any event or inventory hands out.

functions.example:
nf.on("player_drop_item", function(event)
  if nf.items.id(event.item) == "ruby" then
    event:cancel()
  end
end)

functions.name: get
functions.doc: A project item by id, to listen to what players do with it (`nf.items.get("ruby"):on("use", ...)`), or `nil` when the project has no such item.

params.name: item
params.doc: Its folder name under `items/`, or `namespace:id` for one a package it depends on exports (see [Names across packages](packages.md)).

functions.name: all
functions.doc: Every item the calling script can use: its own package's, and those the packages it depends on export.

classes.name: nf.blocks
classes.doc: The project's blocks (`blocks/<id>/`): blocks of its own, drawn by its resource pack, with their own hardness, drops and sounds, held in the world as note block states. A player places one with an item whose `block` names it, or a script with `ProjectBlock:place`.

functions.name: get
functions.doc: A project block by id, to listen to what players do with it (`nf.blocks.get("ruby_ore"):on("break", ...)`) or to place one, or `nil` when the project has no such block.

params.name: block
params.doc: Its folder name under `blocks/`, or `namespace:id` for one a package it depends on exports (see [Names across packages](packages.md)).

functions.name: all
functions.doc: Every block the calling script can use: its own package's, and those the packages it depends on export.

classes.name: nf.recipes
classes.doc: The project's recipes: those in `recipes/<id>.json`, and those scripts register. A recipe can take the project's own items as ingredients (`{ item = "ruby" }`), which only a stack of that item fits, however it looks; and a recipe takes a project item only where it names it, so a ruby built on paper never crafts as paper. Players see a recipe in their recipe book once they've discovered it (`player:discover_recipe`), but can craft it either way.

functions.name: register
functions.doc: Adds a recipe the server learns at once, sent to everyone online. `definition` says what `recipes/<id>.json` would, in Lua spelling: `type` (`"shaped"`, `"shapeless"`, `"furnace"`, `"blasting"`, `"smoking"`, `"campfire_cooking"`, `"smithing_transform"` or `"stonecutting"`), then what that type takes: `pattern` and `key`, `ingredients`, `ingredient`, or `template`, `base` and `addition`; `result` (an `Item`), and `experience`, `cooking_time`, `group` and `category`. An ingredient is an item id (`"minecraft:stick"`), a tag (`"#minecraft:planks"`) or a project item (`{ item = "ruby" }`). Registering an id again replaces the recipe. It lasts as long as the script that registered it (so a reloaded script registers it again in its body). An id a `recipes/` file has, or anything that file would have an error for, is an error.

params.name: id
params.doc: Its id: lowercase letters, digits and `_`, like a file's name. Players discover it by this id.

params.name: definition
params.doc: What the recipe is, as `recipes/<id>.json` would say it, with its keys in snake_case.

functions.name: remove
functions.doc: Takes away a recipe a script registered, from the server and from everyone's recipe book. `false` when there's no such recipe; one from `recipes/` is the file's, so removing it is an error (delete the file instead).

params.name: id
params.doc: Its id.

functions.name: all
functions.doc: Every recipe's id: the project's files', then those scripts registered.

classes.name: nf.loot
classes.doc: Loot tables: the project's own (`loot/<id>.json`) and the game's. A roll picks from each of a table's pools, weighing its entries against each other, and gives the items it picked. The same `seed` always gives the same items (the editor rolls the same way). A table the project doesn't have, or that the game doesn't, is an error; so is a game table that needs something the roll doesn't say (a mob's table needs the mob, as `looted`).

functions.name: roll
functions.doc: Rolls a loot table and gives the items it picked, in the order it picked them: a stack each, more than one when a pick gives more than a stack holds. Nothing is put anywhere: give them to a player, drop them or fill a chest with them. A game table is rolled by the server where the context says (`location`, else its player's or looted entity's place), and needs one of them.

params.name: table
params.doc: A loot table of the project's (`"treasure"`, `loot/treasure.json`; a bare id is the calling package's own), one a package exports (`"acme:treasure"`), or one of the game's by its id (`"minecraft:chests/simple_dungeon"`).

params.name: context
params.doc: Who and what the roll is for: its player, tool, luck and seed. Leave it out for a roll with none of them.

functions.example:
local items = nf.loot.roll("treasure", { player = player, tool = player:equipment("main_hand") })
for _, item in ipairs(items) do
  player:inventory():add_item(item)
end

functions.name: fill
functions.doc: Rolls a loot table into an inventory the way the game fills a chest: each stack into an empty slot picked at random (from the roll's seed), leaving what's there. In a player's inventory only the hotbar and main inventory take loot. What finds no empty slot is left out. A game table is rolled where the inventory is, unless the context says otherwise.

params.name: table
params.doc: A loot table of the project's (`"treasure"`, `loot/treasure.json`; a bare id is the calling package's own), one a package exports (`"acme:treasure"`), or one of the game's by its id (`"minecraft:chests/simple_dungeon"`).

params.name: context
params.doc: Who and what the roll is for: its player, tool, luck and seed. Leave it out for a roll with none of them.

returns.doc: How many items didn't fit: 0 when all of it went in. `nil` once the inventory's gone, and then nothing is rolled.

functions.example:
local block = world:block(vec3(10, 64, 10))
local chest = block and block:inventory()
if chest then
  nf.loot.fill("treasure", chest, { luck = 1 })
end

classes.name: nf.bossbars
classes.doc: Boss bars: bars across the top of players' screens.

functions.name: create
functions.doc: Makes a boss bar, shown to no one yet (`bar:show_to(player)`). It belongs to this script and goes when it unloads. A key the options don't have is an error.
functions.example:
local bar = nf.bossbars.create({ text = "<red>The Warden", color = "red", progress = 1 })
for _, player in ipairs(nf.players.online()) do
  bar:show_to(player)
end

classes.name: nf.teams
classes.doc: The project's scoreboard teams: prefixes and suffixes on names, name colours and glow colours, friendly fire, name tags and collision.

functions.name: create
functions.doc: Makes a team on the server's scoreboard, with no members yet (`team:add_member`). It belongs to this script and goes when the script unloads, so make it in the script's body. A name that isn't letters, digits and `_`, `-`, `.` or `+`, a name one of the project's teams already has, or a key the options don't have is an error; to share a team between scripts, find it with `nf.teams.get` in the others.

params.name: name
params.doc: What the project calls it: `"red"`.

functions.name: get
functions.doc: One of the project's teams by name, or `nil` when it has none by that name.

functions.name: all
functions.doc: Every team the project has now, in the order they were made. Teams made with `/team` or by other plugins aren't among them.

classes.name: nf.schedule
classes.doc: Runs a function at a time of day, every day or week, or by a cron expression: real time, as opposed to ticks (`nf.after`, `nf.every`). Times are in the server owner's time zone (`schedules.time-zone` in `config.yml`, the server's own zone by default), not the player's. Daylight saving follows the zone's rules. A daily or weekly time the clocks skip runs the same distance after the gap begins (`"02:30"` runs at 03:30 on the day clocks jump from 02:00 to 03:00), and one that happens twice runs the first time only. A cron expression matches the clock as it reads: a time the clocks skip doesn't happen that day, one for a single time of day that happens twice (`"30 1 * * *"`) runs the first time only, and one that matches every half hour keeps matching through an hour that repeats. A schedule belongs to the script that made it and ends when that script unloads (a reload, the server stopping), so the script's body makes it again. It's checked once a tick, so a callback runs within a tick (50 ms) of its time. A run the server missed (it was off at the time) is skipped, unless the schedule has `catch_up = true` and an `id`: then it runs once, on start. What a schedule last ran is kept in the server's store by `id`, per package.

functions.name: daily
functions.doc: Calls `callback` every day at a time of day. Runs on the main thread, in the tick that finds the time has come, like an `nf.every` callback. One that errors is logged with its file and line; the schedule carries on.

params.name: time
params.doc: The time of day on a 24-hour clock, `"HH:mm"`: `"18:00"`, `"06:30"`.

params.name: options
params.doc: A table: `id` (a name that survives restarts, which `catch_up` needs) and `catch_up` (run once on start if a run was missed).

functions.name: weekly
functions.doc: Calls `callback` once a week, on a day at a time of day. Runs on the main thread, in the tick that finds the time has come, like an `nf.every` callback. One that errors is logged with its file and line; the schedule carries on.

params.name: day
params.doc: The weekday: `"mon"`, `"tue"`, `"wed"`, `"thu"`, `"fri"`, `"sat"` or `"sun"` (or written out, `"saturday"`), in any case.

params.name: time
params.doc: The time of day, as for `nf.schedule.daily`.

params.name: options
params.doc: A table: `id` (a name that survives restarts, which `catch_up` needs) and `catch_up` (run once on start if a run was missed).

functions.name: cron
functions.doc: Calls `callback` whenever a cron expression matches. Runs on the main thread, in the tick that finds the time has come, like an `nf.every` callback. One that errors is logged with its file and line; the schedule carries on.

params.name: expression
params.doc: Five fields, as Unix cron has them: minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week (`0` or `7` is Sunday; `MON`-`SUN` and `JAN`-`DEC` work), each `*`, a number, a list (`1,15`), a range (`9-17`) or a step (`*/10`, `0-30/5`). `"*/30 * * * *"` is every half hour; `"0 4 * * 1-5"` is 04:00 on weekdays. An expression that isn't valid is an error.

params.name: options
params.doc: A table: `id` (a name that survives restarts, which `catch_up` needs) and `catch_up` (run once on start if a run was missed).

classes.name: nf.economy
classes.doc: Players' money, as the server's economy plugin keeps it, through [Vault](https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/vault.34315/): whichever economy is registered with it (EssentialsX, CMI, …) answers, so a project never names one. Needs Vault and an economy plugin. The plugin has to be on the server and enabled: a package that declares it (`requires`) while it isn't is a problem on the project's problem list until it is, and calling without it is an error. A plugin that is enabled after NetherForge counts from then on. The economy is looked up when it's asked, so one that registers late (after NetherForge starts) works from then on. Amounts are plain numbers in the economy's own currency; a player who is offline works as well as one who is online.

functions.name: balance
functions.doc: How much money the player has: `0` for someone the economy has no account for.

params.name: player
params.doc: Online or not.

functions.example: player:send_message("You have " .. nf.economy.balance(player) .. " coins")

functions.name: deposit
functions.doc: Gives the player money. Returns their new balance, or `nil` when the economy refused (it has no account for them, or can't hold that much). An amount that isn't positive and finite is an error.

params.name: player
params.doc: Online or not.

params.name: amount
params.doc: More than 0.

returns.doc: their balance afterwards

functions.example:
local balance = nf.economy.deposit(player, 50)
if balance then
  player:send_message("Paid out. You have " .. balance)
end

functions.name: withdraw
functions.doc: Takes money from the player. Returns their new balance, or `nil` when the economy refused, usually because they don't have that much (nothing is taken then). An amount that isn't positive and finite is an error.

params.name: player
params.doc: Online or not.

params.name: amount
params.doc: More than 0.

returns.doc: their balance afterwards

functions.example:
if nf.economy.withdraw(player, 100) then
  player:send_message("<green>Bought")
else
  player:send_message("<red>You can't afford that")
end

classes.name: nf.placeholders
classes.doc: Placeholders, through [PlaceholderAPI](https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/placeholderapi.6245/): fill in the `%player_name%`-style placeholders every plugin offers, and offer your own as `%<namespace>_<key>%` to every plugin that reads them (scoreboards, chat formats, holograms). Needs PlaceholderAPI. The plugin has to be on the server and enabled: a package that declares it (`requires`) while it isn't is a problem on the project's problem list until it is, and calling without it is an error. A plugin that is enabled after NetherForge counts from then on.

functions.name: parse
functions.doc: Replaces every placeholder in the text with its value, as PlaceholderAPI does: `"Hello %player_name%"` becomes `"Hello Alex"`. A placeholder nobody answers is left as written. Placeholders registered with `nf.placeholders.register` are answered too. A value is plain text, not MiniMessage: if it comes from players, `nf.text.escape` the result before sending it as MiniMessage.

params.name: text
params.doc: Text with `%placeholders%` in it.

params.name: player
params.doc: Whom the placeholders are about (`%player_name%`); without one, only placeholders that don't need a player have a value.

functions.example:
local line = nf.placeholders.parse("Welcome, %player_name%! Rank: %vault_rank%", player)
player:send_message(nf.text.escape(line))

functions.name: register
functions.doc: Makes `%<namespace>_<key>%` a placeholder for the whole server: PlaceholderAPI asks `callback` for the value whenever any plugin parses it. `callback` is called with the `key` (everything after the first `_`, so `%shop_price_apple%` is `"price_apple"`) and the player it's for, if there is one, and returns the text (or a number) to put there, or `nil` when it has no value for that key (the placeholder is then left as written). It runs on the main thread when the server asks from the main thread; PlaceholderAPI is also asked from other threads (async chat, scoreboard plugins), where scripts can't run: there the placeholder answers the value `callback` last gave for that same key and player, and `nil` before it ever has. The placeholder belongs to the script that registered it and goes when that script unloads (a reload, the server stopping). A namespace another script or plugin already uses is an error.

params.name: namespace
params.doc: What comes before the first `_`: lowercase letters and digits, starting with a letter, at most 32 characters, like `"shop"`.

params.name: callback
params.doc: Gives the value. An error in it is logged with its file and line, and the placeholder is left as written for that request.

functions.example:
nf.placeholders.register("shop", function(key, player)
  if key == "sales" then
    return nf.data("shop").sales or 0
  end
  return nil
end)
-- %shop_sales% now works in any plugin that reads placeholders

classes.name: nf.particles
classes.doc: The project's particle effects (`particles/<id>/effect.json`): timelines of particles authored in the editor, played at a place by scripts.

functions.name: play
functions.doc: Starts playing an effect at a place, from its first tick. It plays for its `duration` (or, looping, until it's stopped) and belongs to the script that played it: when that script unloads, the effect ends (reason `"unloaded"`). Only players within 32 blocks see it (128 for an emitter with `force`), and of those only `viewers` when given. An effect the project doesn't have, a key `options` doesn't take, or an option out of range is an error, and so is an effect whose file has errors and never had a good version (one that did plays its last good version). More than 1024 effects playing on the server at once is an error too: stop the ones you're done with.

params.name: effect
params.doc: Which effect: its folder name under `particles/`.

params.name: location_or_position
params.doc: Where it plays: a `Location`, whose `yaw` and `pitch` turn the effect (nil is 0), or a position in the calling centity's world (the server's first world, in a module or a menu or dialog script).

params.name: options
params.doc: Who sees it, how big it is, whether it loops, and what it follows.

returns.doc: The playing effect, or `nil` when the world isn't loaded.

functions.example:
assert(this:node("lid")):on("click", function(event)
  nf.task(function()
    local here = this:location()
    local effect = here and nf.particles.play("shockwave", here)
    if effect then
      nf.wait_for(effect, "end")
    end
    this:play_animation("open")
  end)
  event:stop()
end)

classes.name: nf.cutscenes
classes.doc: The project's cutscenes (`cutscenes/<id>.json`): camera paths keyed in the editor, played for one player at a time.

functions.name: play
functions.doc: Starts a cutscene for a player, from its first moment. While it plays, the player spectates a camera that follows the cutscene's path, and can't move or interact. Their game mode, position, flying state and anything riding are put back when it ends, however it ends (including when they leave, a reload or the server stopping); someone who was riding something is dismounted and isn't put back on it. It belongs to the script that played it: when that script unloads, it ends (reason `"unloaded"`). A player who is already watching one has it end (reason `"replaced"`) and the new one start without putting them back first, so cutscenes chain without a flash of the world they were in. A cutscene the project doesn't have, a key `options` doesn't take, or one whose file has errors and never had a good version (one that did plays its last good version) is an error. A player who is offline, or a dead one, gets `nil`.

params.name: player
params.doc: Who watches.

params.name: cutscene
params.doc: Which cutscene: its file name under `cutscenes/`, without `.json`.

params.name: options
params.doc: Where the path is, and whether the player may skip it.

returns.doc: The playing cutscene, or `nil` when the player can't watch one.

functions.example:
nf.commands.register("intro", { players_only = true }, function(event)
  local player = assert(event.player)
  local intro = nf.cutscenes.play(player, "intro", { origin = player:location() })
  if intro then
    intro:on("end", function(done)
      done.player:send_message("<gold>Welcome to the village!")
    end)
  end
end)

functions.name: stop
functions.doc: Ends the cutscene a player is watching now, with reason `"stopped"`, and puts them back.

params.name: player
params.doc: Whose cutscene to end.

returns.doc: `false` when they were not watching one.

functions.name: current
functions.doc: The cutscene a player is watching now.

params.name: player
params.doc: Who.

returns.doc: `nil` when they are not watching one.

classes.name: nf.files
classes.doc: Files in the one directory scripts may keep things in: the only state a script has that survives a restart.

functions.name: get
functions.doc: A file or folder in the data directory, which survives restarts and reloads. A handle is a path, not an open file: nothing is read until you ask. Paths that would leave that directory (`..`, backslashes, names starting with a dot) give `nil` rather than an error. No argument is the directory itself.

params.name: path
params.doc: Relative, with `/` between folders.

functions.example:
local save = assert(nf.files.get("scores.json"))
local scores = save:read_json() or {}
scores[player:name()] = (scores[player:name()] or 0) + 1
save:write_json(scores)

classes.name: nf.text
classes.doc: Helpers for the MiniMessage text players see: escaping what players typed, stripping tags, resource pack glyphs, and measuring.

functions.name: escape
functions.doc: Escapes text so MiniMessage shows it as typed rather than reading tags in it. Use it on anything a player wrote (a name they chose, a dialog answer, a chat line) before putting it into MiniMessage: otherwise they can add colours, or worse, `<click:run_command:...>`.

params.name: text
params.doc: Plain text.

returns.doc: MiniMessage that reads as exactly that text.

functions.example: player:send_message("<green>Hello, " .. nf.text.escape(tostring(event.values.nickname)))

functions.name: strip
functions.doc: MiniMessage with its tags taken out: the plain text a player would read, for logs and comparisons.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage.

functions.name: glyph
functions.doc: The character a resource pack glyph is drawn as, for building text by hand.
