In MiniMessage text the tag `<glyph:ui/coin>` is usually simpler: it works anywhere text does (names, lore, chat, titles, dialogs, text displays) and draws the picture in its own colours, while this character is tinted by the text colour around it like any other (wrap it in `<white>` to avoid that). `nil` while the project's resource packs have errors (nothing is built then); a glyph no resource pack has is an error.

params.name: glyph
params.doc: `<pack>/<key>`, like `"ui/coin"`.

functions.example:
local coin = nf.text.glyph("ui/coin")
player:send_message("<white>" .. coin .. "</white> <gold>" .. balance)

functions.name: width
functions.doc: How wide a line of MiniMessage text draws in the game's default font, in pixels (GUI pixels: the font is 8 tall), for laying out menu titles and text displays. Tags draw nothing, except `<bold>` (a pixel more per character) and `<glyph:ui/coin>` (the glyph's own width); text with line breaks measures as its widest line. It reads the default font's widths from `fonts/default.json`, which the editor writes into the project from your Minecraft install. `nil` when it can't be measured exactly: that file is missing (open the project in the editor with Minecraft imported), or the text uses a character it doesn't cover.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage.

functions.example:
local width = nf.text.width("<bold>Shop")
if width then
  log("the title is " .. width .. " pixels wide")
end

classes.name: nf.json
classes.doc: JSON text to and from Lua values.

functions.name: encode
functions.doc: A value as JSON text, written the way a `data()` table is saved: tables numbered from 1 become arrays, other tables objects (with string keys, in order), and the API's own values one-key objects that `nf.json.decode` turns back into them: `vec3(1, 2, 3)` is `{"$vec3":[1,2,3]}`, and `Location`s and `Player`, `Entity`, `Centity` and `World` handles have tags of their own. A key of yours that would read as a tag (`"$vec3"`) is written with one more `$`; any other key (`"$ref"`) is written as it is. A value JSON can't hold (a function, another kind of handle, a table that contains itself, a number key outside a list) is an error naming where it was (`value.callback: a function can't be written as JSON`).
functions.example: log(nf.json.encode({ name = "crate", sizes = { 1, 2, 3 } }))

functions.name: decode
functions.doc: JSON text as a Lua value: objects and arrays become tables, and what `nf.json.encode` tags becomes a `Vec3`, `Location` or handle again. `nil` for text that isn't JSON (and for `null`), so text from a player or a file can be tried without guarding.

classes.name: nf.http
classes.doc: Requests to web services (a Discord webhook, a status API). A package declares the hosts it talks to in `netherforge.json`'s `requires` (`"http": ["discord.com"]`, or `"*.discord.com"` for every name under it), and the server owner sees every host the project and its packages declare when it starts (`/nf requires`); a request to any other host is an error. Every request is held to the package whose code makes it. The server looks a name up once, checks the addresses it leads to and connects to exactly the address it checked: a loopback, private, link-local, shared (`100.64.0.0/10`), unique-local or IPv4-mapped address is refused even when its name is declared, unless the server owner turned on `http.allow-private-addresses` in `config.yml` (for a service on the same machine or network). Redirects (at most 5) are followed, and each one is held to the same rules, host declaration included. The server's proxy settings are never used. Only `http` and `https` URLs work. The server owner also limits requests in `config.yml`'s `http:` section: how large a request and a response may be, how long a request may take, and how many a package may make a minute.

functions.name: request
functions.doc: Sends an HTTP request and gives the response. Any response is a result, whatever its status: a `404` or `500` is `response.status`, not an error, so check it. `nil, err` is for a request that couldn't be made or finished: a name that doesn't resolve, an address that isn't allowed, a refused connection, a timeout, a response over the size limit, too many requests this minute, a redirect to a host the package didn't declare, or more than 5 redirects. A mistake in the call itself (a URL that isn't `http` or `https`, a host the package didn't declare, a body over the limit, a header that can't be sent) is an error at the script's line. It works off the main thread, so its response arrives later: give `callback`, which is called with `response, err` once it's done, or call it inside a task (`nf.task`) without one, and it waits and returns `response, err`. Without a callback outside a task, it's an error. When it fails, `response` is `nil` and `err` says why.

params.name: options
params.doc: The request: its `url`, and optionally its `method`, `headers` and `body`.

params.name: callback
params.doc: Called on the main thread once it's done, as this script's code, with the response: its status, headers and body (or `nil` and why not). Not called if the script has stopped by then.

functions.example:
nf.task(function()
  local response, err = nf.http.request({
    method = "POST",
    url = "https://discord.com/api/webhooks/123/token",
    headers = { ["content-type"] = "application/json" },
    body = nf.json.encode({ content = "someone joined" }),
  })
  if not response then
    log("webhook failed: " .. err)
  elseif response.status >= 400 then
    log("webhook said " .. response.status)
  end
end)

returns.doc: Only without a callback, in a task: the response: its status, headers and body, or `nil`.
Why it failed, when it did; `nil` when it worked.

classes.name: nf.time
classes.doc: Dates and durations as text, in the same unit as `nf.server.unix_time()`: milliseconds. For timers, use ticks (`nf.after`, `nf.wait`); this is for showing and reading clock times and lengths of time.

functions.name: format
functions.doc: A moment as clock time, in English, written the way a pattern says.

params.name: time
params.doc: Milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC, like `nf.server.unix_time()` returns.

params.name: pattern
params.doc: Letters stand for parts of the date: `yyyy` the year, `MM` the month as a number (`MMM` `Oct`, `MMMM` `October`), `dd` the day, `EEE` the weekday (`Sat`; `EEEE` `Saturday`), `HH` the hour from 00 to 23 (`hh` 01 to 12, with `a` for AM or PM), `mm` minutes, `ss` seconds, `XXX` the zone's offset (`+01:00`, or `Z`). Text in single quotes is kept as it is (`'at'`); punctuation and spaces needn't be. A letter that isn't a pattern letter is an error.

functions.example:
local now = nf.server.unix_time()
player:send_message("It's " .. nf.time.format(now, "EEEE, d MMMM 'at' HH:mm", { zone = "UTC" }) .. " UTC")

functions.name: parse
functions.doc: Reads a clock time written the way a pattern says, as milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC. A pattern with no time of day reads as midnight; one with an offset (`XXX`) in it uses the offset it reads rather than `zone`. `nil` when the text doesn't match the pattern (it may come from a player); a pattern without a year, month and day, or with a letter that isn't a pattern letter, is an error.

params.name: pattern
params.doc: As for `nf.time.format`.

functions.example:
local start = nf.time.parse("2026-10-31 20:00", "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm", { zone = "Europe/London" })
if start and nf.server.unix_time() >= start then
  nf.server.broadcast("<gold>The event has begun!")
end

functions.name: duration
functions.doc: A length of time as short text, largest unit first and units that are 0 left out: `"1h 2m 5s"`, `"3d 4h"`, `"45s"`. Less than a second is `"0s"`; a negative length starts with `-`.

params.name: milliseconds
params.doc: How long.

functions.example:
local left = saved.ends_at - nf.server.unix_time()
player:send_message("Ends in " .. nf.time.duration(left))

functions.name: parse_duration
functions.doc: Reads a length of time written as numbers with units, as milliseconds: `"1h30m"`, `"1h 30m"`, `"90s"`, `"2d"`, `"1.5h"`, `"250ms"`. The units are `d`, `h`, `m`, `s` and `ms`, in any order, each at most once; spaces between them are fine. `nil` for text that isn't a duration (it may come from a player).
functions.example:
local cooldown = nf.time.parse_duration(event.arguments.cooldown)
if not cooldown then
  event.sender:send_message("<red>Try something like 10m or 1h30m")
end

classes.name: nf.random
classes.doc: Randomness `math.random` doesn't give: generators of your own that repeat for a seed, smooth noise, and random ids.

functions.name: new
functions.doc: A random generator of its own, apart from `math.random` and every other generator. Two made with the same seed give the same numbers in the same order, on every server, so a seed can stand for a whole dungeon layout or loot roll. One the script lets go of is collected like any table.

params.name: seed
params.doc: Leave it out for a generator seeded at random.

functions.example:
local rng = nf.random.new(42)
local roll = rng:integer(1, 6)
local prize = rng:weighted({ diamond = 1, iron_ingot = 5, bread = 20 })

functions.name: noise2
functions.doc: Smooth 2D noise (simplex): a number from -1 to 1 that changes gradually as `x` and `z` do, the same every time for the same arguments. For terrain heights, patches of blocks, wobble over time.
functions.example:
for x = 0, 31 do
  for z = 0, 31 do
    local height = 64 + math.floor(nf.random.noise2(x, z, { seed = 7, scale = 0.05 }) * 6)
    world:block(vec3(x, height, z)):set_state("minecraft:grass_block")
  end
end

functions.name: noise3
functions.doc: Smooth 3D noise (simplex), like `noise2` with a third coordinate: caves, clouds, or 2D noise that drifts over time (`y` as the tick).

functions.name: uuid
functions.doc: A new random UUID, like `"3f2b8c1e-7a4d-4e0b-9c55-0e8a6f1d2b7c"`: an id no one else will make.

classes.name: nf.math
classes.doc: Small arithmetic `math` doesn't have, for animating by hand: blending, clamping, rescaling and easing.

functions.name: lerp
functions.doc: The number `fraction` of the way from `from` to `to`: 0 is `from`, 1 is `to`, and outside that it carries on past either end. (`Vec3` has its own `lerp`.)

functions.name: clamp
functions.doc: `value`, kept from `min` to `max`. `min` greater than `max` is an error.

functions.name: remap
functions.doc: Moves `value` from one range to another: `from_min` becomes `to_min`, `from_max` becomes `to_max`, and everything else in proportion (beyond the ends too; clamp it if it mustn't). A range from a number to itself is an error.
functions.example: local pitch = nf.math.remap(health, 0, 20, 0.5, 2)

functions.name: ease
functions.doc: Reshapes a fraction from 0 to 1 by one of the curves animation keyframes use: `"linear"` as it is, `"step"` 0 until 1, `"ease_in"` starting slow, `"ease_out"` ending slow, `"ease_in_out"` both. Every curve takes 0 to 0 and 1 to 1; a fraction outside 0 to 1 is clamped first.

params.name: easing
params.doc: Which curve.

params.name: fraction
params.doc: How far along, 0 to 1.

functions.example:
nf.task(function()
  for tick = 0, 20 do
    local t = nf.math.ease("ease_in_out", tick / 20)
    node:set_translation(vec3(0, nf.math.lerp(0, 3, t), 0))
    nf.wait(1)
  end
end)

classes.name: nf.test
classes.doc: What a test file runs on. A project's tests are the `*_test.lua` files anywhere in it (`tests/shop_test.lua`), run by `netherforge test` (or the editor's Run tests) on a fake server: no Minecraft, no network, a world that holds only what the test puts in it. A test file runs like a module (it can `require` the project's modules, and files beside it) and registers its tests with `nf.test.case`; each test runs alone, on a fresh server with the project loaded and its scripts started, so one can never leave something behind for the next. The file's own code runs once for every test, before it, so it's where to `require` and build what the tests share. Nothing here exists on a real server: `nf.test` is `nil` there.

functions.name: case
functions.doc: Registers a test. It passes when `callback` returns, and fails at the line where an `assert` or `error` in it (or in something it calls) went wrong. A script of the project that errors while the test runs fails it too, naming that script and line. Two tests in one file can't have the same name.

params.name: name
params.doc: What the test checks, as a sentence: `"greets a new player"`.

params.name: callback
params.doc: The test. It runs synchronously: `nf.test.advance` is how time passes in it.

functions.example:
nf.test.case("a player joining is greeted", function()
  local alex = nf.test.player("Alex")
  nf.test.advance(1)
  assert(alex:name() == "Alex")
end)

functions.name: advance
functions.doc: Runs the server forward `ticks` ticks (20 are a second), whole ticks at a time: timers fall due, `tick` handlers run, centities tick and mobs think, exactly as on a server, and everything scripts started on other threads finishes first. When it returns, the last tick is done. Script errors during it are collected and fail the test when it ends.

params.name: ticks
params.doc: At least 1.

functions.example:
local count = 0
nf.every(20, function() count = count + 1 end)
nf.test.advance(60)
assert(count == 3)

functions.name: player
functions.doc: Joins a fake player and returns them: the server raises the join events (`player_join`) as it does for a real one, and the player can then be sent messages, given items, moved and clicked at like any other `Player`. Names are unique: a name already joined gives that player.

params.name: name
params.doc: Their name, 3 to 16 letters, digits and `_`: `"Alex"`.

functions.example:
local alex = nf.test.player("Alex")
alex:send_message("<green>hi")
assert(alex:name() == "Alex")

functions.name: raise
functions.doc: Raises a server-wide event as the server would, to the scripts: whoever listens to `event` with `nf.on` hears it, and, for an event the server raises about a player, an entity or a world, the handlers on that handle (`player:on("chat")`) hear it first, in the order the server uses. Each can `stop()` or `cancel()` it or set its writable fields. The few events the runtime stages itself (a death, damage, a click on a centity) reach `nf.on` handlers only. `payload` is what the event carries, the same table its handlers read (`event.player`, `event.message`): a field the event does not have is an error naming the fields. What the server would then do with a cancelled event is not simulated: read the result.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name, as `nf.on` takes it.

params.name: payload
params.doc: The payload: its fields by name. Leave it out for an event that has none.

returns.doc: Whether a handler cancelled it, and the event as the handlers left it.

functions.example:
local alex = nf.test.player("Alex")
local result = nf.test.raise("player_chat", { player = alex, message = "hello", format = "<message>" })
assert(not result.cancelled)
assert(result.event.message == "hello")

classes.name: Centity
classes.doc: One spawned centity: `this` in the centity's script, and what `nf.centities.spawn`, `nf.centities.get` and `nf.centities.all` return. A handle stays valid as long as the instance exists; after it's removed its methods return `nil` or `false` rather than erroring.

events.name: spawn
events.doc: Once, when the instance is first put into the world, after its script's body has run: not when it comes back after a restart or a reload. A script's body runs every time it starts; this is for what happens only once.

events.name: remove
events.doc: The instance is being removed for good (`centity:remove()`, `/nf kill`). Its script then unloads (`nf.on("unload")`), and every handler on it and its nodes goes.

events.name: tick
events.doc: Every tick while the instance's chunk is loaded, or every `n` ticks with `{ every = n }`. A centity nobody listens to this on isn't ticked at all.
events.example:
local angle = 0
this:on("tick", function()
  angle = (angle + 6) % 360
  this:node("blade"):set_rotation(vec3(0, angle, 0))
end)

events.name: click
events.doc: A player clicked one of its hitboxes: after the clicked node and the nodes above it, and before `nf.on("centity_click")`, unless one of them called `event:stop()`.
events.example:
this:on("click", function(event)
  this:play_animation("open")
  event.player:send_message("<gold>Opened")
end)

events.name: animation_start
events.doc: One of its animations started (`play_animation`), from the beginning.

events.name: animation_end
events.doc: An animation reached its end: a `once` clip has finished, a `hold` clip is holding its last pose. Looping clips never end.

events.name: chunk_load
events.doc: Its chunk came back into memory (someone came near), so it's ticking again.

events.name: chunk_unload
events.doc: Its chunk was unloaded (everyone went away): it stops ticking until `chunk_load`. Its handlers stay.

events.name: path_end
events.doc: It stopped walking where `move_to` sent it: it got there (to the end of its path, or within 2 blocks of what it went after), or gave up (no way further, its way blocked with no other way round, or what it went after has gone or left its world). Not after `stop_pathing`, a new `move_to`, `teleport` or a reload of its centity.
events.example:
this:on("path_end", function(event)
  if not event.reached then
    this:move_to(vec3(0, 64, 0))
  end
end)

functions.name: id
functions.doc: The instance's id, unique and stable across restarts. Keep this rather than the handle if you need to find it later.

functions.name: kind
functions.doc: Which centity it is: its folder name under `centities/`. `nil` once removed.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether the instance is still in the world.

functions.name: is_natural
functions.doc: Whether it appeared by itself, from its `spawning` rules in `centity.json`, and is still temporary: it isn't saved, it's removed when no player is near, and it counts against its cap. `false` for one a script spawned, one `keep` has kept, and once it's removed.

functions.name: keep
functions.doc: Makes a natural centity a normal one: it is saved from now on (it comes back after a restart), is never removed for being far from players, and no longer counts against its cap. Nothing happens to one that is already normal.

returns.doc: Whether it was natural: `false` for one that was already normal, and once it is removed.

functions.example:
this:on("click", function(event)
  if this:keep() then
    event.player:send_message("<green>It follows you now")
  end
end)

functions.name: node
functions.doc: One of its nodes by name, or `nil` if it has none by that name.

params.name: name
params.doc: The node's name in `centity.json`.

functions.example: this:node("lid"):set_rotation(vec3(-60, 0, 0))

functions.name: nodes
functions.doc: Every node, parents before their children.

functions.name: roots
functions.doc: Its root nodes (those with no parent), in the file's order. Every other node hangs from one of them.

functions.name: add_node
functions.doc: Adds a root node: one with no parent, whose translation is in the centity's own space, as if `centity.json` had one more. A node a script adds is **runtime state**, like a rest pose a script sets: it takes part in everything a declared node does (its transform follows its parent, a display and an interaction entity are spawned for it and sent to players, a hitbox takes clicks and `click` bubbles up through its parents, a `physics` body is simulated and collides, `raycast` hits it) except what a file names: an animation clip can't drive it, because clips are written against the file's nodes, though it follows its animated parent. It is **not saved**: after a restart, and when its centity is reloaded, it's gone, and the script's body, which runs again, is where to add it. Only nodes a script added can be removed; the nodes `centity.json` declares can't be. A name that's already a node's, or isn't a usable node name (letters, digits, `_` and `-`, at most 64 characters), is an error, and so is a definition the file's rules would refuse. Returns `nil` once the centity is removed.

params.name: name
params.doc: A new name, unique among the centity's nodes.

params.name: definition
params.doc: A table in the shape of one node of `centity.json`, minus its `parent` (it hangs from the node you call this on), in Lua spelling: `transform` (`{ translation?, rotation?, scale? }`, each a `Vec3`: where it starts, as a rest pose a script can change afterwards), `display` (`{ type = "block", block = "minecraft:stone" }`, `{ type = "item", item = "minecraft:diamond", item_transform? }` or `{ type = "text", text = "<red>Hi", billboard?, alignment?, background?, line_width?, see_through?, shadow? }`), `hitbox` (`{ boxes?, shape?, raycast?, fitted_to? }`, a box being `{ min = Vec3, max = Vec3 }`) and `physics` (`{ gravity?, mass?, bounciness?, friction?, drag?, angular_drag?, max_speed?, max_spin?, collider?, shape?, rotates?, sleeps?, blocks?, entities? }`). Every field is optional: a node with none is a pivot to hang others from. Held to the same rules as `centity.json`, by the same validator: a key it does not take, a value of the wrong type, or a block, item or hitbox the file would be refused for is an error.

functions.name: location
functions.doc: Where it stands, in which world, and which way it faces, or `nil` once it's removed. The location's `yaw` is the centity's (`centity:yaw()`); its `pitch` is `nil`, because a centity only turns about the vertical.

functions.name: position
functions.doc: Where it stands in its world: the anchor every node is placed relative to. `nil` once it's removed.

functions.name: world
functions.doc: The world it's in, or `nil` once it's removed.

functions.name: yaw
functions.doc: Which way it faces, in degrees, or `nil` once it's removed. Minecraft's convention: 0 faces south (+z), 90 west (−x), 180 north, −90 east, always given back between −180 and 180. Its +Z axis points that way, and every node is turned with it about its position.

functions.name: set_yaw
functions.doc: Turns the whole centity to face a yaw, about the vertical through its position: every node, its hitboxes and its physics bodies turn with it (a moving body keeps going, turned by as much). The turn is saved. Pitch and roll aren't a centity's: rotate a root node for those. Does nothing once it's removed.

params.name: degrees
params.doc: Minecraft's convention (0 south, 90 west); any number, wrapped into −180 to 180.

functions.example: this:set_yaw(this:yaw() + 90)

functions.name: look_at
functions.doc: Turns it to face a world position, as `set_yaw` does: only about the vertical, so how far above or below the point is makes no difference. A point straight above or below its position leaves it as it is.

params.name: point
params.doc: A position in the world.

returns.doc: `false` once it's removed.

functions.example:
local target = player:position()
if target then
  this:look_at(target)
end

functions.name: to_local
functions.doc: A world position in the centity's own space: what a root node's translation would be to stand there. The centity's own space has its origin at the centity's position (`centity:position()`) and is turned by its yaw (`centity:yaw()`): its +Z is the way the centity faces, its Y is the world's. It's the space a root node's translation is in. `nil` once it's removed.

params.name: point
params.doc: A position in the world.

functions.name: to_world
functions.doc: A position in the centity's own space as a world position. The centity's own space has its origin at the centity's position (`centity:position()`) and is turned by its yaw (`centity:yaw()`): its +Z is the way the centity faces, its Y is the world's. It's the space a root node's translation is in. `nil` once it's removed.

params.name: point
params.doc: A position in the centity's space.

functions.name: teleport
functions.doc: Moves the whole centity: to a `Location` (turning to face its `yaw`, when it has one), or to a position in its current world. It keeps its own facing when the destination has none; a location's `pitch` is ignored.

params.name: location_or_position
params.doc: Where its position (the anchor) goes.

returns.doc: Whether it moved: `false` once it's removed, or for a world that doesn't exist.

functions.example: this:teleport(this:position() + vec3(0, 5, 0))

functions.name: move_to
functions.doc: Makes the whole centity walk somewhere, finding its way round the blocks in the way: to a place in its own world, or after an entity or another centity, looking for a new path to wherever that is every 10 ticks. When it stops, its `path_end` handlers hear whether it got there. A walk goes by the centity's **feet**: the middle of the bottom of its hitboxes as they're placed when it sets off (its position, for a centity without any). The way is found over the blocks' collision shapes, sized to its hitboxes (other centities aren't in the way), and walked a little each tick, before physics and scripts: it steps up and drops down as the options allow, falls when nothing holds it up, and finds another way when a block appears across its path. With `fly = true` it flies instead, through the air in any direction. A new `move_to`, `stop_pathing` and `teleport` end the walk it was on, and so does a reload of its centity (its script's body can set off again). Walks aren't saved, and a centity whose chunk unloads waits where it is until it loads again. Its physics bodies are carried along with it.

params.name: target
params.doc: Where its feet go: a position in its world, a `Location` (in its world: another world is `false`), or an entity or centity to go after.

returns.doc: Whether it found a way and set off, which may only take it as close as it can get: `false` when it can't get any closer than it is (walking, it needs ground under it, within 64 blocks), for a target further away than `range`, in another world or gone, or once it's removed.

functions.example:
this:on("path_end", function(event)
  log(event.reached and "made it" or "gave up")
end)
this:move_to(vec3(10, 64, 10), { speed = 2 })

functions.name: stop_pathing
functions.doc: Stops it where it is, ending its walk without a `path_end`. One that was falling stays in the air: a centity only falls while it walks.

returns.doc: Whether it was walking: `false` when it wasn't, or once it's removed.

functions.name: has_path
functions.doc: Whether it's walking somewhere now (`move_to`). `false` once it's removed.

functions.name: path_target
functions.doc: Where the path it's walking ends, as where its feet will be: where it was sent, or as close as it can get when there's no way all the way there. A walk goes by the centity's **feet**: the middle of the bottom of its hitboxes as they're placed when it sets off (its position, for a centity without any). `nil` when it isn't walking, or once it's removed.

functions.name: data
functions.doc: This instance's own saved table, kept with the instance across restarts and removed with it. Every script that holds the instance (its own, a module's) gets the same table. It may hold strings, numbers, booleans, tables of them (keyed by strings, or a list numbered from 1), and the API's own values: `Vec3`s, `Location`s, `Item` tables, and `Player`, `Entity`, `Centity` and `World` handles, which come back as the same types (a handle to something gone answers `nil` or `false`, as handles do). Anything else (a function, a `Menu` window, a `Subscription`) is skipped when it's saved, with a line in the log naming where it was (`data.inventory[3]: a function can't be saved`). The table is live: change it and the change is saved, at the next autosave (every five minutes), when the project reloads and when the server stops. It stays in memory across hot reloads rather than being read again, so a script that reloads finds it as it left it. A table that would take more than 1 MiB isn't saved (the last save stands), and the log says so. `nil` once it's removed.
functions.example:
local data = assert(this:data())
data.opened = (data.opened or 0) + 1
data.last_player = event.player

functions.name: remove
functions.doc: Takes it out of the world for good. Its `remove` handlers hear it, then its script unloads.

functions.name: play_animation
functions.doc: Starts one of its animations, from the beginning (or `from_tick`), restarting it if it's already playing. Its `animation_start` handlers hear it before this returns. An animation it doesn't have is an error.

params.name: name
params.doc: The animation's name in `centity.json`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to play it this time. A key it doesn't take is an error.

returns.doc: `false` once it's removed.

functions.name: stop_animation
functions.doc: Stops one animation, or all of them. The nodes it was moving go back to rest.

params.name: name
params.doc: Leave out to stop everything.

functions.name: pause_animation
functions.doc: Holds a playing animation where it is: its nodes keep the pose it had reached, until `resume_animation`. An animation it doesn't have is an error.

returns.doc: `false` when it isn't playing.

functions.name: resume_animation
functions.doc: Carries on with a paused animation from where it stopped. An animation it doesn't have is an error.

returns.doc: `false` when it isn't playing.

functions.name: is_animation_playing
functions.doc: Whether an animation is playing (a paused one still is, and so is a `hold` animation that reached its end).

functions.name: playing_animations
functions.doc: The animations playing now, oldest first.

functions.name: animations
functions.doc: Every animation the centity has.

functions.name: animation_tick
functions.doc: How far into its clip a playing animation is, in ticks (20 a second): within the clip's length, so a looping one starts again from 0 each time round. Not always whole, at a speed other than 1. `nil` when it isn't playing; an animation the centity doesn't have is an error.

functions.name: seek_animation
functions.doc: Jumps a playing animation to a point in its clip, and poses the nodes there at once. Past the end, a looping clip wraps round, and any other ends on its next tick. An animation the centity doesn't have is an error.

params.name: tick
params.doc: Ticks from the start of the clip, at least 0.

returns.doc: `false` when it isn't playing.

functions.name: animation_speed
functions.doc: How fast a playing animation runs: 1 is as authored, 2 twice as fast. `nil` when it isn't playing; an animation the centity doesn't have is an error.

functions.name: set_animation_speed
functions.doc: Changes how fast a playing animation runs, from where it is now. An animation the centity doesn't have is an error.

params.name: multiplier
params.doc: 1 is as authored, 0.5 half speed, 0 holds it still (like pausing). Not negative.

returns.doc: `false` when it isn't playing.

functions.name: is_glowing
functions.doc: Whether every node that draws something glows (`set_glowing`). `false` once it's removed, or when it draws nothing.

functions.name: set_glowing
functions.doc: Outlines every node that draws something, seen through walls, the way the Glowing effect outlines a mob. The colour is `set_glow_color`'s. The same as `set_glowing` on each node.

returns.doc: `false` once it's removed.

functions.example:
this:set_glow_color("#ffaa00")
this:set_glowing(true)

functions.name: glow_color
functions.doc: The colour its block and item displays glow in, as `#RRGGBB`: `nil` when they don't share one, when none was set (they glow white), or once it's removed.

functions.name: set_glow_color
functions.doc: Sets the colour every block and item display node glows in (the same as `set_glow_color` on each). Minecraft draws no glow colour on text displays, so they're left as they are. It doesn't turn the glow on: `set_glowing` does.

params.name: color
params.doc: `#RRGGBB`. Leave it out for the default, white. Anything else is an error.

returns.doc: `false` once it's removed, or when it has no block or item display.

functions.name: hide_from
functions.doc: Hides the whole centity from one player: they don't see its nodes and can't click its hitboxes. Everyone else still does. It stays hidden from them when they leave and come back, and when its chunk unloads and loads again, until `show_to`, a server restart or the centity's removal. Hiding it from someone offline counts for when they join.

returns.doc: `false` once it's removed.

functions.name: show_to
functions.doc: Shows it to a player it was hidden from.

returns.doc: `false` once it's removed.

functions.name: is_hidden_from
functions.doc: Whether `hide_from` hid it from a player.

functions.name: view_range
functions.doc: How far away its displays are drawn, in blocks: 64 unless `set_view_range` changed it. `nil` once it's removed.

functions.name: set_view_range
functions.doc: How far away its displays are drawn, in blocks. Each player's own entity distance setting scales it further, so it's the distance at 100%. Not saved, like everything a script sets on a node.

params.name: blocks
params.doc: At least 0.

returns.doc: `false` once it's removed.

functions.example:
-- A landmark seen from far off.
this:set_view_range(256)

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: A built-in event's name, or a custom event's: any name with a `:` in it, like `"shop:purchased"`.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `centity:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: A built-in event's name, or a custom event's: any name with a `:` in it, like `"shop:purchased"`.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

functions.name: emit
functions.doc: Raises a custom event on this centity: every `centity:on(event)` handler hears it now, in the order they were registered, before this returns. The payload is handed to them as it is, not copied, so a field a handler assigns is there for the caller to read afterwards. A name without a `:` is an error: built-in events are the server's to raise.

params.name: event
params.doc: A custom event's name, with a `:`: `"shop:purchased"`.

params.name: payload
params.doc: The event's fields. Leave it out for none.

returns.doc: Whether a handler cancelled it (`event:cancel()`), so a custom event can be vetoed.

functions.example: door:emit("door:open", { by = event.player })

classes.name: Node
classes.doc: One node of one centity instance. Its transform (`translation`, `rotation`, `scale`) is in its parent's space, in the same units as `centity.json`: blocks, degrees (X then Y then Z) and scale factors. A root node's parent space is the centity's own: origin at the centity's position, turned by its yaw. `world_position`, `to_world`, `to_local` and `world_direction` convert to and from the world; physics (velocities, impulses and the point an impulse lands at) is always in world space. What a script sets is the node's rest pose; an animation driving the same channel overrides it while it plays. Nothing a script sets is saved: the script's body, which runs every time it starts, is where to set it up. A node with `physics` is moved by it: each tick physics writes its translation and rotation, after animations and before scripts, so a script's write has the last word (setting the rotation re-seeds the body's orientation).

events.name: click
events.doc: A player clicked this node's hitbox, or the hitbox of a node under it (`event.target` says which). Then its parent hears it, and so on up to the root, then the centity, then `nf.on("centity_click")`, unless a handler calls `event:stop()`.
events.example:
local crate = assert(this:node("crate"))
crate:on("click", function(event)
  crate:apply_impulse_at(vec3(0, 0, 4), event.hit_position)
  event:stop()
end)

events.name: collide
events.doc: This physics body hit something: a block, another centity, or another body of its own centity. Once per thing touched, when they start touching.
events.example:
ball:on("collide", function(event)
  if event.speed > 2 then
    log("clack")
  end
end)

events.name: wake
events.doc: This physics body started moving again after sleeping: something hit it, what held it up went, or a script pushed it.

events.name: sleep
events.doc: This physics body settled: it's still, and isn't simulated until something wakes it.

functions.name: name
functions.doc: The node's name.

functions.name: centity
functions.doc: The instance it belongs to.

functions.name: parent
functions.doc: Its parent node, or `nil` for a root.

functions.name: children
functions.doc: Its child nodes, by name.

functions.name: add_child
functions.doc: Adds a node that hangs from this one, so it moves, turns and scales with it. A node a script adds is **runtime state**, like a rest pose a script sets: it takes part in everything a declared node does (its transform follows its parent, a display and an interaction entity are spawned for it and sent to players, a hitbox takes clicks and `click` bubbles up through its parents, a `physics` body is simulated and collides, `raycast` hits it) except what a file names: an animation clip can't drive it, because clips are written against the file's nodes, though it follows its animated parent. It is **not saved**: after a restart, and when its centity is reloaded, it's gone, and the script's body, which runs again, is where to add it. Only nodes a script added can be removed; the nodes `centity.json` declares can't be. The name is unique among the centity's nodes, not only this node's children. A name that's taken, or isn't a usable node name, is an error, and so is a definition the file's rules would refuse. Returns `nil` once its centity or this node is gone.

params.name: name
params.doc: A new name, unique among the centity's nodes.

params.name: definition
params.doc: A table in the shape of one node of `centity.json`, minus its `parent` (it hangs from the node you call this on), in Lua spelling: `transform` (`{ translation?, rotation?, scale? }`, each a `Vec3`: where it starts, as a rest pose a script can change afterwards), `display` (`{ type = "block", block = "minecraft:stone" }`, `{ type = "item", item = "minecraft:diamond", item_transform? }` or `{ type = "text", text = "<red>Hi", billboard?, alignment?, background?, line_width?, see_through?, shadow? }`), `hitbox` (`{ boxes?, shape?, raycast?, fitted_to? }`, a box being `{ min = Vec3, max = Vec3 }`) and `physics` (`{ gravity?, mass?, bounciness?, friction?, drag?, angular_drag?, max_speed?, max_spin?, collider?, shape?, rotates?, sleeps?, blocks?, entities? }`). Every field is optional: a node with none is a pivot to hang others from. Held to the same rules as `centity.json`, by the same validator: a key it does not take, a value of the wrong type, or a block, item or hitbox the file would be refused for is an error.

functions.name: remove
functions.doc: Removes this node and every node below it, with their displays and hitboxes (players see them go at the end of the tick), their physics bodies and every handler on them; the handles answer `nil` and `false` after that. Only a node a script added can be removed: removing one `centity.json` declares is an error, since animations, physics and other scripts are written against it. Returns whether it was removed: `false` if it is already gone, or its centity is.

functions.name: translation
functions.doc: Its offset from its parent (for a root node, from the centity's position), as shown now: animation and physics included. `nil` once its centity is removed.

functions.name: rotation
functions.doc: Its rotation relative to its parent, in degrees, applied X then Y then Z. `nil` once its centity is removed.

functions.name: scale
functions.doc: Its scale on each of its own axes. `nil` once its centity is removed.

functions.name: set_translation
functions.doc: Moves it relative to its parent (a root node, relative to the centity's position).

params.name: translation
params.doc: In its parent's space, in blocks.

functions.name: set_rotation
functions.doc: Turns it relative to its parent. Displays ease to the new pose over a tick, so setting it every tick looks smooth.

params.name: rotation
params.doc: Degrees, applied X then Y then Z.

functions.example:
local angle = 0
this:on("tick", function()
  angle = (angle + 6) % 360
  this:node("blade"):set_rotation(vec3(0, angle, 0))
end)

functions.name: set_scale
functions.doc: Scales it along its own axes.

params.name: scale
params.doc: A factor per axis: `vec3.one` is its natural size.

functions.name: world_position
functions.doc: Where its origin is in the world, as shown now: animation and physics included. `nil` once its centity is removed.

functions.name: world_rotation
functions.doc: Its rotation relative to the world, in degrees applied X then Y then Z, as shown now: its own and every ancestor's together. Scale doesn't count. `nil` once its centity is removed.

functions.name: to_local
functions.doc: A world position in this node's own space: the space its children's translations are in, which moves, turns and scales with it, as shown now. `nil` once its centity is removed, or while it's scaled to nothing on some axis.

params.name: point
params.doc: A position in the world.

functions.name: to_world
functions.doc: A position in this node's own space (where a child at that translation would be) as a world position, as shown now. `nil` once its centity is removed.

params.name: point
params.doc: A position in the node's space.

functions.example:
-- The top centre of a block display, wherever it has rolled to.
local top = crate:to_world(vec3(0.5, 1, 0.5))

functions.name: world_direction
functions.doc: A direction in this node's own space as a world direction: turned with the node, but not moved or scaled. `node:world_direction(vec3.south)` is where its +Z points. `nil` once its centity is removed.

params.name: direction
params.doc: A direction in the node's space.

functions.name: look_at
functions.doc: Turns it so its +Z axis points at a world position, keeping its X axis level (no roll), by setting its rotation as `set_rotation` does. Exact unless an ancestor is scaled unevenly. Pointing at its own origin leaves it as it is.

params.name: point
params.doc: A position in the world.

returns.doc: `false` once its centity is removed, or while its parent is scaled to nothing.

functions.example: this:node("head"):look_at(player:position() + vec3(0, 1.6, 0))

functions.name: rotate
functions.doc: Turns it further, by an angle about an axis in its parent's space, by the right-hand rule (as `Vec3:rotated` does), by setting its rotation as `set_rotation` does.

params.name: axis
params.doc: In its parent's space; any length but zero.

returns.doc: `false` once its centity is removed.

functions.name: is_visible
functions.doc: Whether it's set visible (it can still be hidden by a hidden parent).

functions.name: set_visible
functions.doc: Shows or hides it and everything under it. A hidden node can't be clicked.

functions.name: is_clickable
functions.doc: Whether its hitbox takes clicks (`set_clickable`). `true` for a node without one, which has nothing to click anyway.

functions.name: set_clickable
functions.doc: Turns its hitbox off or back on without hiding the node: an unclickable node is still drawn, but clicks pass through it as if it had no hitbox. Its children keep their own. Physics still treats the hitbox as solid. Not saved.
functions.example:
-- A button that only works once.
button:once("click", function()
  button:set_clickable(false)
end)

functions.name: display_kind
functions.doc: What it draws: `"block"`, `"item"` or `"text"`, or `nil` for a node that draws nothing (a pivot, a hitbox alone) or once its centity is removed.

functions.name: display_block
functions.doc: The block state a block display shows, like `"minecraft:oak_slab[type=top]"`, or `nil` when the node isn't a block display.

functions.name: set_display_block
functions.doc: Changes the block a block display shows. A hitbox with `shape: "collision"` follows the new block's shape.

params.name: block
params.doc: A block state, like `"minecraft:oak_slab[type=top]"`.

returns.doc: `false` when the node isn't a block display or the server has no such block state.

functions.name: display_text
functions.doc: What a text display says, as MiniMessage, or `nil` when the node isn't a text display.

functions.name: set_display_text
functions.doc: Changes what a text display says.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage.

returns.doc: `false` when the node isn't a text display.

functions.name: display_item
functions.doc: The item an item display shows, or `nil` when the node isn't an item display.

functions.name: set_display_item
functions.doc: Changes the item an item display shows: any `Item`, so a name, `item_model` or `glint` shows as it would in a hand. Its `count` makes no difference. An item table with a misspelled field, or an item the server doesn't have, is an error.

returns.doc: `false` when the node isn't an item display.

functions.example: this:node("sword"):set_display_item({ kind = "minecraft:diamond_sword", glint = true })

functions.name: display_text_style
functions.doc: How a text display's text is drawn, every field filled in (`background` is `nil` for Minecraft's own grey), or `nil` when the node isn't a text display. Change a field and hand it to `set_display_text_style`.

functions.name: set_display_text_style
functions.doc: Changes how a text display's text is drawn. The whole style is replaced: a field left out goes back to its default, so to change one thing, read `display_text_style()`, change it and write it back. A bad value (an alignment that isn't one, a background that isn't `#AARRGGBB`) is an error.

returns.doc: `false` when the node isn't a text display.

functions.example:
local sign = assert(this:node("sign"))
local style = sign:display_text_style()
if style then
  style.background = "#80000000"
  style.shadow = true
  sign:set_display_text_style(style)
end

functions.name: is_glowing
functions.doc: Whether its display glows (`set_glowing`). `false` for a node that draws nothing.

functions.name: set_glowing
functions.doc: Outlines its display, seen through walls, the way the Glowing effect outlines a mob. Block and item displays glow in `set_glow_color`'s colour (white by default). Not saved.

returns.doc: `false` for a node that draws nothing.

functions.name: glow_color
functions.doc: The colour its block or item display glows in, as `#RRGGBB`, or `nil` for the default (white), for a text display, or for a node that draws nothing.

functions.name: set_glow_color
functions.doc: Sets the colour a block or item display glows in. Minecraft draws no glow colour on a text display, so there it does nothing and returns `false`. It doesn't turn the glow on: `set_glowing` does.

params.name: color
params.doc: `#RRGGBB`. Leave it out for the default, white. Anything else is an error.

returns.doc: `false` for a text display, or a node that draws nothing.

functions.example:
node:set_glow_color("#55ff55")
node:set_glowing(true)

functions.name: brightness
functions.doc: The light its display is drawn with, when `set_brightness` fixed it; `nil` when it's lit by where it stands (the default), or for a node that draws nothing.

functions.name: set_brightness
functions.doc: Draws its display as if lit by fixed light levels, whatever the light where it stands: `{ block_light = 15, sky_light = 15 }` is full brightness in a dark cave. Leave it out (or `nil`) to go back to the light around it. A level outside 0 to 15, or a missing one, is an error.

params.name: brightness
params.doc: Both levels, 0 to 15.

returns.doc: `false` for a node that draws nothing.

functions.example: this:node("lamp"):set_brightness({ block_light = 15, sky_light = 15 })

functions.name: billboard
functions.doc: Which way its display turns to face whoever looks at it: `"fixed"` (it doesn't), `"vertical"` (about the vertical, like a sign on a post), `"horizontal"` or `"center"` (all the way). `nil` for a node that draws nothing.

functions.name: set_billboard
functions.doc: Makes its display turn to face each viewer (or stop). A turning display ignores its rotation (its parents' included) about the axes it turns on. A text display starts as its `billboard` in `centity.json` says (`"center"` by default), a block or item display `"fixed"`. Anything else is an error.

returns.doc: `false` for a node that draws nothing.

functions.name: interpolation_ticks
functions.doc: How many ticks its display takes to ease to a new pose: 1 unless `set_interpolation_ticks` changed it. `nil` once its centity is removed.

functions.name: set_interpolation_ticks
functions.doc: How many ticks its display takes to ease to each new pose (its translation, rotation and scale, and its parents'). The client does the easing, so a pose set once with `set_interpolation_ticks(20)` glides there over a second without the script doing anything more. When the whole centity moves (`teleport`, physics carrying it along), its display glides there over as many ticks, up to 59. 0 jumps. Not saved.

params.name: ticks
params.doc: At least 0.

returns.doc: `false` once its centity is removed.

functions.example:
local door = assert(this:node("door"))
door:set_interpolation_ticks(10)
door:set_rotation(vec3(0, 90, 0)) -- swings open over half a second

functions.name: velocity
functions.doc: How fast a physics body is moving, in blocks per second along the world's axes: `vec3.zero` for a node without `physics`, `nil` once its centity is removed.

functions.name: set_velocity
functions.doc: Replaces a physics body's velocity, and wakes it.

params.name: velocity
params.doc: Blocks per second, along the world's axes.

returns.doc: `false` for a node without `physics`.

functions.name: add_velocity
functions.doc: Adds to a physics body's velocity whatever it weighs ("go this much faster", which is what a jump means), and wakes it.

params.name: velocity
params.doc: Blocks per second, along the world's axes.

returns.doc: `false` for a node without `physics`.

functions.name: angular_velocity
functions.doc: How fast a physics body is turning about each world axis, in degrees per second: `vec3.zero` for a node without `physics`, `nil` once its centity is removed.

functions.name: set_angular_velocity
functions.doc: Replaces a physics body's angular velocity, and wakes it.

params.name: angular_velocity
params.doc: Degrees per second about each world axis.

returns.doc: `false` for a node without `physics`.

functions.name: mass
functions.doc: A physics body's mass: what its `physics` says, or its collider's volume in blocks. 0 for a node without `physics`. `speed * node:mass()` is the impulse that sends it off at `speed`.

functions.name: apply_impulse
functions.doc: Pushes a physics body through its centre of mass: mass times a change in velocity, so the same push moves a light body further than a heavy one. Through the centre, so it doesn't turn it. Wakes it.

params.name: impulse
params.doc: Along the world's axes.

returns.doc: `false` for a node without `physics`.

functions.example: ball:apply_impulse(direction * 4 * ball:mass())

functions.name: apply_impulse_at
functions.doc: The same push, landing at a point instead of through the middle, so it turns the body as well: the further off centre, the more of it becomes angular velocity.

params.name: impulse
params.doc: Along the world's axes.

params.name: point
params.doc: Where it lands, as a world position: `node:to_world(...)` turns a point on the node into one.

returns.doc: `false` for a node without `physics`.

functions.example:
-- Shove the top edge: it topples rather than slides.
local top = crate:to_world(vec3(0.5, 1, 0.5))
if top then
  crate:apply_impulse_at(vec3(0, 0, 4), top)
end

functions.name: is_on_ground
functions.doc: Whether a physics body is resting on something: `not node:is_on_ground()` reliably means falling.

functions.name: is_asleep
functions.doc: Whether a physics body has settled and stopped being simulated. It wakes when something hits it, when what holds it up goes (checked about once a second), or when a script pushes it.

functions.name: wake
functions.doc: Puts a settled physics body back to work, for when a script changed something it can't feel (a block placed beside it).

functions.name: apply_force
functions.doc: Pushes a physics body through its centre of mass for the next tick: a force in mass times blocks per second squared, so calling it every tick is a steady push (and `vec3(0, 32, 0) * node:mass()` holds a body up against default gravity). The same as `apply_impulse(force / 20)`. Wakes it.

params.name: force
params.doc: Along the world's axes.

returns.doc: `false` for a node without `physics`.

functions.name: has_gravity
functions.doc: Whether gravity is on for a physics body: `true` unless `set_gravity(false)` turned it off. How strong it is is the body's `physics.gravity`, which may be 0. `false` for a node without `physics`.

functions.name: set_gravity
functions.doc: Turns gravity off for a physics body, so it floats where it's put and drifts at the speed it has, or back on. Wakes it. Not saved.

returns.doc: `false` for a node without `physics`.

functions.name: is_kinematic
functions.doc: Whether a physics body is kinematic (`set_kinematic`).

functions.name: set_kinematic
functions.doc: Makes a physics body kinematic: moved only by scripts, never by gravity or what it hits. It keeps moving at the velocity and angular velocity a script gives it (`set_velocity`), and its centity's other bodies collide with it as if it were a wall: a moving platform, a piston. Back to a normal body with `false`. Not saved.

returns.doc: `false` for a node without `physics`.

functions.name: is_physics_enabled
functions.doc: Whether a physics body is simulated (`set_physics_enabled`). `false` for a node without `physics`.

functions.name: set_physics_enabled
functions.doc: Freezes a physics body in place, or lets it go again. A frozen body doesn't move at all (scripts can still set its pose), and its centity's other bodies collide with it as with a wall. It keeps its velocity, so it carries on where it left off when it's let go. Not saved.

returns.doc: `false` for a node without `physics`.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `node:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: Entity
classes.doc: Something in a world that isn't a block: an arrow, a minecart, a dropped item, a mob, a player. A handle is its UUID, so keeping one is fine: once the entity has gone (killed, removed) or while its chunk is unloaded, its methods answer `nil` or `false` rather than erroring. Its handle is the class it is: a `Living` (health, effects, equipment), a `Mob` (a target, AI, walking, goals), a `Player` or a `DroppedItem`, each with every `Entity` method too, and taken wherever an `Entity` is. A handle to an entity that wasn't in the world when it was handed out becomes its class once it's back. The entities NetherForge draws centities with are never handed out as `Entity`. Positions are world space.

events.name: damage
events.doc: Something is hurting it: before `nf.on("entity_damage")`, with the same event, so `event:cancel()` here stops it and `event:stop()` keeps it from `nf`. Assign `event.amount` to change how much it takes.
events.example:
pet:on("damage", function(event)
  if event.cause == "fall" then
    event:cancel()
  end
end)

events.name: interact
events.doc: A player right-clicked it: before the player's own `interact_entity` and then `nf.on("player_interact_entity")`, with the same event. `event:cancel()` stops what the click would do (a villager trading, a cow being milked). A `Player`'s own `interact` is them clicking a block instead; a click on a player is heard by the clicker and `nf`.

events.name: hit
events.doc: This projectile hit an entity or a block. `event:cancel()` lets it pass through as if nothing were there (an arrow flies on; a snowball doesn't break). Heard by the entity before `nf.on("projectile_hit")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.
events.example:
local arrow = assert(nf.worlds.default():spawn_entity("arrow", vec3(0, 80, 0), { velocity = vec3(0, -1, 0) }))
arrow:on("hit", function(event)
  if event.block then
    event.block:set_state("minecraft:gold_block")
  end
end)

events.name: explode
events.doc: It exploded: a creeper, TNT, a fireball, an end crystal, a wither skull. `event:cancel()` stops the explosion breaking anything; assign `event.breaks_blocks = false` to keep every block standing but still hurt what is near, or `event.yield` to change how much of what breaks drops. Heard by the entity before `nf.on("entity_explode")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: combust
events.doc: It is catching fire: from lava or fire, sunlight (a zombie, a skeleton), a flaming arrow or a fire aspect sword. `event:cancel()` keeps it from burning; assign `event.ticks` to make it burn for that long instead. Heard by the entity before `nf.on("entity_combust")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: mount
events.doc: It is getting on something to ride it: a horse, a pig with a saddle, a boat, a minecart, another mob (a spider jockey). `event:cancel()` keeps it off. Heard by the entity before `nf.on("entity_mount")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: dismount
events.doc: It is getting off what it rides: sneaking, the vehicle breaking, a teleport, dying. `event:cancel()` keeps it on, except where it can't stay (it died, or what it rode has gone). Heard by the entity before `nf.on("entity_dismount")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

functions.name: id
functions.doc: Its UUID, as a string: the thing to store. A player's gives the same handle back from `nf.players.get(id)`.

functions.name: kind
functions.doc: What it is, like `"minecraft:zombie"` or `"minecraft:player"`, or `nil` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether it's in the world now: alive, and in a loaded chunk. For a player, whether they're online.

functions.name: is_player
functions.doc: Whether it's a player: then it's a `Player` handle.

functions.name: is_living
functions.doc: Whether it's a living entity (a mob, an animal, an armour stand, a player): then it's a `Living` handle, with health, effects and equipment. `false` while it isn't in the world, unless its handle was handed out as a `Living` already.

functions.name: is_mob
functions.doc: Whether it's a mob, something with AI (a zombie, a cow, a bat): then it's a `Mob` handle, with a target, walking and goals. `false` while it isn't in the world, unless its handle was handed out as a `Mob` already.
functions.example:
local entity = player:target_entity()
if entity and entity:is_mob() then
  local mob = entity --[[@as Mob]]
  mob:set_target(player)
end

functions.name: location
functions.doc: Where it is, in which world, and which way it faces, or `nil` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: position
functions.doc: Where it is (its feet), or `nil` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: world
functions.doc: The world it's in, or `nil` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: eye_position
functions.doc: Where its eyes are, which is where it looks from, or `nil` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: yaw
functions.doc: Which way it faces horizontally, in degrees, or `nil` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded). Minecraft's convention: 0 faces south (+z), 90 west (−x), 180 north, −90 east.

functions.name: pitch
functions.doc: How far up or down it looks, in degrees, or `nil` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded): −90 is straight up, 90 straight down.

functions.name: direction
functions.doc: The unit direction it looks in, or `nil` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: set_yaw
functions.doc: Turns it to face a horizontal direction, keeping its pitch.

params.name: degrees
params.doc: 0 south, 90 west.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: set_pitch
functions.doc: Tilts it to look up or down, keeping its yaw.

params.name: degrees
params.doc: −90 up, 90 down.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: look_at
functions.doc: Turns it to look at a point: its yaw and pitch both.

params.name: point
params.doc: A world position.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: teleport
functions.doc: Moves it: to a `Location` (facing its way, when it has a facing), or to a position in its current world. It keeps its own facing when the destination has none, and its passengers come along.

params.name: location_or_position
params.doc: Where it goes.

returns.doc: Whether it moved: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded), and for a world that doesn't exist.

functions.name: velocity
functions.doc: How fast it moves, in blocks per tick, or `nil` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: set_velocity
functions.doc: Sets how fast it moves, in blocks per tick: a push. Friction and gravity carry on from there.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: add_velocity
functions.doc: Adds to how fast it moves, in blocks per tick: a knock.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: is_on_ground
functions.doc: Whether it stands on something. `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: remove
functions.doc: Takes it out of the world for good, without dying: no drops, no death event. Its handlers and its saved table go with it. A player can't be removed: they leave through `kick`.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded), and for a player.

functions.name: name
functions.doc: What players see it called, as MiniMessage: its custom name, or its kind's name (`"Zombie"`). `nil` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: custom_name
functions.doc: Its custom name, as MiniMessage, or `nil` when it has none, and once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: set_custom_name
functions.doc: Names it, or takes its custom name away. Whether players see the name above it without looking at it is `set_custom_name_visible`.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage. Leave it out (or `nil`) to remove the name.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: is_custom_name_visible
functions.doc: Whether its custom name shows above it all the time, not only when a player looks at it. `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: set_custom_name_visible
functions.doc: Shows its custom name above it all the time, or only when a player looks at it.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: tags
functions.doc: Its scoreboard tags (what `/tag` adds), sorted. Empty once it has gone.

functions.name: has_tag
functions.doc: Whether it has a scoreboard tag. `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: add_tag
functions.doc: Adds a scoreboard tag, as `/tag <entity> add` does. Tags are saved with the entity and selectors can find them (`@e[tag=boss]`).

params.name: tag
params.doc: Letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `.` and `+`.

returns.doc: Whether it was added: `false` when it already had it, once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: remove_tag
functions.doc: Takes a scoreboard tag away.

returns.doc: Whether it had it: `false` when it didn't, once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: data
functions.doc: Its own table for scripts to keep things in, saved on the entity itself (its persistent data container), so it goes where the entity goes and is gone when the entity is: the same table every time, shared by every script. Change it in place; it's saved when the server autosaves, when the entity's chunk unloads and when the server stops. It may hold strings, numbers, booleans, tables of them (keyed by strings, or a list numbered from 1), and the API's own values: `Vec3`s, `Location`s, `Item` tables, and `Player`, `Entity`, `Centity` and `World` handles, which come back as the same types (a handle to something gone answers `nil` or `false`, as handles do). Anything else (a function, a `Menu` window, a `Subscription`) is skipped when it's saved, with a line in the log naming where it was (`data.inventory[3]: a function can't be saved`). `nil` while the entity isn't in the world.
functions.example:
local data = zombie:data()
if data then
  data.kills = (data.kills or 0) + 1
end

functions.name: is_glowing
functions.doc: Whether it glows: an outline seen through walls. `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: set_glowing
functions.doc: Makes it glow, or stops it. The outline is white, or its team's colour (`team:set_color`).

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: is_visible
functions.doc: Whether players can see it at all (`set_visible`), whoever they are. `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: set_visible
functions.doc: Hides it from every player, or shows it again. Saved with the entity. To hide it from some players only, use `hide_from`.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: hide_from
functions.doc: Hides it from one player: they stop seeing it (and can't click it), while everyone else still does. It stays hidden from them when they leave and come back, and when the entity's chunk unloads and loads again, until `show_to`.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded), or when the player is offline.

functions.name: show_to
functions.doc: Shows it to a player it was hidden from with `hide_from`.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded), or when the player is offline.

functions.name: is_hidden_from
functions.doc: Whether `hide_from` hid it from this player.

functions.name: team
functions.doc: The project's team it's in (`team:add_member`), or `nil` when it's in none, or in a team the project didn't make (one made with `/team` or by another plugin). For a player it answers while they're offline too; for any other entity, `nil` once it has gone.
functions.example:
local team = player:team()
if team and team:name() == "red" then
  player:send_message("<red>Go, red!")
end

functions.name: is_silent
functions.doc: Whether it makes no sounds. `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: set_silent
functions.doc: Silences it, or lets it make sounds again.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: has_gravity
functions.doc: Whether it falls. `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: set_gravity
functions.doc: Lets it fall, or keeps it floating where it is.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: is_invulnerable
functions.doc: Whether nothing but creative players and the void can hurt it. `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: set_invulnerable
functions.doc: Makes it invulnerable, or not.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: passengers
functions.doc: What rides on it, in order. Empty when nothing does, or once it has gone.

functions.name: add_passenger
functions.doc: Puts something on it to ride: a player on a horse, a zombie on a chicken. It can't ride itself, nor something riding it.

params.name: entity
params.doc: The rider.

returns.doc: Whether it got on: `false` when either has gone, or the game refused.

functions.name: remove_passenger
functions.doc: Takes a rider off it.

params.name: entity
params.doc: The rider.

returns.doc: Whether it was riding it.

functions.name: vehicle
functions.doc: What it rides, or `nil` when it rides nothing, and once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: inventory
functions.doc: What it carries, as an `Inventory`: a player's own inventory, a chest boat's or a donkey's chest, a villager's. `nil` for an entity without one, or once it has gone.

functions.name: target_block
functions.doc: The block it's looking at: a ray from its eyes along its direction, the first block whose shape it hits (fluids don't stop it). `nil` when it looks at nothing within reach, or once it has gone.

params.name: max_distance
params.doc: How far to look, in blocks. Default 20.

functions.example:
local block = player:target_block(5)
if block then
  block:break_naturally()
end

functions.name: target_entity
functions.doc: The entity it's looking at: a ray from its eyes along its direction, the first entity it hits, unless a block is in the way. Never itself. `nil` when there's none within reach, or once it has gone.

params.name: max_distance
params.doc: How far to look, in blocks. Default 20.

functions.name: target_centity
functions.doc: The centity it's looking at: a ray from its eyes along its direction, the first centity hitbox it hits (tested with the same shapes clicks are), unless a block is in the way. `nil` when there's none within reach, or once it has gone.

params.name: max_distance
params.doc: How far to look, in blocks. Default 20.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.example:
local cart = world:spawn_entity("minecraft:minecart", vec3(0, 64, 0))
if cart then
  cart:on("damage", function(event)
    event:cancel()
  end)
end

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `entity:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: Living
classes.doc: A living entity: a mob, an animal, an armour stand, a player. An `Entity` with health, attributes, status effects and equipment.

events.name: death
events.doc: It died: before `nf.on("entity_death")`, with the same event. Its handlers go with it afterwards. A `Player`'s own `death` is `player_death` instead, then `nf.on("entity_death")`.

events.name: heal
events.doc: It is getting health back: eating, regenerating, a potion, a beacon. `event:cancel()` stops it; assign `event.amount` to change how much. Heard by the entity before `nf.on("entity_heal")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: launch_projectile
events.doc: It launched a projectile: an arrow, a trident, a snowball, an egg, an ender pearl, a potion, a fireball. `event:cancel()` stops the projectile coming into the world. A dispenser's projectile has no shooter, so only `nf` hears it. Heard by the entity before `nf.on("projectile_launch")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: shoot_bow
events.doc: It shot a bow or a crossbow (a skeleton, a pillager, a player). `event:cancel()` stops the shot: nothing is fired or used up. Heard by the entity before `nf.on("entity_shoot_bow")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: change_effect
events.doc: One of its status effects is being added, changed, run out or taken away: a potion, a beacon, milk, a command or a script. `event:cancel()` stops the change. Heard by the entity before `nf.on("entity_change_effect")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

functions.name: health
functions.doc: How much health it has, from 0 to `max_health()` (2 is one heart), or `nil` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: set_health
functions.doc: Sets its health, up to `max_health()`. 0 kills it.

params.name: health
params.doc: From 0 to `max_health()`.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: max_health
functions.doc: The most health it can have, or `nil` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: damage
functions.doc: Hurts it, as an attack would: armour and effects count, it flinches, and its `damage` handlers hear it.

params.name: amount
params.doc: How much, before armour: 2 is one heart.

params.name: source
params.doc: Who did it, for knockback, kill credit and angering a mob.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: heal
functions.doc: Gives it health back, up to `max_health()`.

params.name: amount
params.doc: 2 is one heart.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: attribute
functions.doc: The value of one of its attributes now: its base with every modifier applied (its equipment's, its effects', scripts'), within the attribute's range. `nil` for an attribute it doesn't have (`scale` on a dropped item), or once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded). An attribute the server doesn't have is an error.

params.name: attribute
params.doc: Its id: `"minecraft:scale"`, or `"scale"` for short.

functions.example: local speed = zombie:attribute("movement_speed")

functions.name: attribute_base
functions.doc: One of its attributes' base value, before modifiers. `nil` for an attribute it doesn't have, or once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded). An attribute the server doesn't have is an error.

params.name: attribute
params.doc: Its id: `"minecraft:scale"`, or `"scale"` for short.

functions.name: set_attribute_base
functions.doc: Sets one of its attributes' base value. It's saved with the entity. An attribute the server doesn't have is an error.

params.name: attribute
params.doc: Its id: `"minecraft:scale"`, or `"scale"` for short.

params.name: value
params.doc: The new base. The attribute's value stays within the range the game gives it, whatever the base.

returns.doc: `false` for an attribute it doesn't have, once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.example: player:set_attribute_base("scale", 2)

functions.name: attribute_modifiers
functions.doc: Everything changing one of its attributes: the modifiers scripts added, and those from its equipment, effects and the game itself (sprinting), each with its full id. `nil` for an attribute it doesn't have, or once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded). An attribute the server doesn't have is an error.

params.name: attribute
params.doc: Its id: `"minecraft:scale"`, or `"scale"` for short.

functions.name: add_attribute_modifier
functions.doc: Adds a modifier to one of its attributes, replacing the project's modifier of the same id. Modifiers are saved with the entity, so give each a fixed id and remove it when it's done, rather than making new ones. The id is in the project's namespace (`netherforge.json`'s `namespace`): `"slow_zone"` is `"<namespace>:slow_zone"`, so nothing else's modifiers can be replaced or removed. An attribute the server doesn't have is an error.

params.name: attribute
params.doc: Its id: `"minecraft:scale"`, or `"scale"` for short.

params.name: id
params.doc: What it's called, to remove it later: lowercase letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `.` and `/`. `"<namespace>:"` in front is allowed, and the same.

params.name: amount
params.doc: How much.

params.name: operation
params.doc: How `amount` applies, as an item's `attribute_modifiers`: added; added times the base value; or the total multiplied by `1 + amount`. Default `"add_value"`.

returns.doc: `false` for an attribute it doesn't have, once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.example: zombie:add_attribute_modifier("movement_speed", "slow_zone", -0.5, "add_multiplied_total")

functions.name: remove_attribute_modifier
functions.doc: Takes one of the project's modifiers off one of its attributes. An attribute the server doesn't have is an error.

params.name: attribute
params.doc: Its id: `"minecraft:scale"`, or `"scale"` for short.

params.name: id
params.doc: The id `add_attribute_modifier` was given, with or without `"<namespace>:"`. Another namespace is an error: only the project's own modifiers can be removed.

returns.doc: Whether it had it: `false` when it didn't, for an attribute it doesn't have, once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: effects
functions.doc: Its status effects, like speed or poison. Empty once it has gone.

functions.name: has_effect
functions.doc: Whether it has a status effect. An effect the server doesn't have is an error. `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).
