params.name: effect
params.doc: Its id: `"minecraft:speed"`.

functions.name: add_effect
functions.doc: Gives it a status effect, replacing one of the same kind it has. An effect the server doesn't have is an error.

params.name: effect
params.doc: Its id: `"minecraft:speed"`.

params.name: ticks
params.doc: How long it lasts. -1 is for ever.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.example: player:add_effect("minecraft:speed", 20 * 10, { amplifier = 1 })

functions.name: remove_effect
functions.doc: Takes a status effect away. An effect the server doesn't have is an error.

params.name: effect
params.doc: Its id.

returns.doc: Whether it had it.

functions.name: equipment
functions.doc: What it holds or wears in a slot, or `nil` for nothing, and once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

params.name: slot
params.doc: `"body"` is a horse's or a wolf's armour.

functions.name: set_equipment
functions.doc: Puts an item in one of its slots, or empties it. An item table with a misspelled field, or an item the server doesn't have, is an error.

params.name: item
params.doc: Leave it out (or `nil`) to empty the slot.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `living:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: Mob
classes.doc: A mob: a `Living` with AI, like a zombie, a cow or a bat. It has a target, walks where it's sent (`move_to`), and its AI runs goals, the game's and any written in Lua.

events.name: path_end
events.doc: It stopped walking where `move_to` sent it: it got there (within 2 blocks), or gave up (no way further, its own AI sent it elsewhere, or the entity it went after has gone or left its world). Not after `stop_pathing` or a new `move_to`.
events.example:
zombie:on("path_end", function(event)
  if not event.reached then
    zombie:teleport(vec3(10, 64, 10))
  end
end)

events.name: target
events.doc: This mob is picking a target to go after, or forgetting the one it had (`event.target` is `nil`). `event:cancel()` keeps the target it had. The server only reports targets while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. Heard by the entity before `nf.on("entity_target")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

functions.name: target
functions.doc: What it is after (to attack it, or follow it), or `nil` for nothing, and once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: set_target
functions.doc: Sets what it is after, or calms it.

params.name: entity
params.doc: Leave it out (or `nil`) to clear it.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: has_ai
functions.doc: Whether it thinks for itself: moves, looks around, attacks. `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: set_ai
functions.doc: Lets it think for itself, or freezes it in place (it can still be pushed and hurt).

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: move_to
functions.doc: Makes it walk somewhere, finding its way round what's in the way: to a place in its own world, or after an entity, looking for a new path to wherever that entity is every 10 ticks. When it stops, its `path_end` handlers hear whether it got there. A new `move_to` replaces the walk it was on. Its own AI still runs, and can send it elsewhere (a zombie that sees a player goes for them), which ends the walk as given up; with `set_ai(false)` it doesn't walk at all.

params.name: target
params.doc: Where: a position in its world, a `Location` (in its world: another world is `false`), or an entity to go after.

returns.doc: Whether it found a path and set off: `false` when there's no way there from where it is (in the air, just spawned or falling, it finds none until it lands), for a target in another world or gone, once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.example:
zombie:on("path_end", function(event)
  log(event.reached and "made it" or "gave up")
end)
zombie:move_to(vec3(10, 64, 10), { speed = 1.2 })

functions.name: stop_pathing
functions.doc: Stops it walking where it was going, whoever sent it: a `move_to`, or its own AI. A walk `move_to` started ends without a `path_end`.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: has_path
functions.doc: Whether it is walking somewhere now, whoever sent it: a `move_to`, or its own AI. `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: path_target
functions.doc: Where the path it is walking ends, whoever sent it: as close as it can get to where it was sent, which is short of it when there's no way all the way there. `nil` when it isn't walking, or once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: goals
functions.doc: Every goal its AI has, the game's and any added: its regular goals (walking about, attacking, looking at players) and its targeting goals (what it picks a fight with), each with its key, its priority and the controls it claims. In no particular order. `nil` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: remove_goal
functions.doc: Takes goals off it: every one with the key, the game's or one a script added. Goals aren't saved, so a mob that unloads and loads again has the game's goals back.

params.name: key
params.doc: A goal's key, as `goals()` lists it: `"minecraft:random_stroll"`, or `"random_stroll"` for short (a key without a namespace is the game's). The project's own goals are `"<namespace>:<id>"`.

returns.doc: Whether it had one: `false` when it didn't, once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.example: zombie:remove_goal("minecraft:random_stroll")

functions.name: clear_goals
functions.doc: Takes every goal off it, its targeting goals too, but those `options.keep` names. A mob with no goals stands where it is but for what moves it (`move_to`, being pushed); goals added afterwards run as usual. Goals aren't saved, so a mob that unloads and loads again has the game's goals back.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.example: zombie:clear_goals({ keep = { "float" } })

functions.name: add_goal
functions.doc: Gives it a goal written in Lua, which its AI runs with the goals it has. Every tick or two the AI asks `should_start` of each goal that isn't running and whose controls are free, or held by goals of a lower priority (a bigger number), which it then stops; `start` runs when it starts, `tick` while it runs, and `stop` once `should_continue` says no or a more important goal takes one of its controls. A goal that claims `"target"` is a targeting goal: it runs with the mob's targeting goals (`hurt_by_target`, `nearest_attackable_target`) rather than its regular goals, so it claims nothing else. The id is in the project's namespace: `"guard_post"` is `"<namespace>:guard_post"`, and a goal with an id the mob already has replaces it. Goals aren't saved: they go when the mob unloads, and when the script that added them stops (a reload), so set them up again when it spawns or in the script's body. A callback that errors is reported, with its line, and its goal is taken off the mob. Goals added or removed from inside a goal's own callbacks change before the mob's next tick.

params.name: id
params.doc: What it's called, to remove it later: lowercase letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `.` and `/`. `"<namespace>:"` in front is allowed, and the same.

params.name: definition
params.doc: What it claims and does.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.example:
zombie:on("target", function(event)
  if event.target and event.target:is_player() then
    event:cancel()
  end
end)

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `mob:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: DroppedItem
classes.doc: An item lying on the ground, which players pick up by walking over it: an `Entity` holding one stack.

functions.name: item
functions.doc: The stack it is, or `nil` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: set_item
functions.doc: Changes the stack it is. An item table with a misspelled field, or an item the server doesn't have, is an error.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: pickup_delay
functions.doc: How many ticks until it can be picked up, or `nil` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: set_pickup_delay
functions.doc: Sets how many ticks until it can be picked up.

params.name: ticks
params.doc: 0 for at once; 32767 for never.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

classes.name: Player
classes.doc: Someone on the server: a `Living`, with everything living entities have, and more. A handle is a UUID, so keeping one is fine: if they leave, its methods answer `nil` or `false` rather than erroring, and work again when they come back. `nf.players.get` hands out handles to people who are offline too. Their real inventory is numbered: the hotbar 0 to 8, the rest of the main inventory 9 to 35, armour 36 (feet), 37 (legs), 38 (chest) and 39 (head), the offhand 40, then body armour 41 and a saddle 42 (what the game keeps there for any entity).

events.name: join
events.doc: A player joined the server. Assign `event.message` to change what everyone is told, or `nil` to say nothing. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_join")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: quit
events.doc: A player left. Assign `event.message` to change what everyone is told, or `nil` to say nothing. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_quit")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: chat
events.doc: A player is saying something in chat. `event:cancel()` stops anyone seeing it; assign `event.message` to change what they said, or `event.format` to change how the line looks. Handlers run on the main thread while the chat waits for them, so keep them quick. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_chat")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: interact
events.doc: A player clicked a block or the air (not an entity), once for each hand the game asks about. `event:cancel()` stops it: no door opens, nothing is placed or used. A right click with an item goes on to `player_use_item` unless it was cancelled. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_interact")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: interact_entity
events.doc: A player right-clicked an entity that isn't part of a centity (those are `centity_click`): after the entity's `interact` and the player's `interact_entity`. `event:cancel()` stops what the click would do. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_interact_entity")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: move
events.doc: A player moved into another block: walking, swimming, flying, falling, riding. Only moves that change block are heard, not every step or turn of the head, and teleports are `player_teleport` instead. `event:cancel()` puts them back where they were. The server only watches moves while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_move")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: teleport
events.doc: A player is being teleported: a command, a script, an ender pearl, a portal. `event:cancel()` keeps them where they are; assign `event.to` to send them somewhere else. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_teleport")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: change_world
events.doc: A player arrived in another world: through a portal, or teleported there. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_change_world")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: death
events.doc: A player died: before `nf.on("entity_death")` hears the same death. Assign `event.message` to change what everyone is told (or `nil` for nothing), `event.keep_inventory` to let them keep what they carry, and `event.drops` to change what falls. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_death")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: respawn
events.doc: A player is coming back after dying, or after leaving the end. Assign `event.location` to bring them back somewhere else. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_respawn")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: drop_item
events.doc: A player is dropping an item from their inventory. `event:cancel()` keeps it in their inventory. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_drop_item")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: pickup_item
events.doc: A player is picking up a dropped item. `event:cancel()` leaves it lying there (it is asked again while they stand on it). Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_pickup_item")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: use_item
events.doc: A player right-clicked with an item, on a block or the air, after `player_interact`: starting to eat or drink, drawing a bow, throwing a pearl, emptying a bucket, placing a block. `event:cancel()` stops the item being used, but not what the click does to the block (a door still opens). Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_use_item")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: consume_item
events.doc: A player finished eating or drinking something. `event:cancel()` stops it: the item stays and does nothing. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_consume_item")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: swap_hands
events.doc: A player pressed the key that swaps the items in their hands. `event:cancel()` leaves them where they are, so the key can be used for something else. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_swap_hands")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: sneak
events.doc: A player started or stopped sneaking. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_sneak")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: command
events.doc: A player typed a command (any command: Minecraft's, a plugin's or a script's), before it runs. `event:cancel()` stops it running. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_command")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: input
events.doc: A player's movement keys changed: what they hold down now, as their game sends it (forward, back, left, right, jump, sneak, sprint), whether or not they can move. For steering something they ride or controlling a centity. The server only watches input while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_input")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: change_slot
events.doc: A player picked another hotbar slot: a number key or the scroll wheel. `event:cancel()` keeps the slot they had. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_change_slot")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: swing
events.doc: A player swung an arm: every left click, on a block, an entity or the air, and some right clicks. The one way to hear a left click on the air. `event:cancel()` stops others seeing the swing, but not what the click does. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_swing")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: sprint
events.doc: A player started or stopped sprinting. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_sprint")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: fly
events.doc: A player started or stopped flying (in creative, or where `set_can_fly` lets them). `event:cancel()` keeps them as they were. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_fly")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: jump
events.doc: A player jumped. `event:cancel()` puts them back where they jumped from. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_jump")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: change_game_mode
events.doc: A player's game mode is changing: a command, a script, or the server. `event:cancel()` keeps the one they have. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_change_game_mode")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: change_food
events.doc: A player's food level is changing: going down as they get hungry, up as they eat. `event:cancel()` keeps it as it is; assign `event.food` to set it to another level. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_change_food")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: gain_experience
events.doc: A player is getting experience points: picking up orbs, or from a script or command. Assign `event.amount` to give another amount (0 for none). Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_gain_experience")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: change_level
events.doc: A player's experience level changed, up or down. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_change_level")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: kick
events.doc: A player is being kicked: by a command, a plugin or a script, or by the server (flying, timing out, a bad packet). `event:cancel()` keeps them on the server; assign `event.text` to change what their screen says, or `event.message` to change what everyone is told (`nil` for nothing). Leaving then goes on to `player_quit`. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_kick")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: complete_advancement
events.doc: A player completed an advancement (or a recipe was unlocked for them: those are advancements too, under `minecraft:recipes/`). Assign `event.message` to change what everyone is told, or `nil` to say nothing. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_complete_advancement")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: stop_using_item
events.doc: A player let go of an item they were using before it finished: a bow or crossbow drawn, a shield raised, a spyglass, food or a potion part-eaten. `event.ticks` says how long they held it. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_stop_using_item")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: break_item
events.doc: A tool, weapon or piece of armour a player was using wore out and broke. `event.item` is what it was, before it went. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_break_item")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: open_inventory
events.doc: A player is opening a vanilla inventory: a chest, a furnace, a crafting table, a villager's trades, a horse's. Not one of the project's menus: those are `menu_open`. `event:cancel()` keeps it closed. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_open_inventory")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: close_inventory
events.doc: A player closed a vanilla inventory (not one of the project's menus: those are `menu_close`), or left the server with it open. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_close_inventory")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: craft
events.doc: A player is taking what they crafted out of the result slot (with shift, as many as they can make). `event:cancel()` leaves it there and keeps the ingredients. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_craft")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: prepare_craft
events.doc: What's in a crafting grid changed (a crafting table's, or the 2×2 in a player's inventory), and the game is working out what it makes. Assign `event.result` to make something else, or `nil` for nothing: a recipe of your own. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_prepare_craft")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: prepare_anvil
events.doc: What is in an anvil changed (or the name typed into it), and the game is working out the result. Assign `event.result` to make something else (or `nil` for nothing), and `event.cost` to change how many levels it takes. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_prepare_anvil")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: prepare_smithing
events.doc: What is in a smithing table changed, and the game is working out the result. Assign `event.result` to make something else, or `nil` for nothing. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_prepare_smithing")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: prepare_grindstone
events.doc: What is in a grindstone changed, and the game is working out the result. Assign `event.result` to make something else, or `nil` for nothing. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_prepare_grindstone")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: enchant_item
events.doc: A player is enchanting an item at an enchanting table. `event:cancel()` stops it: nothing is enchanted or spent. Assign `event.cost` to change how many levels it takes. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_enchant_item")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

functions.name: name
functions.doc: Their name, as they have it now (a player can change theirs between visits).

functions.name: display_name
functions.doc: What chat and other plugins call them, as MiniMessage: their name unless something changed it. `nil` when they're offline.

functions.name: set_display_name
functions.doc: Changes what chat calls them, until they leave. Their real name, and what's above their head, stay.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: send_message
functions.doc: Sends them a chat line only they see.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage, like `"<green>Done!"`.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: send_actionbar
functions.doc: Shows a line above their hotbar for a couple of seconds.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: send_title
functions.doc: Shows a big title in the middle of their screen, with a smaller line under it.

params.name: title
params.doc: MiniMessage.

params.name: subtitle
params.doc: MiniMessage. Default none.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.example: player:send_title("<gold>Round 2", "<gray>Fight!", { stay = 40 })

functions.name: clear_title
functions.doc: Takes a title off their screen.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: play_sound
functions.doc: Plays a sound only they hear, where they are, following them. The same sounds `world:play_sound` takes: an unknown one is an error.

params.name: sound
params.doc: A Minecraft sound (`"minecraft:ui.button.click"`) or one of the project's resource pack sounds (`"<pack>/<key>"`, like `"ui/click"`).

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.example: player:play_sound("minecraft:ui.button.click", { pitch = 2 })

functions.name: stop_sound
functions.doc: Stops a sound playing for them, or every sound when it's left out. An unknown sound is an error.

params.name: sound
params.doc: The sound to stop.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: spawn_particle
functions.doc: Spawns particles only they see, in their world: `world:spawn_particle` with `viewers = { player }`, so `viewers` isn't an option here.

params.name: particle
params.doc: A particle id: `"minecraft:happy_villager"`.

params.name: position
params.doc: Where, in their world.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: run
functions.doc: Runs a command as them, with their permissions. The leading slash is optional.

returns.doc: Whether it ran.

functions.name: has_permission
functions.doc: Whether they have a permission node. `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: set_permission
functions.doc: Grants them a permission node (`true`), or denies it (`false`), alongside whatever a permissions plugin gives them. It's kept with the project's other grants and given back every time they join, until `unset_permission`; it works while they're offline too. A package (every project is one) may only grant nodes its own `netherforge.json` lists under `allow.permissions`, held to the package whose code makes the call as `requires` is (each entry allows itself and everything under it: `"shop"` allows `shop` and `shop.vip`): anything else is an error, and grants a later edit no longer allows stop applying.

params.name: permission
params.doc: The node: lowercase letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`, like `"shop.vip"`.

params.name: value
params.doc: `true` grants it; `false` denies it.

functions.example: player:set_permission("shop.vip", true)

functions.name: unset_permission
functions.doc: Takes back a node `set_permission` granted or denied: they have it again only if something else gives it to them.

params.name: permission
params.doc: The node.

returns.doc: `false` when the project hadn't set it.

functions.name: permissions
functions.doc: The nodes the project has set for them with `set_permission`, each to `true` (granted) or `false` (denied). Not every permission they have: `has_permission` answers that.

functions.name: is_operator
functions.doc: Whether they're a server operator, online or not.

functions.name: game_mode
functions.doc: Their game mode, or `nil` when they're offline.

functions.name: set_game_mode
functions.doc: Changes their game mode.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: food
functions.doc: How full they are, 0 to 20 (20 is a full bar), or `nil` when they're offline.

functions.name: set_food
functions.doc: Sets how full they are.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: saturation
functions.doc: How long until they get hungry again, 0 up to their food level, or `nil` when they're offline.

functions.name: set_saturation
functions.doc: Sets their saturation, up to their food level.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: level
functions.doc: Their experience level, or `nil` when they're offline.

functions.name: set_level
functions.doc: Sets their experience level.

params.name: level
params.doc: At least 0.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: experience_progress
functions.doc: How far the experience bar is towards the next level, 0 to 1, or `nil` when they're offline.

functions.name: set_experience_progress
functions.doc: Moves the experience bar, keeping their level.

params.name: progress
params.doc: 0 to 1.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: give_experience
functions.doc: Gives them experience points, as orbs would: their level goes up when the bar fills.

params.name: points
params.doc: At least 0.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: is_flying
functions.doc: Whether they're flying. `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: set_flying
functions.doc: Starts or stops them flying. They have to be able to fly (`set_can_fly`) to start.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: can_fly
functions.doc: Whether they may fly (double-tapping jump), as in creative. `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: set_can_fly
functions.doc: Lets them fly, or not.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: walk_speed
functions.doc: How fast they walk, 0 to 1 (0.2 is normal), or `nil` when they're offline.

functions.name: set_walk_speed
functions.doc: Sets how fast they walk.

params.name: speed
params.doc: −1 to 1; 0.2 is normal.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: fly_speed
functions.doc: How fast they fly, 0 to 1 (0.1 is normal), or `nil` when they're offline.

functions.name: set_fly_speed
functions.doc: Sets how fast they fly.

params.name: speed
params.doc: −1 to 1; 0.1 is normal.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: is_sneaking
functions.doc: Whether they're sneaking. `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: is_sprinting
functions.doc: Whether they're sprinting. `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: locale
functions.doc: The language their game is set to, like `"en_us"`, or `nil` when they're offline. Right after they join it can still be the default until their game says.

functions.name: ping
functions.doc: How long a message takes to reach them and come back, in milliseconds, as the server estimates it; `nil` when they're offline.

functions.name: kick
functions.doc: Disconnects them from the server.

params.name: reason
params.doc: What their screen says, MiniMessage. Default the server's own message.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: first_played
functions.doc: When they first joined this server, as Unix time in milliseconds (like `nf.server.unix_time()`), or `nil` for someone who never has (a handle from `nf.players.whitelisted()`, say).

functions.name: last_seen
functions.doc: When they were last on this server, as Unix time in milliseconds (like `nf.server.unix_time()`): now while they're online, `nil` for someone who never has been.
functions.example:
local seen = player:last_seen()
if seen then
  local days = (nf.server.unix_time() - seen) // 86400000
  log(player:name(), "was here", days, "days ago")
end

functions.name: is_banned
functions.doc: Whether they're banned from the server (by `ban`, `/ban` or anything else), and the ban hasn't run out.

functions.name: ban
functions.doc: Bans them from the server: they can't join until it runs out or `unban`. Kicks them, with the reason, when they're online. Banning someone already banned replaces their ban.
functions.example: player:ban({ reason = "Griefing", expires = nf.server.unix_time() + 7 * 86400000 })

functions.name: unban
functions.doc: Lifts their ban.

returns.doc: `false` when they weren't banned.

functions.name: is_whitelisted
functions.doc: Whether they're on the server's whitelist (which only keeps people out while it's on: `nf.server.is_whitelist_enabled()`).

functions.name: set_whitelisted
functions.doc: Puts them on the server's whitelist, or takes them off. Taking someone online off doesn't kick them.

functions.name: ender_chest
functions.doc: Their ender chest, as an `Inventory`, or `nil` when they're offline.

functions.name: held_item
functions.doc: What's in their main hand (the selected hotbar slot), or `nil` for nothing or when they're offline.

functions.name: set_held_item
functions.doc: Puts an item in their main hand, or empties it. An item table with a misspelled field, or an item the server doesn't have, is an error.

params.name: item
params.doc: Leave it out (or `nil`) to empty it.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: off_hand_item
functions.doc: What's in their offhand, or `nil` for nothing or when they're offline.

functions.name: set_off_hand_item
functions.doc: Puts an item in their offhand, or empties it.

params.name: item
params.doc: Leave it out (or `nil`) to empty it.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: held_slot
functions.doc: Which hotbar slot they have selected, 0 to 8, or `nil` when they're offline.

functions.name: set_held_slot
functions.doc: Selects a hotbar slot for them.

params.name: index
params.doc: 0 to 8.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

functions.name: give_item
functions.doc: Puts an item into their inventory, topping up matching stacks first, and drops what doesn't fit at their feet. An item table with a misspelled field, or an item the server doesn't have, is an error.

returns.doc: How many were dropped at their feet: 0 when everything fitted. `nil` when they're offline.

functions.example: player:give_item({ kind = "minecraft:gold_nugget", count = 5, data = { coin = true } })

functions.name: discover_recipe
functions.doc: Puts a recipe in their recipe book (with the toast that says so). `false` when they're offline, already had it, or the server has no such recipe; a project recipe id the project doesn't have is an error.

params.name: recipe
params.doc: A project recipe's id (`"ruby_sword"`), or any recipe the server has by its namespaced id (`"minecraft:bread"`).

functions.name: undiscover_recipe
functions.doc: Takes a recipe out of their recipe book. They can still craft it. `false` when they're offline or didn't have it.

params.name: recipe
params.doc: A project recipe's id (`"ruby_sword"`), or any recipe the server has by its namespaced id (`"minecraft:bread"`).

functions.name: has_discovered_recipe
functions.doc: Whether a recipe is in their recipe book. `false` when they're offline.

params.name: recipe
params.doc: A project recipe's id (`"ruby_sword"`), or any recipe the server has by its namespaced id (`"minecraft:bread"`).

functions.name: grant_advancement
functions.doc: Meets an advancement's criteria for them, as if they'd earned them: every criterion, or just `criterion`. Once the advancement is complete they get the toast, the chat line and its rewards, as when the game completes it.

params.name: advancement
params.doc: One of the project's advancements (`"first_steps"`, `advancements/first_steps.json`; a bare id is the calling package's own), one a package exports (`"acme:quests"`), or one of the game's by its key (`"minecraft:story/mine_diamond"`). One the server doesn't have is an error; so is a project advancement added since the server started, until it restarts.

params.name: criterion
params.doc: Only this criterion, by the name the advancement's file gives it. One it doesn't have is an error. Leave it out for every criterion.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline or had already met it.

functions.example:
player:grant_advancement("minecraft:story/mine_diamond")
-- One step of a quest of the project's own (advancements/treasure_hunter.json):
player:grant_advancement("treasure_hunter", "first")

functions.name: revoke_advancement
functions.doc: Takes an advancement back: every criterion of it, or just `criterion`.

params.name: advancement
params.doc: One of the project's advancements (`"first_steps"`, `advancements/first_steps.json`; a bare id is the calling package's own), one a package exports (`"acme:quests"`), or one of the game's by its key (`"minecraft:story/mine_diamond"`). One the server doesn't have is an error; so is a project advancement added since the server started, until it restarts.

params.name: criterion
params.doc: Only this criterion, by the name the advancement's file gives it. One it doesn't have is an error. Leave it out for every criterion.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline or hadn't met any of it.

functions.name: has_advancement
functions.doc: Whether they've completed an advancement. `false` when they're offline.

params.name: advancement
params.doc: One of the project's advancements (`"first_steps"`, `advancements/first_steps.json`; a bare id is the calling package's own), one a package exports (`"acme:quests"`), or one of the game's by its key (`"minecraft:story/mine_diamond"`). One the server doesn't have is an error; so is a project advancement added since the server started, until it restarts.

functions.name: advancement_progress
functions.doc: How far they are with an advancement: the criteria they've met and those left. `nil` when they're offline.

params.name: advancement
params.doc: One of the project's advancements (`"first_steps"`, `advancements/first_steps.json`; a bare id is the calling package's own), one a package exports (`"acme:quests"`), or one of the game's by its key (`"minecraft:story/mine_diamond"`). One the server doesn't have is an error; so is a project advancement added since the server started, until it restarts.

functions.example:
local progress = player:advancement_progress("minecraft:adventure/adventuring_time")
if progress then
  player:send_message(#progress.done .. " biomes, " .. #progress.remaining .. " to go")
end

functions.name: item_cooldown
functions.doc: How many ticks are left before they can use an item again, or 0. `nil` when they're offline.

params.name: key
params.doc: An item kind (`"minecraft:ender_pearl"`), or a cooldown group an item's `cooldown` names.

functions.name: set_item_cooldown
functions.doc: Makes them wait before using an item again, as an ender pearl does: every item of that kind, or every item in that cooldown group. Items whose own `cooldown` names another group aren't affected by their kind's.

params.name: key
params.doc: An item kind, or a cooldown group: `"<namespace>:<name>"`.

params.name: ticks
params.doc: How long; 0 ends it.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: open_menu
functions.doc: Opens a menu for them: the shared window for a `shared` menu, otherwise a new window of their own, filled from the file (or from the template). Its script's body has run (for a new window) and its `open` handlers have heard it by the time this returns. A menu the project doesn't have is an error; a template that's gone opens nothing (`nil`).

params.name: menu
params.doc: Its folder name under `menus/`, or a `MenuTemplate` from `nf.menus.create`.

params.name: options
params.doc: What to open it with: `context` for the new window. A key it doesn't take is an error.

returns.doc: The window, or `nil` when they're offline.

functions.name: menu
functions.doc: The project menu window they're looking at, or `nil` (nothing open, or a chest that isn't one of ours).

functions.name: close_menu
functions.doc: Closes the project menu they have open. Anything else on their screen (a chest, their own inventory) stays open.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline or have no menu of ours open.

functions.name: open_inventory
functions.doc: Shows them a real inventory, as if they'd opened it: a chest's, another player's, their ender chest. Whatever was on their screen closes.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline, or the inventory has gone.

functions.example:
local chest = player:ender_chest()
if chest then
  player:open_inventory(chest)
end

functions.name: close_inventory
functions.doc: Closes whatever container screen they have open: a chest, a project menu, their own inventory.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: open_dialog
functions.doc: Puts a dialog on their screen: the same as `dialog:open_for(player, options)`. One of the project's dialogs already on their screen is closed (its `close` handlers hear it). A dialog the project doesn't have is an error; a `Dialog` from `nf.dialogs.create` that's gone opens nothing (`false`).

params.name: dialog
params.doc: Its folder name under `dialogs/`, or a `Dialog` (one from `nf.dialogs.create`, say).

params.name: options
params.doc: What to open it with, for this opening only: `context`, input `values`, a `title` or `body` text.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.example: player:open_dialog("welcome", { values = { nickname = player:name() } })

functions.name: close_dialog
functions.doc: Takes whatever dialog is on their screen away. When it's one of the project's, its `close` handlers hear it.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: sidebar
functions.doc: Their sidebar: the panel of lines at the right of their screen. Always the same handle for the same player.
functions.example: player:sidebar():set_lines({ "<gold>Coins: " .. coins, "<gray>Round 2" })

functions.name: border
functions.doc: A border of their own, which only they see: the first call gives them one, a copy of their world's, and they see it instead of their world's until `reset_border()` or they leave (it follows them from world to world). The server draws it for them but doesn't enforce it: it doesn't hurt them. `nil` when they're offline.
functions.example:
local border = player:border()
if border then
  border:set_center(vec3(100, 0, 100))
  border:set_size(16)
end

functions.name: has_own_border
functions.doc: Whether they see a border of their own (`player:border()`) rather than their world's. `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: reset_border
functions.doc: Takes their own border away: they see their world's again, and the handle `border()` gave answers `nil`.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline or had no border of their own.

functions.name: tab_header
functions.doc: The text above the player list (what tab shows), as MiniMessage, or `nil` when there's none or they're offline.

functions.name: set_tab_header
functions.doc: Sets the text above the player list.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage; `""` for none.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: tab_footer
functions.doc: The text below the player list, as MiniMessage, or `nil` when there's none or they're offline.

functions.name: set_tab_footer
functions.doc: Sets the text below the player list.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage; `""` for none.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: tab_name
functions.doc: What the player list (tab) calls them, as MiniMessage: their name unless `set_tab_name` changed it. Their team's prefix and suffix go around it. `nil` when they're offline.

functions.name: set_tab_name
functions.doc: Changes what the player list calls them, until they leave. Their real name, what chat calls them and what's over their head stay.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage. Leave it out to go back to their name.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.example: player:set_tab_name("<gold>★ " .. player:name())

functions.name: tab_order
functions.doc: Where they come in the player list: higher comes first, and equal ones are sorted as Minecraft sorts them (by team, then name). 0 unless `set_tab_order` changed it; `nil` when they're offline.

functions.name: set_tab_order
functions.doc: Moves them up or down the player list, until they leave.

params.name: order
params.doc: Higher comes first; default 0.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: is_listed_for
functions.doc: Whether they're in another player's player list (`set_listed_for`). `false` when either is offline.

params.name: viewer
params.doc: Whose list.

functions.name: set_listed_for
functions.doc: Takes them out of another player's player list, or puts them back. Only the list's entry goes: the viewer still sees them in the world and hears them in chat (to hide them altogether, `hide_from`). It stays that way when either of them leaves and comes back, until it's set back.

params.name: viewer
params.doc: Whose list.

returns.doc: `false` when either is offline.

functions.example:
for _, other in ipairs(nf.players.online()) do
  staff:set_listed_for(other, false)
end

functions.name: below_name
functions.doc: The line under their name tag (`set_below_name`), as MiniMessage, or `nil` when they have none (or they're offline).

functions.name: set_below_name
functions.doc: Puts a line of text under their name tag, which every player sees: a rank, their health, a level. It goes when they leave. Minecraft draws this line for every player as soon as anyone has one, so while someone does, players without one show an empty line. It's shown through the scoreboard's below-name slot, which it takes over from anything else showing there.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage. Leave it out to take the line away.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.example: player:set_below_name("<gold>VIP")

functions.name: bossbars
functions.doc: The project's boss bars they're among the viewers of (`bossbar:show_to`), offline or not.

functions.name: resource_pack_status
functions.doc: What became of the project's resource pack on their game: `"loaded"`, `"declined"`, `"failed"`, `"pending"` (accepted, still downloading), or `nil` before their game has answered (and when they're offline, or there's no resource pack).

functions.name: send_block_change
functions.doc: Shows them a block that isn't there: only their game draws it, and the world doesn't change. It lasts until the real block updates (something changes it, or their game reloads the chunk), or `reset_block`. They can't walk through or stand on it any differently from the real block. A block state the server doesn't have is an error.

params.name: location_or_position
params.doc: Any point in the block; a bare vector is in their world.

params.name: state
params.doc: A block state, as `world:set_block` takes it: `"minecraft:gold_block"`.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.example: player:send_block_change(vec3(10, 64, 10), "minecraft:gold_block")

functions.name: reset_block
functions.doc: Shows them the real block again, after `send_block_change`.

params.name: location_or_position
params.doc: Any point in the block; a bare vector is in their world.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: send_equipment_change
functions.doc: Shows them another entity (or player) wearing or holding something it isn't: only their game draws it. It lasts until that entity's equipment really changes, or it goes out of their sight and comes back. An item table with a misspelled field, or an item the server doesn't have, is an error.

params.name: entity
params.doc: Whose equipment.

params.name: slot
params.doc: Which slot.

params.name: item
params.doc: What to show there. Leave it out (or `nil`) to show it empty.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline or the entity has gone.

functions.example: player:send_equipment_change(other, "head", { kind = "minecraft:carved_pumpkin" })

functions.name: camera
functions.doc: The entity they're watching through, as a spectator (`set_camera`), or `nil` when they're looking through their own eyes (or offline).

functions.name: set_camera
functions.doc: Makes them watch through another entity's eyes, as a spectator does when they click one: they see what it sees until they sneak, or this is called without one. They have to be in spectator mode (`set_game_mode("spectator")`).

params.name: entity
params.doc: Whose eyes. Leave it out (or `nil`) to give them their own back.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline, not in spectator mode, or the entity has gone.

functions.example:
player:set_game_mode("spectator")
player:set_camera(boss)
nf.after(100, function()
  player:set_camera()
end)

functions.name: compass_target
functions.doc: Where their compasses point (those that aren't tied to a lodestone): the world's spawn unless `set_compass_target` changed it. `nil` when they're offline.

functions.name: set_compass_target
functions.doc: Points their compasses somewhere: a quest, a base, a meeting point. It lasts until they leave.

params.name: location
params.doc: Where.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: open_book
functions.doc: Opens a book on their screen, as if they'd opened a written book, without giving them one.

params.name: pages
params.doc: Each page, MiniMessage, in order. At most 100.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: view_distance
functions.doc: How many chunks around them the server is sending: the server's own view distance, or what `set_view_distance` asked for, either of them lowered by their own game's setting. A change shows here from the next tick. `nil` when they're offline.

functions.name: set_view_distance
functions.doc: Changes how many chunks around them the server sends, until they leave, from the next tick. Their own game's setting still limits it: `view_distance()` says what they get.

params.name: distance
params.doc: In chunks, 2 to 32.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: data
functions.doc: Their saved table: one per player, by id, kept across restarts and shared by every script. By convention each module keeps its own part of it under its name (`player:data().shop`), so modules don't trip over each other. It works for someone offline too (`nf.players.get` finds anyone who has joined). It may hold strings, numbers, booleans, tables of them (keyed by strings, or a list numbered from 1), and the API's own values: `Vec3`s, `Location`s, `Item` tables, and `Player`, `Entity`, `Centity` and `World` handles, which come back as the same types (a handle to something gone answers `nil` or `false`, as handles do). Anything else (a function, a `Menu` window, a `Subscription`) is skipped when it's saved, with a line in the log naming where it was (`data.inventory[3]: a function can't be saved`). The table is live: change it and the change is saved, at the next autosave (every five minutes), when the project reloads and when the server stops. It stays in memory across hot reloads rather than being read again, so a script that reloads finds it as it left it. A table that would take more than 1 MiB isn't saved (the last save stands), and the log says so. It's also saved when they leave.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `player:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: Sender
classes.doc: Whoever ran a command: a player or the console. What `event.sender` is in a command handler. For a player, `event.player` is the same person as a `Player`.

functions.name: name
functions.doc: Their name: a player's name, or `"CONSOLE"`.

functions.name: send_message
functions.doc: Sends them a line: a chat line for a player, a log line for the console.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage, like `"<green>Done!"`.

returns.doc: `false` for a player who has gone offline.

functions.name: has_permission
functions.doc: Whether they have a permission node. The console has every one.

functions.name: is_player
functions.doc: Whether a player ran it.

functions.name: is_console
functions.doc: Whether the console ran it.

classes.name: World
classes.doc: A world on the server (the overworld, the nether, the end, or another the server loads). A handle is its name, so keeping one is fine: if the world is unloaded its methods answer `nil` or `false`. Positions are world space, in blocks.

events.name: block_break
events.doc: A player is breaking a block in this world: before `nf.on("block_break")`, with the same event, so `event:cancel()` here stops it and `event:stop()` keeps it from `nf`. Assign `event.drops` and `event.experience` to change what it drops.
events.example:
nf.worlds.default():on("block_break", function(event)
  if event.state == "minecraft:diamond_ore" then
    event:cancel()
  end
end)

events.name: block_place
events.doc: A player is placing a block in this world: before `nf.on("block_place")`, with the same event.

events.name: entity_spawn
events.doc: An entity is coming into this world: before `nf.on("entity_spawn")`, with the same event, so `event:cancel()` here stops it and `event:stop()` keeps it from `nf`.
events.example:
nf.worlds.default():on("entity_spawn", function(event)
  if event.entity:kind() == "minecraft:phantom" then
    event:cancel()
  end
end)

events.name: block_explode
events.doc: A block exploded: a bed in the nether or the end, a respawn anchor charged away from the overworld. `event:cancel()` stops the explosion breaking anything; assign `event.breaks_blocks = false` to keep every block standing but still hurt what is near, or `event.yield` to change how much of what breaks drops. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_explode")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_ignite
events.doc: A block is catching fire: flint and steel, a fire charge, lava, lightning, fire spreading, an explosion. `event:cancel()` keeps it from burning. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_ignite")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_burn
events.doc: A block is burning away in a fire. `event:cancel()` keeps it there (it may still catch fire again). In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_burn")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_spread
events.doc: A block is spreading to another: grass, mycelium, moss, vines, mushrooms, fire, sculk. `event.block` is where it spreads to, `event.source` where from. `event:cancel()` stops it. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_spread")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_flow
events.doc: Water or lava is flowing into another block (or a dragon egg teleporting there). `event:cancel()` stops it. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_flow")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_grow
events.doc: A crop, sapling stage, sugar cane, cactus, bamboo, pumpkin or melon is growing by itself (bone meal included). `event:cancel()` stops it. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_grow")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_fade
events.doc: A block is fading by itself: ice or snow melting, coral dying, fire burning out, farmland drying. `event:cancel()` keeps it as it is. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_fade")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_form
events.doc: A block is forming by itself: snow falling, ice freezing, concrete setting, obsidian or cobblestone from lava, frost walker ice or a snow golem's trail (`event.entity` says which). `event:cancel()` stops it. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_form")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: leaves_decay
events.doc: Leaves are decaying, far from any log. `event:cancel()` keeps them. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("leaves_decay")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: piston_extend
events.doc: A piston is pushing out. `event:cancel()` keeps it in, and everything it would push where it is. In this world: heard before `nf.on("piston_extend")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: piston_retract
events.doc: A piston is pulling back. `event:cancel()` keeps it out, and (for a sticky one) the block it would pull where it is. In this world: heard before `nf.on("piston_retract")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_redstone
events.doc: A block's redstone power is changing: a lever, a button, a pressure plate, a redstone lamp or wire. Assign `event.to` to give it another power. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_redstone")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: sign_change
events.doc: A player finished writing on a sign. `event:cancel()` keeps the sign as it was. In this world: heard before `nf.on("sign_change")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_start_break
events.doc: A player started hitting a block to break it. `event:cancel()` stops them breaking it; assign `event.instant = true` to break it at once, or `false` to make them wait for it. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_start_break")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_drop_item
events.doc: A block a player broke is dropping its items, its contents included (a chest's, a furnace's): after `block_break`, once it has gone. `event:cancel()` drops nothing. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_drop_item")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: weather_change
events.doc: It is starting or stopping raining (or snowing) in a world. `event:cancel()` keeps the weather it has. In this world: heard before `nf.on("weather_change")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: thunder_change
events.doc: A thunderstorm is starting or stopping in a world. `event:cancel()` keeps the weather it has. In this world: heard before `nf.on("thunder_change")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: lightning_strike
events.doc: Lightning is striking: a storm, a trident with channeling, a command or a script. `event:cancel()` stops it. In this world: heard before `nf.on("lightning_strike")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: chunk_load
events.doc: A chunk came into memory: someone came near, or it was generated for the first time (`event.generated`). The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("chunk_load")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: chunk_generated
events.doc: A chunk was generated, the first time it was loaded: its terrain, structures and the game's decorations are in place, so a script can add its own (a centity in a grove, a shrine on a hill). Its blocks are `event.x * 16` to `event.x * 16 + 15` across, the same along `z`, and can be read and changed in the handler; the chunks beside it may not be generated yet, so keep what you place inside it. Once per chunk, ever: one generated while no script listened isn't heard later. It happens for every new chunk a player explores, so keep handlers quick and leave most chunks alone. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("chunk_generated")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.
events.example:
nf.on("chunk_generated", function(event)
  if event.world:name() ~= "wilds" or math.random() > 0.2 then
    return
  end
  local ground = event.world:highest_block(vec3(event.x * 16 + 8, 0, event.z * 16 + 8))
  if ground and ground:biome() == "minecraft:dark_forest" then
    nf.centities.spawn("grove_spirit", event.world:location(ground:position() + vec3(0.5, 1, 0.5)))
  end
end)

events.name: chunk_unload
events.doc: A chunk is leaving memory, as everyone has gone away. Its blocks can still be read and changed in the handler. In this world: heard before `nf.on("chunk_unload")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: furnace_smelt
events.doc: A furnace, smoker or blast furnace finished smelting one item. `event:cancel()` stops it: the item stays unsmelted. Assign `event.result` to make something else. In this world: heard before `nf.on("furnace_smelt")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

functions.name: name
functions.doc: Its name, as `nf.worlds.get` takes it: `"world"`, `"world_nether"`.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether the server has it loaded now.

functions.name: environment
functions.doc: What kind of world it is, or `nil` once it has gone. A world of a custom dimension type says `"normal"`.

functions.name: location
functions.doc: A `Location` in this world, for the functions that take one (`player:teleport`, `nf.centities.spawn`). Give both `yaw` and `pitch`, or neither for a location with no facing; a `yaw` alone faces level.

params.name: position
params.doc: Where.

params.name: yaw
params.doc: Which way it faces horizontally, in degrees (0 south, 90 west).

params.name: pitch
params.doc: How far up or down, in degrees (−90 up, 90 down).

functions.example: player:teleport(nf.worlds.default():location(vec3(0, 80, 0), 180, 0))

functions.name: time_of_day
functions.doc: The time of day in ticks, 0 to 23999: 0 is sunrise, 6000 noon, 12000 sunset, 18000 midnight. `nil` once the world has gone. It's the game's clock, not the wall clock (`nf.server.unix_time()`).

functions.name: set_time_of_day
functions.doc: Sets the time of day, keeping the day count. Taken modulo 24000. Doesn't stop the clock (that's the daylight cycle game rule).

params.name: ticks
params.doc: 0 sunrise, 6000 noon, 12000 sunset, 18000 midnight.

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.name: day_count
functions.doc: How many whole days have gone by in this world, or `nil` once it has gone.

functions.name: weather
functions.doc: The weather now, or `nil` once the world has gone. Thunder always comes with rain.

functions.name: set_weather
functions.doc: Changes the weather, for `options.ticks` or for as long as the game would have kept it. A `ticks` below 1 is an error, as is a key `options` doesn't take.

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.example: world:set_weather("thunder", { ticks = 20 * 60 })

functions.name: spawn_location
functions.doc: Where players appear in this world when nothing else decides, or `nil` once the world has gone.

functions.name: set_spawn_location
functions.doc: Moves the world's spawn. A `Location` in another world is an error.

params.name: location_or_position
params.doc: Where: a `Location` in this world (its facing is used, when it has one) or a position.

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.name: min_height
functions.doc: The lowest block y there can be, or `nil` once the world has gone.

functions.name: max_height
functions.doc: One above the highest block y there can be, or `nil` once the world has gone.

functions.name: block
functions.doc: The block at a position: a handle that reads the world live, so it sees later changes. The position is floored to the block it's in. `nil` once the world has gone.

params.name: position
params.doc: Any point in the block.

functions.example: local below = this:world():block(this:position() - vec3(0, 1, 0))

functions.name: set_block
functions.doc: Changes the block at a position. A block state the server doesn't have (an unknown block, property or value) is an error. Blocks in chunks that aren't loaded can't be read or changed: that answers `nil` or `false`, and never loads the chunk (`world:load_chunk` does).

params.name: position
params.doc: Any point in the block.

params.name: state
params.doc: A block state: `"minecraft:stone"`, `"minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east]"`. Properties left out take their defaults.

returns.doc: Whether it changed: `false` in an unloaded chunk or a world that's gone.

functions.example: world:set_block(vec3(10, 64, 10), "minecraft:gold_block")

functions.name: fill_blocks
functions.doc: Sets every block in the box between two corners (both included) to one state. One call changes at most 32768 blocks: a bigger box is an error, so spread a big fill over several ticks with a task. A block state the server doesn't have is an error. Blocks in unloaded chunks are skipped.

params.name: from
params.doc: One corner.

params.name: to
params.doc: The opposite corner.

params.name: state
params.doc: A block state, as `set_block` takes it.

returns.doc: How many blocks it changed: 0 in a world that has gone.

functions.example:
nf.task(function()
  for y = 64, 127 do
    world:fill_blocks(vec3(0, y, 0), vec3(63, y, 63), "minecraft:air")
    nf.wait(1)
  end
end)

functions.name: highest_block
functions.doc: The highest block at a column that isn't air, ignoring the position's `y`. `nil` in an unloaded chunk, or a world that has gone.

params.name: position
params.doc: Any point in the column.

functions.name: is_chunk_loaded
functions.doc: Whether the chunk a position is in is loaded: whether its blocks can be read and changed now.

params.name: position
params.doc: Any point in the chunk.

functions.name: load_chunk
functions.doc: Loads the chunk a position is in, now, generating it if it's new: that can take a while, so do it rarely. The server unloads it again when nobody is near, as it does any chunk.

params.name: position
params.doc: Any point in the chunk.

returns.doc: Whether it's loaded: `false` for a world that has gone.

functions.name: locate_biome
functions.doc: Finds the nearest place where the world's generator puts a biome, as `/locate biome` does: it asks the generator, so it finds places in chunks nobody has been to, and never loads or generates a chunk. It looks out from `options.near` in a square spiral, every 32 blocks across and 64 up and down, so the place it gives is in the biome but may be up to 32 blocks past its nearest edge, and a biome narrower than that can be missed. A biome the world's generator never places (a nether biome in the overworld) is found nowhere at once. An id that isn't a biome on this server (a bare id that isn't one of the project's is an error saying how to write the game's), or a `radius` out of range, is an error at once. Finding nothing within the radius, or a world that has gone, fails. It works off the main thread, so its position arrives later: give `callback`, which is called with `position, err` once it's done, or call it inside a task (`nf.task`) without one, and it waits and returns `position, err`. Without a callback outside a task, it's an error. When it fails, `position` is `nil` and `err` says why.

params.name: id
params.doc: The biome, named as a file names one: the project's own by its id (`"ruby_grove"`, `biomes/ruby_grove.json`), a package's `"acme:grove"` (if it exports it), the game's always written in full (`"minecraft:desert"`).

params.name: callback
params.doc: Called on the main thread once it's done, as this script's code, with the place it found: a block position in this world, at the height it found the biome (or `nil` and why not). Not called if the script has stopped by then.

functions.example:
nf.task(function()
  local desert, err = world:locate_biome("minecraft:desert", { near = player:position() })
  if not desert then
    player:send_message("No desert near: " .. err)
    return
  end
  local ground = world:highest_block(desert)
  if ground then
    player:teleport(world:location(ground:position() + vec3(0.5, 1, 0.5)))
  end
end)

returns.doc: Only without a callback, in a task: the place it found: a block position in this world, at the height it found the biome, or `nil`.
Why it failed, when it did; `nil` when it worked.

functions.name: players
functions.doc: Everyone in this world now. Empty once the world has gone.

functions.name: centities
functions.doc: The live centity instances in this world: the same as `nf.centities.all` with this world as the filter's `world`.

params.name: filter
params.doc: Only some of them, as `nf.centities.all` takes it. Its `world`, if given, must be this one.

functions.name: entities
functions.doc: The entities in this world's loaded chunks, players included (as `Player` handles), or those the filter picks. Never the entities centities are drawn with. Empty once the world has gone. A filter key that isn't one of `EntityFilter`'s is an error.

params.name: filter
params.doc: Only one kind, one tag, living ones, or those near a point.

functions.example:
for _, zombie in ipairs(world:entities({ kind = "minecraft:zombie", near = here, radius = 16 })) do
  zombie:set_glowing(true)
end

functions.name: spawn_entity
functions.doc: Spawns an entity, set up as `options` say before anything sees it (its `entity_spawn` handlers included). A kind the server doesn't have, or one that can't be spawned (a player), is an error.

params.name: kind
params.doc: What: `"minecraft:zombie"`.

params.name: location_or_position
params.doc: Where: a `Location` in this world (facing its way, when it has a facing), or a position.

returns.doc: The new entity, or `nil` when the world has gone, its chunk isn't loaded, or an `entity_spawn` handler (or another plugin) cancelled it.

functions.name: spawn_item
functions.doc: Drops an item stack at a position, as if a block broke there. An item table with a misspelled field, or an item the server doesn't have, is an error.

params.name: position
params.doc: Where, in this world.

returns.doc: The dropped item, or `nil` when the world has gone, its chunk isn't loaded, or something cancelled it.

functions.name: spawn_particle
functions.doc: Spawns particles at a position. The particle's id comes from the server (`"minecraft:flame"`), and which options it takes depends on its kind: `color` and `size` for dust, `color` for coloured particles, `block_state` for block particles, `item` for item particles. An unknown particle, an option it doesn't take, or one it needs left out is an error. Particles that need data NetherForge can't send (vibrations, trails) are an error too. Players see them within 32 blocks, or 128 with `force`.

params.name: particle
params.doc: A particle id: `"minecraft:flame"`, `"minecraft:dust"`.

params.name: position
params.doc: Where, in the world.

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.name: play_sound
functions.doc: Plays a sound at a position, for everyone near enough to hear it. A Minecraft sound (`"minecraft:block.note_block.pling"`, checked against the server's sounds) or one of the project's resource pack sounds (`"<pack>/<key>"`, like `"ui/click"`, checked against `resource_packs/`). An unknown sound is an error.

params.name: sound
params.doc: A sound id.

params.name: position
params.doc: Where it comes from, in the world.

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.example: world:play_sound("minecraft:block.note_block.pling", block:position(), { pitch = 1.5 })

functions.name: explode
functions.doc: Makes an explosion at a position, as TNT would (TNT's power is 4): it damages and knocks back entities, and breaks blocks unless `break_blocks` is `false`.

params.name: position
params.doc: Its centre.

params.name: power
params.doc: How strong: 4 is TNT, 6 a charged creeper. At least 0.

returns.doc: Whether it went off: `false` when another plugin stopped it, or the world has gone.

functions.name: strike_lightning
functions.doc: Strikes lightning at a position: it sets fire and hurts what it hits, unless `effect_only`.

params.name: position
params.doc: Where it lands.

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.name: raycast
functions.doc: Casts a ray from a point and answers the first thing it hits within `max_distance`: a block's collision shape, an entity's hitbox, or a centity's hitbox (tested with the same shapes clicks are). `nil` when it hits nothing, and in a world that has gone. Blocks in unloaded chunks aren't hit.

params.name: from
params.doc: Where the ray starts, in the world.

params.name: direction
params.doc: Which way it goes: any length but zero.

params.name: max_distance
params.doc: How far it reaches, in blocks.

functions.example:
local world, eyes, facing = player:world(), player:eye_position(), player:direction()
local hit = world and eyes and facing and world:raycast(eyes, facing, 20)
if hit and hit.centity then
  hit.centity:play_animation("wobble")
end

functions.name: game_rule
functions.doc: A game rule's value: a `boolean` or an `integer`, depending on the rule. `nil` once the world has gone. A rule the server doesn't have is an error.

params.name: rule
params.doc: Its id, as the server names it: `"keep_inventory"`, `"random_tick_speed"`.

functions.name: set_game_rule
functions.doc: Sets a game rule in this world. A rule the server doesn't have, or a value of the wrong type for it (a `boolean` rule given a number), is an error.

params.name: rule
params.doc: Its id: `"keep_inventory"`.

params.name: value
params.doc: A `boolean` or an `integer`, as the rule takes.

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.example: world:set_game_rule("keep_inventory", true)

functions.name: spawn_limit
functions.doc: How many mobs of a spawn category the game keeps around each player here before it stops spawning more (the mob cap, per player, scaled by how many chunks are loaded around them), or `nil` once the world has gone. It's this world's own setting, or the server's (`bukkit.yml`) when the world has none.

params.name: category
params.doc: Which mobs count: `"monster"` for hostile ones, `"animal"` for farm animals, `"ambient"` for bats, and so on.

functions.name: set_spawn_limit
functions.doc: Sets this world's mob cap for a spawn category (see `world:spawn_limit`). `0` stops that category spawning naturally. A negative number goes back to the server's own setting. Mobs already there stay.

params.name: category
params.doc: Which mobs count.

params.name: limit
params.doc: The most of them there may be.

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.example: world:set_spawn_limit("monster", 30)

functions.name: spawn_interval
functions.doc: How many ticks pass between the game's attempts to spawn mobs of a spawn category here, or `nil` once the world has gone. It's this world's own setting, or the server's (`bukkit.yml`) when the world has none.

params.name: category
params.doc: Which mobs.

functions.name: set_spawn_interval
functions.doc: Sets how many ticks pass between spawn attempts for a spawn category in this world (see `world:spawn_interval`): lower is faster. `0` stops that category spawning naturally. A negative number goes back to the server's own setting.

params.name: category
params.doc: Which mobs.

params.name: ticks
params.doc: Ticks between attempts.

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.example: world:set_spawn_interval("monster", 2)

functions.name: is_managed
functions.doc: Whether this project may unload it (`world:unload`): it's one the project's scripts created (`nf.worlds.create`, `nf.worlds.copy`) or named in `netherforge.json`'s `managedWorlds`, and it isn't the server's main world. Any script can find, load and use any world; only managed ones can be taken away.

functions.name: unload
functions.doc: Unloads the world: players in it are moved out first (to the spawn of `options.move_players_to`, else of the main world), then the server saves it (unless `save` is `false`) and lets it go. With `delete`, its files are deleted too, off the main thread, and the project forgets it. Only a world this project manages can be unloaded (see `world:is_managed`): any other, the server's main world included, is an error, as is a `move_players_to` in this same world. A world it created stays the project's after a restart; find it again with `nf.worlds.load`.

returns.doc: Whether it was unloaded: `false` when it had gone already, or the server (another plugin) kept it.

functions.example: arena:unload({ save = false, delete = true, move_players_to = nf.worlds.get("lobby") })

functions.name: border
functions.doc: The world's border: the wall players can't pass, shown to everyone in the world (except a player given a border of their own with `player:border()`). `nil` once the world has gone.
functions.example:
local border = world:border()
if border then
  border:set_center(vec3(0, 0, 0))
  border:set_size(200)
  border:set_size(20, { ticks = 20 * 60 })
end

functions.name: save_structure
functions.doc: Saves the box between two corners (both included) as a structure named `id`, to place later with `place_structure`: an arena to reset, a prefab to stamp. It's saved in the server's data folder, not the project, and kept across restarts; saving the same id again replaces it. An id that isn't an id (lowercase letters, digits and `_`), or that one of the project's structures (`structures/<id>.nbt`) already has, is an error, as is a box over 48 blocks along any side. Air is saved too, so placing it puts back the empty space as well; it loads the chunks the box covers, as `/place` does.

params.name: id
params.doc: Its name: `"arena_reset"`.

params.name: from
params.doc: One corner.

params.name: to
