params.doc: The opposite corner.

returns.doc: Whether it was saved: `false` when the world has gone, or the file couldn't be written.

functions.example: world:save_structure("arena_reset", vec3(0, 60, 0), vec3(47, 90, 47), { entities = false })

functions.name: place_structure
functions.doc: Places a structure with its smallest corner at `position` (before it's turned): one of the project's (`structures/<id>.nbt`) or one a script saved (`save_structure`). Loads the chunks it covers, as `/place` does. A structure there's none of, one whose file can't be read, a `rotation` that isn't a multiple of 90 or an `integrity` outside 0 to 1 is an error.

params.name: id
params.doc: Which structure.

params.name: position
params.doc: Where its smallest corner goes, floored to a block.

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.example: world:place_structure("arena_reset", vec3(0, 60, 0), { rotation = 90, mirror = "none", integrity = 1, entities = false })

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `world:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: WorldBorder
classes.doc: A border: the wall at the edge of a square area, which players can't walk through and which hurts them outside it. Either a world's (`world:border()`), which everyone in the world sees, or one player's own (`player:border()`), which only they see and which the server draws for them but doesn't enforce: it doesn't hurt them, and doesn't stop what isn't them. Sizes and positions are blocks; times are ticks (20 a second). Its methods answer `nil` or `false` once its world has gone, or for a player's own, once they've left or gone back to their world's (`player:reset_border()`).

functions.name: center
functions.doc: Its centre, with `y` 0, or `nil` once it has gone.

functions.name: set_center
functions.doc: Moves its centre. `y` is ignored. More than 29,999,984 blocks out is an error.

params.name: center
params.doc: Where.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone.

functions.name: size
functions.doc: How wide it is, side to side, in blocks: while it's growing or shrinking, how wide it is now. `nil` once it has gone.

functions.name: set_size
functions.doc: Changes how wide it is: at once, or moving steadily there over `options.ticks`. A size below 1 or over 59,999,968, or negative `ticks`, is an error.

params.name: size
params.doc: Side to side, in blocks.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone.

functions.example: border:set_size(50, { ticks = 20 * 30 }) -- shrinks to 50 over 30 seconds

functions.name: damage
functions.doc: How it hurts players outside it, or `nil` once it has gone.

functions.name: set_damage
functions.doc: Changes how it hurts players outside it; what `damage` leaves out stays as it was. A negative value is an error. A player's own border is only drawn, so this changes nothing for them.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone.

functions.example: border:set_damage({ amount = 0.5, buffer = 2 })

functions.name: warning
functions.doc: When players' screens turn red as it comes near, or `nil` once it has gone.

functions.name: set_warning
functions.doc: Changes when players' screens turn red; what `warning` leaves out stays as it was. A negative value is an error.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone.

functions.example: border:set_warning({ distance = 5, ticks = 20 * 15 })

functions.name: contains
functions.doc: Whether a place is inside it. A `Location` in another world is outside a world's border; a player's own border has no world, so only the position counts. `false` once it has gone.

params.name: location_or_position
params.doc: Where: a `Location`, or a position.

functions.example:
local here = player:location()
if here and not border:contains(here) then
  player:send_message("<red>Get back inside!")
end

classes.name: Block
classes.doc: One block position in one world. The handle is the position, not what's there: it reads the world live, so a `Block` kept from earlier sees later changes. Blocks in chunks that aren't loaded can't be read or changed: that answers `nil` or `false`, and never loads the chunk (`world:load_chunk` does).

functions.name: world
functions.doc: The world it's in.

functions.name: position
functions.doc: Its corner with the smallest x, y and z: whole numbers, in the world.

functions.name: location
functions.doc: Its corner as a `Location`, with no facing.

functions.name: kind
functions.doc: What block it is, like `"minecraft:stone"`, or `nil` in an unloaded chunk.

functions.name: state
functions.doc: Its whole block state, like `"minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=bottom,shape=straight,waterlogged=false]"` (properties sorted), or `nil` in an unloaded chunk.

functions.name: property
functions.doc: One property's value, like `"east"` for `facing`, or `nil` when the block has no such property or its chunk isn't loaded.

params.name: name
params.doc: The property: `"facing"`.

functions.name: properties
functions.doc: Every property and its value; empty for a block without any, and `nil` in an unloaded chunk.

functions.name: is_air
functions.doc: Whether it's air (any kind). `false` in an unloaded chunk.

functions.name: is_solid
functions.doc: Whether it's solid: something players stand on and can't walk through. `false` in an unloaded chunk.

functions.name: is_liquid
functions.doc: Whether it's water or lava. `false` in an unloaded chunk.

functions.name: set_state
functions.doc: Changes it, as `world:set_block` does. A block state the server doesn't have is an error.

params.name: state
params.doc: A block state: `"minecraft:stone"`.

returns.doc: `false` in an unloaded chunk.

functions.name: set_property
functions.doc: Changes one property, keeping the rest of its state. A property the block doesn't have, or a value it can't take, is an error.

params.name: name
params.doc: The property: `"facing"`.

params.name: value
params.doc: Its new value: `"north"`.

returns.doc: `false` in an unloaded chunk.

functions.example:
local door = world:block(vec3(10, 64, 10))
if door then
  door:set_property("open", "true")
end

functions.name: break_naturally
functions.doc: Breaks it as a player would: it drops what it would drop (for that tool, when given) and turns to air.

params.name: tool
params.doc: What it was broken with, for its drops: silk touch, fortune, or the wrong tool dropping nothing.

returns.doc: Whether it broke: `false` for air, or in an unloaded chunk.

functions.name: relative
functions.doc: The block at an offset from this one.

params.name: offset
params.doc: An offset in blocks (floored), or the face of the neighbour: `"up"` is the block above.

functions.example: local above = block:relative("up")

functions.name: inventory
functions.doc: What a container block holds (a chest, a barrel, a hopper, a furnace, a shulker box), as an `Inventory`: the same one players see. A double chest's is both halves. `nil` for a block that isn't a container, and in an unloaded chunk.
functions.example:
local chest = world:block(vec3(10, 64, 10)):inventory()
if chest then
  chest:add_item({ kind = "minecraft:bread", count = 8 })
end

functions.name: custom
functions.doc: The project block that's here, as a `CustomBlock` (the same handle: one position, one block), or `nil` when what's here isn't one of the project's blocks, or its chunk isn't loaded.
functions.example:
local custom = world:block(vec3(10, 64, 10)):custom()
if custom then
  log(custom:id())
end

functions.name: light_level
functions.doc: How bright it is there, 0 to 15: the brighter of block light and sky light. `nil` in an unloaded chunk.

functions.name: sky_light_level
functions.doc: How much sky light reaches it, 0 to 15, whatever the time of day. `nil` in an unloaded chunk.

functions.name: biome
functions.doc: The biome here, named as `locate_biome` takes one: a biome of the project reads as its id (`"ruby_grove"`), a package's as `"acme:grove"` (to a package's own scripts, its own is bare), the game's as `"minecraft:plains"`. The game keeps biomes per 4×4×4 blocks, so neighbouring blocks share one. `nil` in an unloaded chunk.
functions.example:
if block:biome() == "minecraft:snowy_plains" then
  block:set_state("minecraft:snow_block")
end

functions.name: data
functions.doc: This position's own table for scripts to keep things in, saved with the chunk: the same table every time, shared by every script. Change it in place; it's saved when the server autosaves, when the chunk unloads and when the server stops. It stays with the position, whatever happens to the block. It may hold strings, numbers, booleans, tables of them (keyed by strings, or a list numbered from 1), and the API's own values: `Vec3`s, `Location`s, `Item` tables, and `Player`, `Entity`, `Centity` and `World` handles, which come back as the same types (a handle to something gone answers `nil` or `false`, as handles do). Anything else (a function, a `Menu` window, a `Subscription`) is skipped when it's saved, with a line in the log naming where it was (`data.inventory[3]: a function can't be saved`). `nil` in an unloaded chunk.
functions.example:
local data = block:data()
if data then
  data.uses = (data.uses or 0) + 1
end

classes.name: CustomBlock
classes.doc: A block of the project's own at a position, which is a `Block` like any other: it reads the world live, so one kept from earlier turns into whatever is there now (`block:custom()` says whether it still is one). The game holds it as a note block state its resource pack draws as the block, so `kind()` and `state()` answer that; `id()` and `project()` say which block it is. `data()` is its own table: it starts empty when the block is placed and is gone when the block is, whatever replaced it. `break_naturally` rolls its loot table; replacing or filling over it with `set_state` or `world:fill_blocks` removes it without drops.

functions.name: id
functions.doc: Its id: its project block's folder name under `blocks/`, or `namespace:id` for one a package it depends on exports, as the calling script names it. `nil` once what's here isn't a block of the project's.

functions.name: project
functions.doc: The project block it's one of, or `nil` once what's here isn't one.

classes.name: ProjectBlock
classes.doc: A project block from `blocks/<id>/block.json`: `this` in the block's script, and what `nf.blocks.get` hands out. It's the kind of block, not one placed in the world: its handlers hear what players do with any block of it (see `CustomBlock` for one placed). If the block is deleted, its methods answer `nil` or `false` and its handlers go.

events.name: place
events.doc: A block of this kind is about to be placed: by a player right-clicking with an item that places it (`event.player`, `event.item`), or by a script (`project_block:place`, neither set). `event:cancel()` stops it. It is heard before the world's own `block_place`, which a player's placing also raises (with the block's note block state as `state`).
events.example:
this:on("place", function(event)
  if event.player and not event.player:has_permission("mine.build") then
    event:cancel()
  end
end)

events.name: break
events.doc: A player is breaking a block of this kind: before the world's own `block_break`, then `nf.on("block_break")`, with the same event, so `event:cancel()` here stops it. `event.drops` is what its loot table rolled for the tool they hold (none when `requiresTool` and it isn't the right one); assign it, and `event.experience`, to change what drops. Breaking it by a script (`break_naturally`) or an explosion rolls the same drops without this event.

events.name: click
events.doc: A player clicked a block of this kind: `event.click` is `"left"` (hitting it, which also starts breaking it) or `"right"`. It is heard after the player's own `interact` and `nf.on("player_interact")`, so one of them cancelling the click keeps it from here. `event:cancel()` stops what the click would do, which for a right click is placing something against it.
events.example:
this:on("click", function(event)
  if event.click == "right" then
    event.player:send_message("<red>Ruby ore")
  end
end)

events.name: tick
events.doc: Every `tick` ticks (the block's `tick` in `block.json`; without it nothing ticks) for each block of this kind in a loaded chunk. Blocks in chunks that aren't loaded are not ticked, and a block placed or loaded is first ticked a full interval later. Keep per-block state in `event.block:data()`.
events.example:
this:on("tick", function(event)
  local data = event.block:data()
  if data then
    data.age = (data.age or 0) + 1
  end
end)

functions.name: id
functions.doc: Its id: its folder name under `blocks/`.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether the project still has it.

functions.name: place
functions.doc: Places one at the block position a location is in, as `world:set_block` would: whatever is there is replaced, and nothing drops. Its `place` handlers are not asked (a script placing a block isn't a player placing one), and it isn't a `block_place` either. If the block has a centity, it's spawned over the block. `nil` when the chunk isn't loaded, or when the game has no note block state left to hold the block in (the project has more blocks than that).

params.name: location
params.doc: Where.

functions.example:
local ore = nf.blocks.get("ruby_ore")
if ore then
  ore:place(player:location())
end

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `block:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: Inventory
classes.doc: A real inventory: a player's (`player:inventory()`), their ender chest, a container block's (`block:inventory()`: a chest, a barrel, a hopper, a furnace) or an entity's (a chest boat, a donkey, a villager). Its item methods work like `Menu`'s. The handle is where the inventory is, so it reads live; once that's gone (a chest broken, a player offline, a chunk unloaded) its methods answer `nil`, `false` or nothing. Slots are numbered from 0. A player's: the hotbar 0 to 8, the rest of the main inventory 9 to 35, armour 36 (feet), 37 (legs), 38 (chest) and 39 (head), the offhand 40, then body armour 41 and a saddle 42 (what the game keeps there for any entity). A double chest's inventory is both halves, 0 to 53.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether it's there now: the player online, the container still a container, the entity in the world and its chunk loaded.

functions.name: kind
functions.doc: What kind of inventory it is: `"player"`, `"ender_chest"`, `"chest"`, `"barrel"`, `"shulker_box"`, `"hopper"`, `"dispenser"`, `"dropper"`, `"furnace"`, `"brewing"`, … `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: size
functions.doc: How many slots it has: 43 for a player, 27 for a chest, 54 for a double chest. 0 once it's gone.

functions.name: holder
functions.doc: Whose it is: the `Player` (for a player's inventory and ender chest), the `Entity`, or the `Block`. `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: item
functions.doc: What is in a slot, or `nil` for an empty one (or once it's gone). A slot outside it is an error.

params.name: index
params.doc: From 0.

functions.name: set_item
functions.doc: Puts an item in a slot, replacing what was there, or empties it. A slot outside it, an item table with a misspelled field, or an item the server doesn't have is an error.

params.name: index
params.doc: From 0.

params.name: item
params.doc: Leave it out (or `nil`) to empty the slot.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: items
functions.doc: Every item in it, keyed by slot. Empty slots are left out, so `pairs` visits only what is there.
functions.example:
for index, item in pairs(player:inventory():items()) do
  log(index, item.kind, item.count)
end

functions.name: add_item
functions.doc: Puts an item wherever it fits, topping up matching stacks first, the way picking something up does. In a player's inventory only the hotbar and main inventory take it, never armour or the offhand.

returns.doc: How many didn't fit: 0 when all of it went in, all of it once the inventory's gone.

functions.name: remove_item
functions.doc: Takes away items that match, from the first slot on, until `count` are gone or none are left.

params.name: match
params.doc: An item kind (`"minecraft:diamond"`), or a partial `Item` that matches a stack when every field it gives matches: `{ kind = "minecraft:paper", name = "<gold>Ticket" }`. Its `data` matches as a subset, so `{ data = { coin = true } }` finds coins whatever else they carry. `count` and `raw` have no place in a match; a field `Item` doesn't have is an error.

params.name: count
params.doc: How many at most. Leave it out for every one that matches.

returns.doc: How many it took.

functions.example: local taken = player:inventory():remove_item({ kind = "minecraft:gold_nugget", data = { coin = true } }, 10)

functions.name: count_item
functions.doc: How many items match, across every slot.

params.name: match
params.doc: An item kind (`"minecraft:diamond"`), or a partial `Item` that matches a stack when every field it gives matches: `{ kind = "minecraft:paper", name = "<gold>Ticket" }`. Its `data` matches as a subset, so `{ data = { coin = true } }` finds coins whatever else they carry. `count` and `raw` have no place in a match; a field `Item` doesn't have is an error.

functions.name: has_item
functions.doc: Whether at least `count` items match.

params.name: match
params.doc: An item kind (`"minecraft:diamond"`), or a partial `Item` that matches a stack when every field it gives matches: `{ kind = "minecraft:paper", name = "<gold>Ticket" }`. Its `data` matches as a subset, so `{ data = { coin = true } }` finds coins whatever else they carry. `count` and `raw` have no place in a match; a field `Item` doesn't have is an error.

params.name: count
params.doc: Default 1.

functions.name: first_slot
functions.doc: The first slot holding an item that matches, or `nil` when none does.

params.name: match
params.doc: An item kind (`"minecraft:diamond"`), or a partial `Item` that matches a stack when every field it gives matches: `{ kind = "minecraft:paper", name = "<gold>Ticket" }`. Its `data` matches as a subset, so `{ data = { coin = true } }` finds coins whatever else they carry. `count` and `raw` have no place in a match; a field `Item` doesn't have is an error.

functions.name: clear
functions.doc: Empties every slot. To empty one, `set_item(index, nil)`.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: viewers
functions.doc: The players who have it open on their screen now. (A player's own inventory, open in their own inventory screen, doesn't count: the server can't tell.)

classes.name: BossBar
classes.doc: A bar across the top of players' screens, made by `nf.bossbars.create`. It shows to the players it's shown to (`show_to`), and stays theirs when they leave and come back. It belongs to the script that made it and goes when that script unloads (or `remove()`): from then on its methods answer `nil` or `false`.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether it's still there: `false` once it's removed or its script has unloaded.

functions.name: show_to
functions.doc: Shows it to a player, now if they're online and again whenever they join.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: hide_from
functions.doc: Stops showing it to a player.

returns.doc: Whether they were among its viewers: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: viewers
functions.doc: Everyone it's shown to, online or not. Empty once it's gone.

functions.name: text
functions.doc: What it says, as MiniMessage, or `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_text
functions.doc: Changes what it says.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: progress
functions.doc: How full it is, 0 to 1, or `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_progress
functions.doc: Fills it to a fraction. Outside 0 to 1 is an error.

params.name: progress
params.doc: 0 to 1.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.example: bar:set_progress(time_left / round_length)

functions.name: color
functions.doc: Its colour, or `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_color
functions.doc: Changes its colour.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: style
functions.doc: Whether it's one bar or split into notches, or `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_style
functions.doc: Makes it one bar, or splits it into 6, 10, 12 or 20 notches.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: remove
functions.doc: Takes it off every screen for good.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone already.

classes.name: Sidebar
classes.doc: The panel of lines at the right of one player's screen, from `player:sidebar()`: up to 15 lines of MiniMessage under a title, without the score numbers vanilla shows. Setting its title or lines shows it. A sidebar needs a scoreboard of the player's own, so while it shows NetherForge gives them one that copies the server's teams and the lines under name tags (the project's own changes at once, anyone else's within a second), keeping team colours and name tags working; hiding it gives them the server's back. It's cleared when they leave. For someone offline its methods answer `nil` or `false`.

functions.name: title
functions.doc: Its title, as MiniMessage, or `nil` when it has none (or they're offline).

functions.name: set_title
functions.doc: Changes its title, and shows it.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: lines
functions.doc: Its lines, top first, as MiniMessage. Empty when it has none (or they're offline).

functions.name: set_lines
functions.doc: Replaces its lines, and shows it. More than 15 is an error.

params.name: lines
params.doc: MiniMessage, top first. Lines may repeat; an empty string is a blank line.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.example:
player:sidebar():set_title("<gold><b>Arena")
player:sidebar():set_lines({ "Kills: " .. kills, "", "<gray>play.example.net" })

functions.name: is_visible
functions.doc: Whether they see it now. `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: set_visible
functions.doc: Shows it, or hides it and gives them the server's scoreboard back, keeping its title and lines for next time.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: clear
functions.doc: Takes its title and lines away and hides it, giving them the server's scoreboard back.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

classes.name: Team
classes.doc: A scoreboard team, made by `nf.teams.create`: what goes before and after its members' names (over their heads and in the player list), the colour of those names and of their glow, whether members can hurt each other, see each other while invisible, see name tags and push each other. Members are players and other entities. Teams live on the server's scoreboard, so every player sees them (while a player's sidebar shows, its scoreboard copies them). A team belongs to the script that made it and goes when that script unloads (a reload, the server stopping), members and all, so the script's body makes it again; from then on its methods answer `nil` or `false`. On the server's scoreboard it's called `nf.<name>` (what `/team` commands name it), so it never collides with a team made with `/team` or by another plugin, and NetherForge never touches those.

functions.name: name
functions.doc: Its name, as `nf.teams.create` was given it (without the `nf.` the scoreboard adds).

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether it's still there: `false` once it's removed or its script has unloaded.

functions.name: add_member
functions.doc: Puts a player or entity in it, taking them out of any other team they're in (one team at a time is Minecraft's rule). A player stays in it when they leave and come back, and can be added while offline.

params.name: member
params.doc: A player or any other entity.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone, or once the entity has.

functions.example: red:add_member(player)

functions.name: remove_member
functions.doc: Takes a player or entity out of it.

params.name: member
params.doc: A player or any other entity.

returns.doc: Whether they were in it: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: has_member
functions.doc: Whether a player or entity is in it. `false` once it's gone.

params.name: member
params.doc: A player or any other entity.

functions.name: members
functions.doc: Its members that are here: players online (as `Player`) and entities in loaded chunks. Empty once it has gone.

functions.name: display_name
functions.doc: What it's called where Minecraft names a team (the `/team list` output), as MiniMessage; `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_display_name
functions.doc: Changes what it's called.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: prefix
functions.doc: What goes before each member's name, over their head and in the player list, as MiniMessage; `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_prefix
functions.doc: Changes what goes before each member's name.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage; `""` for none.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: suffix
functions.doc: What goes after each member's name, as MiniMessage; `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_suffix
functions.doc: Changes what goes after each member's name.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage; `""` for none.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: color
functions.doc: The colour of its members' names, and of their outline when they glow; `nil` when it has none (or once it's gone).

functions.name: set_color
functions.doc: Colours its members' names, and their outline when they glow (a glowing entity's outline is white otherwise). A prefix's own colours still win over it for the prefix.

params.name: color
params.doc: Leave it out for none.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.example:
red:set_color("red")
zombie:set_glowing(true)

functions.name: has_friendly_fire
functions.doc: Whether members can hurt each other. `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_friendly_fire
functions.doc: Lets members hurt each other, or stops them.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: can_see_invisible_teammates
functions.doc: Whether members see each other, faintly, while invisible. `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_can_see_invisible_teammates
functions.doc: Lets members see each other while invisible, or stops them.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: nametags
functions.doc: Who sees its members' name tags; `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_nametags
functions.doc: Changes who sees its members' name tags.

params.name: visibility
params.doc: `"always"` (the default), `"never"`, `"hide_for_other_teams"` (only teammates see them) or `"hide_for_own_team"` (only players outside the team see them).

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: collision
functions.doc: Who its members push, and are pushed by; `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_collision
functions.doc: Changes who its members push, and are pushed by.

params.name: rule
params.doc: `"always"` (the default), `"never"`, `"push_other_teams"` (members pass through each other) or `"push_own_team"` (members push only each other).

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: remove
functions.doc: Takes it off the scoreboard for good; its members are in no team any more.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone already.

classes.name: Database
classes.doc: A database, from `nf.db()` or `nf.db('network')`. `nf.db()` is this package's own: one SQLite file per package, kept across restarts, which every other package (a dependency, or the project using one) never sees; its tables are made by the package's `migrations/NNN_name.sql` files, applied in order when the project loads. `nf.db('network')` (a name) is a connection to a MySQL or PostgreSQL server that the server's owner set up under `databases:` in the plugin's `config.yml`: shared by every package the owner lists for it, so give tables a name no other package would (`shop_scores`), create them yourself (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`: migrations belong to the package's own database only), and write the SQL in the server's dialect. The handle is the same either way: the same calls, `?` and `params`, rows and `value, err` answers. Every function is asynchronous (see `nf.task`): the work runs on a background thread, so a slow query never holds up the server, and one database runs its work in the order it was given, so a task's `db:execute` is always done before its next `db:query`. Use it from a task (`local rows, err = db:query(...)`) or give a callback. A mistake in the SQL, a constraint a row breaks or a database that couldn't be migrated is `nil, err`, never a thrown error.

functions.name: query
functions.doc: Runs a statement that reads rows and gives them all. Each row is a table keyed by column name; a `NULL` column is left out of its row (so `row.nickname` is `nil`), integers come as `integer`s, reals as `number`s and text as `string`s; what a MySQL or PostgreSQL server has beyond those arrives as one of them (a boolean as `1` or `0`, a `DECIMAL` as a `number`, a date or time as its text, an integer too big for an `integer` as text; `CAST(column AS CHAR)` keeps a decimal exact). A column that holds a blob is an error: `hex(column)` it in the SQL (`encode(column, 'hex')` on PostgreSQL). One SQL statement in the database's own dialect (SQLite's for the package's own database; MySQL's or PostgreSQL's for a connection the server owner set up), with `?` where a value goes: the values come in `params`, never inside the text, so a name a player typed can't become SQL. A second statement after a `;` is an error: use `db:transaction` for several. On PostgreSQL a literal `?` (the JSON operators) is written `??`. It works off the main thread, so its rows arrives later: give `callback`, which is called with `rows, err` once it's done, or call it inside a task (`nf.task`) without one, and it waits and returns `rows, err`. Without a callback outside a task, it's an error. When it fails, `rows` is `nil` and `err` says why.

params.name: sql
params.doc: The statement: `"SELECT name, score FROM scores WHERE score > ?"`.

params.name: params
params.doc: The values for the `?`s, in order: `{ player_name, 5 }`. Each is a `string`, `number`, `integer` or `boolean` (stored as 1 or 0); a hole in the list (`{ 1, nil, 3 }`) is SQL `NULL`, and so are the last `?`s when the list is shorter (Lua can't tell `{ name, nil }` from `{ name }`). Any other kind of value is an error, and more values than `?`s fails the statement.

params.name: callback
params.doc: Called on the main thread once it's done, as this script's code, with the rows, in the order the statement gave them (empty when there are none) (or `nil` and why not). Not called if the script has stopped by then.

functions.example:
local db = nf.db()
nf.task(function()
  local rows, err = db:query("SELECT name, score FROM scores ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT ?", { 10 })
  if not rows then
    log("no scores: " .. err)
    return
  end
  for place, row in ipairs(rows) do
    log(place, row.name, row.score)
  end
end)

returns.doc: Only without a callback, in a task: the rows, in the order the statement gave them (empty when there are none), or `nil`.
Why it failed, when it did; `nil` when it worked.

functions.name: execute
functions.doc: Runs a statement that changes data (`INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`) and says what it changed. It's committed on its own. One SQL statement in the database's own dialect (SQLite's for the package's own database; MySQL's or PostgreSQL's for a connection the server owner set up), with `?` where a value goes: the values come in `params`, never inside the text, so a name a player typed can't become SQL. A second statement after a `;` is an error: use `db:transaction` for several. On PostgreSQL a literal `?` (the JSON operators) is written `??`. It works off the main thread, so its result arrives later: give `callback`, which is called with `result, err` once it's done, or call it inside a task (`nf.task`) without one, and it waits and returns `result, err`. Without a callback outside a task, it's an error. When it fails, `result` is `nil` and `err` says why.

params.name: sql
params.doc: The statement: `"INSERT INTO scores (name, score) VALUES (?, ?)"`.

params.name: params
params.doc: The values for the `?`s, in order: `{ player_name, 5 }`. Each is a `string`, `number`, `integer` or `boolean` (stored as 1 or 0); a hole in the list (`{ 1, nil, 3 }`) is SQL `NULL`, and so are the last `?`s when the list is shorter (Lua can't tell `{ name, nil }` from `{ name }`). Any other kind of value is an error, and more values than `?`s fails the statement.

params.name: callback
params.doc: Called on the main thread once it's done, as this script's code, with how many rows it changed and the last row it inserted (or `nil` and why not). Not called if the script has stopped by then.

functions.example:
nf.task(function()
  local result, err = nf.db():execute("INSERT INTO scores (name, score) VALUES (?, ?)", { player:name(), 10 })
  if not result then
    log("not saved: " .. err)
  end
end)

returns.doc: Only without a callback, in a task: how many rows it changed and the last row it inserted, or `nil`.
Why it failed, when it did; `nil` when it worked.

functions.name: transaction
functions.doc: Runs several statements as one: all of them happen, or, when one fails, none do (the ones before it are undone) and the error says which failed. Other work on the database waits until it is done, so nothing sees it half-way. It works off the main thread, so its results arrives later: give `callback`, which is called with `results, err` once it's done, or call it inside a task (`nf.task`) without one, and it waits and returns `results, err`. Without a callback outside a task, it's an error. When it fails, `results` is `nil` and `err` says why.

params.name: statements
params.doc: The statements, run in order. Rows they would give are ignored: a transaction changes data.

params.name: callback
params.doc: Called on the main thread once it's done, as this script's code, with what each statement changed, in the same order (or `nil` and why not). Not called if the script has stopped by then.

returns.doc: Only without a callback, in a task: what each statement changed, in the same order, or `nil`.
Why it failed, when it did; `nil` when it worked.

classes.name: Menu
classes.doc: A live menu window from `menus/<id>/`: `this` in the menu's script, and what `player:open_menu`, `nf.menus.shared` and every menu event hand out. One that isn't `shared` exists from the moment it's opened for someone until its last viewer closes it; after that its methods return `nil` or `false` rather than erroring, and its handlers (and its slots') are gone. A shared one lives as long as the project.

events.name: open
events.doc: Someone opened this window: `player:open_menu`, or `menu:open_for`. Then the `MenuTemplate` it was made from (if it was) hears it, then `nf.on("menu_open")`.

events.name: close
events.doc: Someone closed this window, or left the server with it open. Then the `MenuTemplate` it was made from (if it was) hears it, then `nf.on("menu_close")`. When the last viewer of a window that isn't shared closes it, the window goes, and with it every handler on it.

events.name: click
events.doc: Someone clicked while this window was open, in it or in their own inventory below it. A click on one of its slots is heard by that slot first; then the menu; then the `MenuTemplate` it was made from, if it was; then `nf.on("menu_click")`. `event:cancel()` keeps it from moving anything. A locked window starts every click that would move items in or out already cancelled; `event:uncancel()` lets one through.
events.example:
this:on("click", function(event)
  if event.in_menu and event.index == 15 then
    event.player:close_menu()
    event:cancel()
  end
end)

events.name: drag
events.doc: Someone dragged a stack across slots of this window (spreading it out, or dropping one in each). Then the `MenuTemplate` it was made from (if it was) hears it. A locked window starts it already cancelled.

functions.name: id
functions.doc: This window's id: the menu's own id for a shared one, a fresh one for each window of a menu that isn't.

functions.name: kind
functions.doc: Which menu it is: its folder name under `menus/`. Nil once the window is gone, and for a window made from a `MenuTemplate` (see `template()`).

functions.name: template
functions.doc: The `MenuTemplate` this window was made from (`player:open_menu(template)`), or `nil` for a window of a menu file, and once the window or the template is gone.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether the window is still there. One that isn't shared goes when its last viewer closes it.

functions.name: is_shared
functions.doc: Whether this is the one window the whole server shares.

functions.name: context
functions.doc: What the script that opened this window passed along: `player:open_menu(menu, { context = value })`. The very value, not a copy, so a table can carry anything (the item being bought, a callback, the centity that was clicked). Every event on the window carries it too, as `event.context`. `nil` when nothing was passed, and always for a shared window, which nobody opens with a context.
functions.example:
-- opened with player:open_menu("shop", { context = { discount = 0.1 } })
local discount = (this:context() or {}).discount or 0

functions.name: size
functions.doc: How many slots it has. Slots are numbered from 0, left to right, then down.

functions.name: rows
functions.doc: How many rows of slots it has: a chest's 1 to 6, a hopper's 1, a dispenser's 3. `size() / rows()` is how many are in a row.

functions.name: title
functions.doc: The title, as MiniMessage, without the skin drawn in front of it.

functions.name: set_title
functions.doc: Renames the window. Minecraft can't rename a window that's open, so everyone looking sees it close and open again: fine between clicks, wrong every tick.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone.

functions.name: skin
functions.doc: The resource pack skin drawn behind it, as `<pack>/<key>`, or `nil` for the vanilla look.

functions.name: set_skin
functions.doc: Changes the background. A skin is drawn in the title, so this costs the same close-and-open `set_title` does. A skin the project's resource packs don't have is an error.

params.name: skin
params.doc: `<pack>/<key>`, or leave it out for the vanilla look.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone.

functions.example: this:set_skin("ui/shop_night")

functions.name: is_locked
functions.doc: Whether clicks are kept from moving items into or out of it: such a click reaches handlers already cancelled. Scripts hear the clicks either way.

functions.name: set_locked
functions.doc: Locks or unlocks this window. Not saved: a reload goes back to what the file says.

functions.name: slot
functions.doc: One of its slots, as a handle. A slot outside the window is an error. A handle is the window's id and the index, so it's fine to keep while the window lasts.

params.name: index
params.doc: From 0.

functions.example:
local buy = this:slot(13)
buy:set_item({ kind = "minecraft:emerald", name = "<green>Buy" })

functions.name: item
functions.doc: What is in a slot, or `nil` for an empty one. A slot outside the window is an error.

params.name: index
params.doc: From 0.

functions.name: set_item
functions.doc: Puts an item in a slot, replacing what was there, or empties it. An item table with a misspelled field, or an item id the server doesn't have, is an error.

params.name: index
params.doc: From 0.

params.name: item
params.doc: Leave it out (or `nil`) to empty the slot.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone.

functions.example:
local bread = this:item(11)
if bread then
  bread.count = bread.count - 1
  this:set_item(11, bread)
end

functions.name: add_item
functions.doc: Puts an item wherever it fits, topping up matching stacks first, the way picking something up does.

returns.doc: How many didn't fit: 0 when all of it went in.

functions.name: items
functions.doc: Every item in it, keyed by slot. Empty slots are left out, so `pairs` visits only what is there.
functions.example:
for index, item in pairs(this:items()) do
  log(index, item.kind, item.count)
end

functions.name: set_items
functions.doc: Puts several items in at once, by slot, replacing what was in those slots; the others are left alone. Every item is checked before any slot changes, so a mistake (a slot outside the window, a misspelled field, an item the server doesn't have) is an error that leaves the window as it was.

params.name: items
params.doc: Items by slot, from 0: `{ [11] = bread, [15] = cake }`.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone.

functions.name: fill
functions.doc: Puts a copy of one item in every empty slot, or in each of the listed slots (empty or not): a border of glass panes, say. A slot outside the window is an error.

params.name: indices
params.doc: The slots to fill, from 0. Leave it out for every empty one.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone.

functions.example: this:fill({ kind = "minecraft:gray_stained_glass_pane", hide_tooltip = true })

functions.name: clear
functions.doc: Empties every slot. To empty one, `set_item(index, nil)`.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone.

functions.name: viewers
functions.doc: Everyone looking at it now.

functions.name: cursor_item
functions.doc: What a viewer is carrying on their cursor while they have this window open, or `nil` for nothing (and when they aren't looking at it).

functions.name: set_cursor_item
functions.doc: Puts an item on a viewer's cursor, replacing what they were carrying, or empties it. What's on the cursor goes back to their inventory (or drops) when they close the window.

params.name: item
params.doc: Leave it out (or `nil`) to empty the cursor.

returns.doc: `false` when they aren't looking at this window or the window is gone.

functions.name: refresh
functions.doc: Sends the whole window to everyone looking at it again. Changes are sent by themselves, so this is only for when a viewer's screen may be out of step: after a cancelled click left a ghost item on it, say.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone.

functions.name: open_for
functions.doc: Shows this very window to someone too: a second pair of eyes on one menu. Its `open` handlers hear it. To give someone a window of their own, use `player:open_menu`.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline or the window is gone.

functions.name: close_for
functions.doc: Closes it for one viewer.

returns.doc: `false` when the window is gone or they weren't looking at it.

functions.name: close_all
functions.doc: Closes it for everyone looking at it.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `menu:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: Slot
classes.doc: One slot of one menu window, from `menu:slot(index)` (`this:slot(index)` in the menu's script). After the window goes, its methods return `nil` or `false` rather than erroring, and its handlers are gone.

events.name: click
events.doc: Someone clicked this slot. Then the menu hears it, then `nf.on("menu_click")`, unless a handler calls `event:stop()`.
events.example:
this:slot(13):on("click", function(event)
  event.player:send_message("<red>Sold out")
  event:cancel()
  event:stop()
end)

functions.name: index
functions.doc: Its number in the window, from 0.

functions.name: menu
functions.doc: The window it belongs to.

functions.name: item
functions.doc: What is in it, or `nil` when it's empty or the window is gone.

functions.name: set_item
functions.doc: Puts an item in it, replacing what was there, or empties it. An item table with a misspelled field, or an item id the server doesn't have, is an error.

params.name: item
params.doc: Leave it out (or `nil`) to empty the slot.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone.

functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

classes.name: MenuTemplate
classes.doc: A menu made by a script with `nf.menus.create` rather than read from `menus/<id>/`: what a window opened from it starts as. Open a window of it with `player:open_menu(template)`, as many as you like, each a `Menu` of its own; handlers on the template hear every one of its windows (after the window's own handlers). It lives as long as the script that created it: when that script unloads, or `remove()` is called, its windows close and its handlers go, and its methods answer `nil` or `false` rather than erroring.

events.name: open
events.doc: Someone opened a window made from this template: after the window's own `open` handlers, before `nf.on("menu_open")`.

events.name: close
events.doc: Someone closed a window made from this template, or left the server with it open: after the window's own `close` handlers, before `nf.on("menu_close")`.

events.name: click
events.doc: Someone clicked while a window made from this template was open: after the clicked slot's and the window's handlers, before `nf.on("menu_click")`. `event.menu` is the window, `event.index` the slot. A locked template's windows start every click that would move items already cancelled; `event:uncancel()` lets one through.
events.example:
template:on("click", function(event)
  if event.in_menu and event.index == 13 then
    event.player:send_message("<green>Bought!")
  end
end)

events.name: drag
events.doc: Someone dragged a stack across slots of a window made from this template: after the window's own `drag` handlers. A locked template's windows start it already cancelled.

functions.name: id
functions.doc: Its id, made up when it was created. It never names a folder under `menus/`, and it's only good while the template lasts.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether it's still there: until `remove()`, or until the script that created it unloads.

functions.name: size
functions.doc: How many slots its windows have.

functions.name: rows
functions.doc: How many rows of slots its windows have: a chest's 1 to 6, a hopper's 1, a dispenser's 3.

functions.name: title
functions.doc: The title its windows start with, as MiniMessage, without the skin.

functions.name: skin
functions.doc: The resource pack skin its windows start with, as `<pack>/<key>`, or `nil` for the vanilla look.

functions.name: is_locked
functions.doc: Whether its windows start locked: clicks that would move items into or out of them reach handlers already cancelled.

functions.name: item
functions.doc: What a slot of a new window starts with, or `nil` for an empty one. A slot outside its windows is an error.

params.name: index
params.doc: From 0.

functions.name: windows
functions.doc: Every window made from it that is still open.

functions.name: remove
functions.doc: Takes it away before its script unloads: its windows close, and its handlers go.

returns.doc: `false` when it was already gone.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.example:
local picker = nf.menus.create({ type = "hopper", title = "Pick one" })
picker:on("click", function(event)
  event.player:send_message("You picked slot " .. tostring(event.index))
end)

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `template:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: Dialog
classes.doc: A dialog from `dialogs/<id>/`: `this` in the dialog's script, and what `nf.dialogs.get` returns. A dialog holds nothing, so there is one of each for the whole server and showing it is all there is to do with it. Every button runs Lua with the answers to the inputs in hand; none of them is a command. Handlers on it last while the project has the dialog, across reloads of it. One made by `nf.dialogs.create` works the same way, and lasts as long as the script that made it.

events.name: press
events.doc: Someone pressed one of its buttons, with every input's answer in `event.values`: heard by the button first, then the dialog, then `nf.on("dialog_press")`. Escape on a notice is a press of its button, and on a confirmation a press of its second ("no") button.

events.name: close
events.doc: Someone left it without pressing one of its buttons: escape, or the exit button NetherForge gives a dialog (a `multi_action` dialog's "Back", a `dialog_list`'s own button, or the one standing in for a notice's or confirmation's missing button); or a script closed it (`player:close_dialog()`) or opened another dialog over it. Not when they leave the server (`player_quit` covers that), and not for escape on a notice or confirmation that has the button escape presses.

functions.name: id
functions.doc: Its folder name under `dialogs/`, or for one from `nf.dialogs.create`, an id made up for it.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether the project still has this dialog (a reload can take it away), or, for one from `nf.dialogs.create`, whether the script that made it is still running.

functions.name: title
functions.doc: Its title, as MiniMessage.

functions.name: buttons
functions.doc: The button keys, in the order they are drawn: what `event.key` can be.

functions.name: inputs
functions.doc: The input keys, in the order they are asked: the keys of `event.values`.

functions.name: button
functions.doc: One of its buttons, as a handle. A key the dialog has no button for is an error.

params.name: key
params.doc: The button's `key` in `dialog.json`.

functions.name: open_for
functions.doc: Puts it on someone's screen. It's built fresh each time, so what they see is the dialog as it is now, with whatever `options` change for this opening. A project dialog already on their screen is closed (its `close` handlers hear it).

params.name: options
params.doc: What to open it with, for this opening only. A key it doesn't take, an input or body element the dialog doesn't have, or a value of the wrong kind for its input is an error.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline or the dialog is gone.

functions.name: ask
functions.doc: Opens it for `player` and pauses the task until they answer: returns their press, or `nil` if they close it (see the `close` event: escape through NetherForge's exit button, or a script closing it or opening another dialog over it), leave the server, or it couldn't be opened (they're offline, or the dialog is gone). The press still goes to the dialog's handlers and `nf.on("dialog_press")` as usual; `ask` hears it at the dialog, so a button handler that calls `event:stop()` hides it from `ask` too.

params.name: options
params.doc: What to open it with, as for `open_for`.

functions.example:
nf.task(function()
  local answer = nf.dialogs.get("confirm"):ask(player)
  if answer and answer.key == "yes" then
    player:send_message("<green>Done.")
  end
end)

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

params.name: handler

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: Button
classes.doc: One button of a dialog, from `dialog:button(key)` (`this:button(key)` in the dialog's script). If a reload takes the button away, its methods return `nil` rather than erroring, and its handlers are gone.

events.name: press
events.doc: Someone pressed this button. Then the dialog hears it, then `nf.on("dialog_press")`, unless a handler calls `event:stop()`.

functions.name: key
functions.doc: Its `key` in `dialog.json`: what `event.key` is when it's pressed.

functions.name: dialog
functions.doc: The dialog it belongs to.

functions.name: label
functions.doc: What it says, as MiniMessage, or `nil` once the dialog no longer has it.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

params.name: event

params.name: handler

classes.name: ProjectItem
classes.doc: A project item from `items/<id>/item.json`: `this` in the item's script, and what `nf.items.get` hands out. It's the item itself, not one stack of it: its handlers hear what players do with any stack of it, wherever the stack came from. A stack of it is an `Item` table whose `item` is this id. If the item is deleted, its methods answer `nil` or `false` and its handlers go.

events.name: use
events.doc: A player right-clicked with a stack of this item in hand: `event.item` is the stack, `event.hand` which hand. Then the player's own `use_item`, then `nf.on("player_use_item")`, with the same event, so `event:cancel()` here cancels it for all of them and `event:stop()` keeps it from them. `event:cancel()` stops the item being used.

events.name: interact
events.doc: A player clicked a block or the air holding a stack of this item: `event.click` is `"left"` or `"right"`, `event.block` the block (`nil` for the air), `event.item` the stack. Then the player's own `interact`, then `nf.on("player_interact")`, with the same event, so `event:cancel()` here cancels it for all of them and `event:stop()` keeps it from them.

events.name: interact_entity
events.doc: A player right-clicked an entity (not a centity) holding a stack of this item in `event.hand`; read the stack with `event.player:held_item()` (or `off_hand_item()`). The entity's own `interact` handlers hear it first, then this item's. Then the player's own `interact_entity`, then `nf.on("player_interact_entity")`, with the same event, so `event:cancel()` here cancels it for all of them and `event:stop()` keeps it from them.

events.name: consume
events.doc: A player finished eating or drinking a stack of this item (`event.item`). Then the player's own `consume_item`, then `nf.on("player_consume_item")`, with the same event, so `event:cancel()` here cancels it for all of them and `event:stop()` keeps it from them.

events.name: hit
events.doc: A player is attacking an entity with a stack of this item in their main hand: `event.attacker` is the player, `event.entity` who is hit, `event.amount` the damage (writable). Read the stack with `event.attacker:held_item()`. Then the entity's own `damage`, then `nf.on("entity_damage")`, with the same event.

events.name: break_block
events.doc: A player is breaking a block with a stack of this item in their main hand (read it with `event.player:held_item()`). Then the world's own `block_break`, then `nf.on("block_break")`, with the same event; assign `event.drops` and `event.experience` to change what it drops.

events.name: drop
events.doc: A player is dropping a stack of this item (`event.item`). Then the player's own `drop_item`, then `nf.on("player_drop_item")`, with the same event, so `event:cancel()` here cancels it for all of them and `event:stop()` keeps it from them.

events.name: pickup
events.doc: A player is picking up a stack of this item (`event.item`) from the item entity `event.entity`. Then the player's own `pickup_item`, then `nf.on("player_pickup_item")`, with the same event, so `event:cancel()` here cancels it for all of them and `event:stop()` keeps it from them.

functions.name: id
functions.doc: Its id: its folder name under `items/`.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether the project still has it.

functions.name: create
functions.doc: A stack of it, as an `Item` table: the same as `nf.items.create(this:id(), overrides)`. `nil` once the item is gone.

params.name: overrides
params.doc: `Item` fields for this stack: `{ count = 3, data = { found = "cave" } }`. A field the item's file sets is replaced only until the file changes (see `nf.items.create`).

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.
