params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `item:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: Effect
classes.doc: One playing particle effect, from `nf.particles.play`. Once it has ended (it finished, was stopped, lost what it followed, its file was deleted, or the script that played it unloaded) its methods answer `nil` or `false` rather than erroring, except `kind()`. An effect is ephemeral: it has no `id()` and can't be saved in a `data()` table.

events.name: end
events.doc: The effect ended, for any reason (`event.reason` says which): heard once, while the handle still answers (`is_active()` is still true and `location()` says where it was; `stop()` is `false`, as it's already ending), so `nf.wait_for(effect, "end")` hands back the event. After it, the effect is gone and so is every handler on it. A looping effect never ends `"finished"`.
events.example:
effect:on("end", function(event)
  if event.reason == "target_gone" then
    log("they left before it was over")
  end
end)

functions.name: kind
functions.doc: Which effect it is: its folder name under `particles/`, even after it has ended.

functions.name: is_active
functions.doc: Whether it's still playing. `false` once it has ended, for any reason (its `end` handlers still see `true`).

functions.name: stop
functions.doc: Ends it now, with reason `"stopped"`. Particles already spawned live out their short lives on the players' screens.

returns.doc: `false` when it had already ended.

functions.name: location
functions.doc: Where it is now, facing the way it faces: in world space. `nil` once it has ended.

functions.name: teleport
functions.doc: Moves it, and stops it following anything. A `Location`'s `yaw` and `pitch` become its facing (nil is 0); a `Vec3` keeps its world and its facing.

params.name: location_or_position
params.doc: Where to, in world space.

returns.doc: `false` once it has ended.

functions.name: follow
functions.doc: Makes it follow something, from the next tick on. Each tick, before it spawns anything, the effect moves to the target: its position (a node's `world_position()`), facing the target's yaw (a node's centity's), pitch 0. When the target stops existing (a removed centity, a player who left, an entity that died or was removed, a centity or entity whose chunk unloaded) the effect ends with reason `"target_gone"`. Calling it again switches targets; `teleport` stops following.

params.name: target
params.doc: What to follow.

params.name: offset
params.doc: Where the effect sits from the target, in the effect's own space (turned with the target's yaw): `vec3(0, 2, 0)` is above its head, `vec3(0, 0, 1)` in front. Default `vec3.zero`.

returns.doc: `false` once it has ended.

functions.example:
local here = player:location()
local halo = here and nf.particles.play("halo", here, { loop = true })
if halo then
  halo:follow(player, vec3(0, 2.2, 0))
end

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.example:
local here = this:location()
local effect = here and nf.particles.play("sparkle", here)
if effect then
  effect:on("end", function(event)
    log("sparkle ended:", event.reason)
  end)
end

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `effect:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: Cutscene
classes.doc: One cutscene playing for one player, from `nf.cutscenes.play`. Once it has ended (it finished, was stopped or skipped, was replaced by another, its player left, or the script that played it unloaded) its methods answer `nil` or `false` rather than erroring, except `kind()` and `length()`. A cutscene is ephemeral: it has no `id()` and can't be saved in a `data()` table.

events.name: end
events.doc: The cutscene ended, for any reason (`event.reason` says which): heard once, after the player has been put back (so a handler that moves them or changes their game mode has the last word), while the handle still answers (`is_active()` is still true; `stop()` is `false`, as it is already ending), so `nf.wait_for(cutscene, "end")` hands back the event. After it, the cutscene is gone and so is every handler on it. When the player left, `event.player` is them offline.
events.example:
local scene = nf.cutscenes.play(player, "intro")
if scene then
  scene:on("end", function(event)
    if event.reason == "skipped" then
      event.player:send_message("<gray>You skipped the intro.")
    end
  end)
end

events.name: cue
events.doc: The cutscene reached a cue that names an `event` (`cues` in its file), at that time.
events.example:
local scene = nf.cutscenes.play(player, "intro")
if scene then
  scene:on("cue", function(event)
    if event.cue == "boom" then
      event.player:play_sound("minecraft:entity.generic.explode")
    end
  end)
end

functions.name: kind
functions.doc: Which cutscene it is: its file name under `cutscenes/`, even after it has ended.

functions.name: length
functions.doc: How long it lasts, in seconds, even after it has ended.

functions.name: player
functions.doc: Who is watching. `nil` once it has ended.

functions.name: is_active
functions.doc: Whether it's still playing. `false` once it has ended, for any reason (its `end` handlers still see `true`).

functions.name: time
functions.doc: Seconds played so far. `nil` once it has ended.

functions.name: stop
functions.doc: Ends it now, with reason `"stopped"`, and puts the player back.

returns.doc: `false` when it had already ended.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.example:
local intro = nf.cutscenes.play(player, "intro")
if intro then
  intro:on("end", function(event)
    log("intro ended:", event.reason)
  end)
end

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `cutscene:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: File
classes.doc: A path in the scripts' data directory (`plugins/NetherForge/data/`, on the editor's dev server too). The only state a script has that survives a restart. Files are capped at 1 MiB; writes past it are refused, not truncated.

functions.name: path
functions.doc: The path from the data directory; `""` for the directory itself.

functions.name: name
functions.doc: The last part of the path.

functions.name: parent
functions.doc: The folder it's in, or `nil` for the data directory itself.

functions.name: child
functions.doc: Something inside this folder, whether or not it exists yet. `nil` for a name that isn't allowed.

params.name: name
params.doc: One name, no `/`.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether anything is there.

functions.name: is_folder
functions.doc: Whether it's a folder.

functions.name: size
functions.doc: Its size in bytes, or `nil` when it isn't a file.

functions.name: children
functions.doc: What's directly inside, sorted by name; empty for a file or nothing.

functions.name: read
functions.doc: The contents, or `nil` when there's no file.

functions.name: write
functions.doc: Replaces the contents, creating folders above it as needed.

returns.doc: `false` for a folder, past the size cap, or on a disk error.

functions.name: append
functions.doc: Adds to the end.

functions.name: read_json
functions.doc: The contents parsed as JSON, as `nf.json.decode` does, or `nil` when there's no file or it isn't JSON.

functions.name: write_json
functions.doc: Writes a value as JSON, as `nf.json.encode` does.

returns.doc: `false` for something JSON can't hold (a function, a table inside itself) or a failed write.

functions.name: modified_time
functions.doc: When it last changed, as Unix time in milliseconds (like `nf.server.unix_time()`), or `nil` when there's nothing there.

functions.name: lines
functions.doc: An iterator over its lines, for a `for` loop: each without its line ending (`\n` or `\r\n`). Nothing for a file that isn't there.
functions.example:
for line in nf.files.get("motd.txt"):lines() do
  player:send_message(line)
end

functions.name: rename
functions.doc: Moves it (a file, or a folder and everything in it) to another path in the data directory, creating folders above it as needed. Nothing already there is overwritten.

params.name: path
params.doc: From the data directory, as `nf.files.get` takes it.

returns.doc: It at its new path; `nil` when there's nothing to move, the path isn't allowed or is taken, or the move failed.

functions.example: assert(nf.files.get("scores.json")):rename("backups/scores-1.json")

functions.name: copy_to
functions.doc: Copies a file to another path in the data directory, creating folders above it as needed. Nothing already there is overwritten. Folders can't be copied.

params.name: path
params.doc: From the data directory, as `nf.files.get` takes it.

returns.doc: The copy; `nil` when it isn't a file, the path isn't allowed or is taken, or the copy failed.

functions.name: create_folder
functions.doc: Creates the folder, and any above it.

functions.name: delete
functions.doc: Deletes a file or an empty folder.

classes.name: Subscription
classes.doc: What `:on` and `:once` return: one handler listening for one event on one handle (or on `nf`). A handler lives as long as **both** the script that registered it and the handle it's on: a module's handler on a centity's node goes when the module unloads or the centity is removed, whichever comes first; one on a menu window goes with the window. A handler that errors 20 times in a row is cancelled.

functions.name: cancel
functions.doc: Stops the handler being called. Cancelling one already cancelled does nothing.

functions.name: is_active
functions.doc: Whether the handler is still listening: `false` once it's cancelled (by `cancel()`, after a `once` handler ran, or after 20 errors in a row), its script has unloaded, or the handle it's on has gone.

classes.name: Task
classes.doc: What `nf.task`, `nf.after` and `nf.every` return: a task that may be waiting, or a callback waiting to run.

functions.name: cancel
functions.doc: Ends it: a task stops where it's waiting and never carries on; a callback doesn't run (again). A task that cancels itself stops at its next wait. Cancelling one that has ended does nothing.

functions.name: is_active
functions.doc: Whether it will still run: `false` once it's cancelled, once a task has finished, errored or lost the handle it was waiting on, once an `nf.after` callback has run, after an `nf.every` callback's 20th error in a row, or once its script has unloaded.

classes.name: Schedule
classes.doc: What `nf.schedule.daily`, `weekly` and `cron` return: a schedule that will run at its next time, until it is cancelled or its script unloads.

functions.name: cancel
functions.doc: Ends it: it doesn't run again. What it last ran is kept, so a schedule made again with the same `id` doesn't catch up a run it already made. Cancelling one that has ended does nothing.

functions.name: is_active
functions.doc: Whether it will still run: `false` once it's cancelled or its script has unloaded.

functions.name: next_run
functions.doc: When it runs next, as Unix time in milliseconds (like `nf.server.unix_time()`; `nf.time.format` writes it as a date). `nil` once it has ended.

classes.name: Random
classes.doc: A random generator from `nf.random.new`: numbers that repeat for its seed, apart from `math.random` and every other generator.

functions.name: integer
functions.doc: A whole number from `min` to `max`, both included, each as likely as the others. `min` greater than `max` is an error.

functions.name: number
functions.doc: A number from 0 up to (not including) 1, or from `min` up to `max`.

params.name: min
params.doc: Give both or neither.

functions.name: pick
functions.doc: One item of a list, each as likely as the others. `nil` for an empty list.

params.name: list
params.doc: A list, numbered from 1.

functions.example: local greeting = rng:pick({ "Hello", "Welcome back", "Hi there" })

functions.name: shuffle
functions.doc: Puts a list in a random order, in place.

params.name: list
params.doc: A list, numbered from 1.

functions.name: weighted
functions.doc: One key of a table, picked with odds in proportion to its number: in `{ common = 3, rare = 1 }`, `"common"` comes up three times in four. Keys with weight 0 never come up; `nil` when there are none with more. A weight that is negative or not a number is an error. The same seed picks the same keys when the keys are strings, numbers or booleans.

params.name: weights
params.doc: Each choice, with its weight.

functions.example: local kind = rng:weighted({ ["minecraft:diamond"] = 1, ["minecraft:iron_ingot"] = 9 })

values.name: Vec3
values.doc: Three numbers: a position, an offset, a velocity, a direction or a scale. Every place the API takes or gives one of those, it's a `Vec3`. Build one with `vec3(x, y, z)`. Vectors are immutable: methods and operators return a new vector, and assigning to `v.x` is an error. `a == b` compares the numbers exactly, and `tostring(v)` is `"vec3(1, 2, 3)"`.

fields.name: x
fields.doc: East (+) and west (−).

fields.name: y
fields.doc: Up (+) and down (−).

fields.name: z
fields.doc: South (+) and north (−).

operators.doc: `a * b`: component by component, for scales.

functions.name: length
functions.doc: How long it is.

functions.name: length_squared
functions.doc: Its length squared: cheaper than `length()`, and enough for comparing distances.

functions.name: normalized
functions.doc: The same direction with length 1. The zero vector stays zero rather than becoming NaN.

functions.name: dot
functions.doc: The dot product.

functions.name: cross
functions.doc: The cross product: a vector at right angles to both, by the right-hand rule.

functions.name: distance
functions.doc: How far it is to another point.

functions.name: distance_squared
functions.doc: The distance squared: cheaper than `distance()`, and enough for comparing.

functions.name: lerp
functions.doc: The point `fraction` of the way to `other`: 0 is this vector, 1 is `other`.

params.name: fraction
params.doc: Usually 0 to 1; outside that it carries on past either end.

functions.name: flat
functions.doc: A copy with `y` set to 0: the horizontal part.
functions.example: local toward = (target - player:position()):flat():normalized()

functions.name: with_x
functions.doc: A copy with `x` replaced.

functions.name: with_y
functions.doc: A copy with `y` replaced.

functions.name: with_z
functions.doc: A copy with `z` replaced.

functions.name: floor
functions.doc: Each component rounded down: the block a position is in.

functions.name: round
functions.doc: Each component rounded to the nearest whole number, halves up.

functions.name: rotated
functions.doc: Turned about an axis through the origin, by the right-hand rule: with your right thumb along the axis, positive degrees turn the way your fingers curl. About `vec3.up`, 90 degrees turns east into north.

params.name: axis
params.doc: Any length but zero.

functions.example: local left = forward:rotated(vec3.up, 90)

functions.name: unpack
functions.doc: The three numbers, for code that wants them separately.

returns.doc: x
y
z

functions.example: local x, y, z = v:unpack()

library.name: vec3
library.doc: Builds vectors (`vec3(x, y, z)`), and holds the common ones and `vec3.from_yaw_pitch`.

functions.name: from_yaw_pitch
functions.doc: The unit direction a yaw and pitch face, in Minecraft's convention: yaw 0 faces south (+z), 90 west (−x), 180 north, −90 east; pitch −90 is straight up, 90 straight down.

params.name: yaw
params.doc: Degrees.

params.name: pitch
params.doc: Degrees.

functions.example: local ahead = vec3.from_yaw_pitch(player:yaw() or 0, 0) * 2

values.name: Location
values.doc: A position in a particular world, with an optional facing. Immutable, like `Vec3`. What `location()` returns on a player or a centity; build one with `world:location(position, yaw?, pitch?)`. Methods that place things (`teleport`, `nf.centities.spawn`) take a `Location`, or a bare `Vec3` meaning "in the same world". `a == b` when every field is equal.

fields.name: world
fields.doc: Which world.

fields.name: position
fields.doc: Where in the world.

fields.name: yaw
fields.doc: Which way it faces horizontally, in degrees (0 south, 90 west), or `nil` for a location with no facing.

fields.name: pitch
fields.doc: How far up or down it faces, in degrees (−90 up, 90 down), or `nil` for a location with no facing.

functions.name: with_position
functions.doc: A copy somewhere else in the same world, keeping the facing.

functions.name: offset
functions.doc: A copy moved by an offset, keeping the facing.
functions.example: player:teleport(player:location():offset(vec3(0, 10, 0)))

functions.name: direction
functions.doc: The unit direction it faces (`vec3.from_yaw_pitch`, a missing pitch counting as level), or `nil` when it has no facing.

aliases.name: Text
aliases.doc: MiniMessage a player reads, like `"<green>Done!"`: a string. A `<glyph:pack/key>` tag in it names a glyph the way the script's own files would: one of its own package's resource packs bare, or `<glyph:namespace:pack/key>` for one a package it depends on exports. The tag means that glyph wherever and whenever the text is shown, whoever shows it; one naming a glyph the script can't use draws nothing, and the server log says why. Text handed back to a script names its glyphs the same way.

surfaces.name: centity
surfaces.doc: A centity's script (`centities/<id>/*.lua`, named by `script` in `centity.json`). One copy runs per spawned instance, with its own globals; `this` is the instance. The script's body runs every time it starts (spawning, a restart, a reload): that's where it sets up its nodes and registers its handlers, with `this:on(...)` and `this:node(name):on(...)`.

globals.name: this
globals.doc: The centity instance this script runs on.

surfaces.name: module
surfaces.doc: A module's files (`modules/<id>/**/*.lua`). `init.lua` runs when the server loads the module; other files run when something requires them. All of a module's files share one set of globals. Modules listen with `nf.on` (and `:on` on any handle they hold) and add commands with `nf.commands.register`.

surfaces.name: menu
surfaces.doc: A menu's script (`menus/<id>/*.lua`, named by `script` in `menu.json`). Every window gets its own copy, with its own globals, started when the window is made: when it's opened for someone, or at load for a `shared` one. The body runs before anyone sees the window, so it's where to fill it in and register handlers (`this:on("click", ...)`, `this:slot(13):on("click", ...)`). Its handlers go with the window.

globals.name: this
globals.doc: The window this script runs for.

surfaces.name: dialog
surfaces.doc: A dialog's script (`dialogs/<id>/*.lua`, named by `script` in `dialog.json`). There's one of each dialog, so its script runs once, from load until the dialog is reloaded. Its body registers handlers: `this:on("press", ...)`, `this:button(key):on("press", ...)`, `this:on("close", ...)`.

globals.name: this
globals.doc: The dialog this script belongs to.

surfaces.name: item
surfaces.doc: A project item's script (`items/<id>/*.lua`, named by `script` in `item.json`). There's one of each item, so its script runs once (not once per stack), from load until the item is reloaded. Its body registers handlers for what players do with any stack of the item: `this:on("use", ...)`, `this:on("hit", ...)`, `this:on("pickup", ...)`.

globals.name: this
globals.doc: The project item this script belongs to.

surfaces.name: block
surfaces.doc: A project block's script (`blocks/<id>/*.lua`, named by `script` in `block.json`). There's one of each block, so its script runs once (not once per placed block), from load until the block is reloaded. Its body registers handlers for what players do with any block of it: `this:on("click", ...)`, `this:on("break", ...)`, `this:on("tick", ...)`.

globals.name: this
globals.doc: The project block this script belongs to.

shapes.name: Event
shapes.doc: What every event handler receives: a table with the event's own fields (its payload, named `<Something>Event` in this reference) and these. What a handler returns means nothing; it changes what happens through `stop`, `cancel` and the event's writable fields. A field the event doesn't list as writable can't be assigned.

functions.name: stop
functions.doc: No later handler hears it: none further along its path (a parent node, the centity, `nf`), and none after this one on the same handle.

functions.name: cancel
functions.doc: Cancels what caused it: the click doesn't move an item, the block isn't broken. Only for cancellable events; on any other, it's an error. A later handler can still `uncancel()`.

functions.name: uncancel
functions.doc: Undoes an earlier handler's `cancel()`, or a locked menu's.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The event's name where the handler is listening: `"click"` on a node, `"centity_click"` on `nf`.

fields.name: current
fields.doc: The handle whose handler is running (the node, centity, slot, menu, button or dialog), or `nil` in an `nf.on` handler. As an event bubbles it changes; `target` stays what was hit.

fields.name: cancelled
fields.doc: Whether what caused it will be cancelled, as things stand. Read-only: use `cancel()` and `uncancel()`.

fields.name: stopped
fields.doc: Whether a handler called `stop()`. Read-only.

shapes.name: EventOptions
shapes.doc: How `:on` listens. Every key is optional, and each applies only to the events that say so: a key that isn't one of these, or one the event doesn't take, is an error.

fields.name: every
fields.doc: For `tick`: run every this many ticks instead of every tick (at least 1). `every = 20` is once a second.

shapes.name: SettingChangedEvent
shapes.doc: One of the package's settings changed.

fields.name: setting
fields.doc: The setting's name, as `netherforge.json` declares it.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: What it is now, as `nf.config` gives it.

fields.name: previous
fields.doc: What it was.

shapes.name: TickEvent
shapes.doc: A server tick went by.

fields.name: tick
fields.doc: The server tick it is, the same as `nf.server.tick()`.

shapes.name: ClickEvent
shapes.doc: A player clicked a centity's hitbox. Heard by the clicked node, then each node above it, then the centity, then `nf.on("centity_click")`.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: target
fields.doc: The node whose hitbox was clicked. `event.current` is the node or centity whose handler is running.

fields.name: click
fields.doc: Which kind of click: the left (attack) or right (use) button.

fields.name: hit_position
fields.doc: Where the player's line of sight met the hitbox, as a world position: what `node:apply_impulse_at` takes. `nil` when the server couldn't tell.

fields.name: hit_normal
fields.doc: The unit direction straight out of the face that was hit, in world space. `nil` when the server couldn't tell.

shapes.name: CentityEvent
shapes.doc: Something happened to a centity instance as a whole.

fields.name: centity
fields.doc: The instance.

shapes.name: CentityNaturalSpawnEvent
shapes.doc: A centity is about to appear by itself, from its `spawning` rules, near a player.

fields.name: centity
fields.doc: Which centity, as the project names it: its folder name under `centities/` (`wisp`), or `acme:wisp` for one a package brings.

fields.name: location
fields.doc: Where it will stand, facing included (its yaw is the way the centity turns). Writable: assign another `Location` to put it somewhere else, in any world the server has; the spawner does not check its rules again there.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: The player it is appearing near.

shapes.name: AnimationEvent
shapes.doc: One of a centity's animations started or ended.

fields.name: centity
fields.doc: The instance.

fields.name: animation
fields.doc: The animation's name.

shapes.name: NodeEvent
shapes.doc: Something happened to a node's physics body.

fields.name: node
fields.doc: The node.

shapes.name: CollideEvent
shapes.doc: A physics body started touching something it wasn't touching the tick before: the moment of impact, not every tick while it rests there.

fields.name: node
fields.doc: The body that hit something.

fields.name: other
fields.doc: The other body when it was one of the same centity's, or `nil` for a block or another centity's hitbox.

fields.name: hit_position
fields.doc: Where they touched, as a world position.

fields.name: hit_normal
fields.doc: The unit direction from what it hit towards the body, in world space.

fields.name: speed
fields.doc: How fast they were closing, in blocks per second: small for a touch, large for a crash. Handy for how loud a sound should be.

shapes.name: PlayerJoinEvent
shapes.doc: A player joined the server.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: first_join
fields.doc: Whether they have never played here before.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: The join message everyone sees, as MiniMessage. Writable: assign another, or `nil` for none.

shapes.name: PlayerQuitEvent
shapes.doc: A player left the server.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: The leave message everyone sees, as MiniMessage. Writable: assign another, or `nil` for none.

shapes.name: PlayerChatEvent
shapes.doc: A player is saying something in chat.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: What they said, as plain text: never MiniMessage, so it can be shown as it is. Writable: assign other text to change what everyone sees.

fields.name: format
fields.doc: How the line is shown, as MiniMessage, where `<player>` is the player's display name and `<message>` what they said (both shown as they are, never read as tags). Starts as Minecraft's own look, `"\\<<player>> <message>"`. Writable: assign another, like `"<gray><player>: <white><message>"`.

shapes.name: PlayerInteractEvent
shapes.doc: A player clicked a block or the air with one hand. The game asks for each hand in turn, so one right click can arrive twice: once for the main hand and, unless that did something, once for the off hand.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: click
fields.doc: Which kind of click: the left (attack) or right (use) button.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: The block, or `nil` for a click on the air.

fields.name: face
fields.doc: Which face of the block was clicked, or `nil` for a click on the air.

fields.name: item
fields.doc: What's in the hand the click was with, or `nil` for an empty hand.

fields.name: hand
fields.doc: Which hand: the game asks for each hand in turn.

shapes.name: BlockBreakEvent
shapes.doc: A player is breaking a block: heard by its world, then `nf.on("block_break")`.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: The block. A handle reads the world live, so what it says depends on when you ask: `state` is what it was when this happened.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: Its whole block state as it was being broken, like `"minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=bottom,shape=straight,waterlogged=false]"`.

fields.name: drops
fields.doc: What it will drop, for the tool they're breaking it with: an empty list for nothing. Writable: assign another list of items (or change this one) to drop those instead.

fields.name: experience

shapes.name: PlayerEvent

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

shapes.name: PlayerMoveEvent

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: from
fields.doc: Where they were, facing included: in the block they are leaving.

fields.name: to
fields.doc: Where they are going, facing included: in another block from `from`.

shapes.name: PlayerTeleportEvent

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: from
fields.doc: Where they are, facing included.

fields.name: to
fields.doc: Where they are going, facing included. Writable: assign another `Location` to send them there instead (a world the server doesn't have leaves it as it was).

fields.name: cause
fields.doc: Why, as Minecraft names it: `"command"`, `"plugin"` (a plugin or a script), `"ender_pearl"`, `"chorus_fruit"`, `"nether_portal"`, `"end_portal"`, `"end_gateway"`, `"spectate"`, `"dismount"`, `"exit_bed"`, `"unknown"`, …

shapes.name: PlayerChangeWorldEvent
shapes.doc: A player went from one world to another.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: from
fields.doc: The world they left.

fields.name: to
fields.doc: The world they are in now.

shapes.name: PlayerDeathEvent

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: killer
fields.doc: Who killed them, when someone did.

fields.doc: The death message everyone sees, as MiniMessage. Writable: assign another, or `nil` for none.

fields.name: keep_inventory
fields.doc: Whether they keep what they carry. Writable: `true` keeps their inventory, and then nothing from it drops (unless `drops` is assigned too).

fields.name: drops
fields.doc: What they drop where they died. Writable: assign another list of items (or change this one) to drop those instead.

shapes.name: PlayerRespawnEvent
shapes.doc: A player is coming back after dying (or leaving the end).

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: location
fields.doc: Where they will appear: their bed, respawn anchor or the world's spawn. Writable: assign another `Location` to bring them back there (a world the server doesn't have leaves it as it was).

shapes.name: PlayerItemEvent

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: item

shapes.name: PlayerPickupItemEvent

fields.name: player

fields.name: item

shapes.name: PlayerUseItemEvent

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: item

fields.name: hand

shapes.name: PlayerSneakEvent
shapes.doc: A player started or stopped sneaking.

fields.name: player

fields.name: sneaking

shapes.name: PlayerCommandEvent
shapes.doc: A player typed a command.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: input

shapes.name: CentityFilter
shapes.doc: Which centities `nf.centities.all` lists. Every key is optional; an instance is listed when it matches all of those given. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: world

fields.name: near

fields.name: shooter

shapes.name: ProjectileHitEvent
shapes.doc: A projectile hit something.

fields.name: projectile
fields.doc: The projectile.

fields.name: shooter
fields.doc: Who launched it, when someone did.

fields.name: entity
fields.doc: The entity it hit, or `nil` for a block.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: The block it hit, or `nil` for an entity.

fields.name: face
fields.doc: Which face of the block it hit, or `nil` for an entity.

shapes.name: EntityShootBowEvent

fields.name: entity
fields.doc: Who shot it.

fields.name: bow
fields.doc: The bow or crossbow, or `nil` for a mob without one.

fields.name: projectile
fields.doc: What it shot: an arrow, or a firework from a crossbow. Its methods already work.

fields.name: force
fields.doc: How far the bow was drawn, 0 to 1 (always 1 for a crossbow).

fields.name: hand
fields.doc: Which hand.

shapes.name: EntityTargetEvent

fields.name: entity
fields.doc: The mob.

fields.name: target
fields.doc: What it's going after, or `nil` when it's forgetting its target.

fields.name: cause
fields.doc: Why, as Minecraft names it: `"closest_player"`, `"target_attacked_entity"`, `"target_attacked_nearby_entity"`, `"forgot_target"`, `"target_died"`, `"temptation"`, `"custom"` (a plugin or a script), …

shapes.name: ExplodeEvent
shapes.doc: Something exploded: an entity (`entity_explode`) or a block (`block_explode`).

fields.name: entity
fields.doc: What exploded, for `entity_explode`; `nil` for a block.

fields.name: block

fields.doc: Where it exploded.

fields.name: blocks
fields.doc: The blocks it will break, as their handles: read them to see what would go.

fields.name: breaks_blocks
fields.doc: Whether `blocks` will break. Writable: `false` keeps every block standing, but the explosion still hurts and pushes what is near.

fields.name: yield
fields.doc: The chance each broken block drops as an item, 0 to 1. Writable: assign another (1 drops everything).

shapes.name: EntityCombustEvent

fields.name: block
fields.doc: The block that set it alight (fire, lava), when one did.

shapes.name: EntityChangeEffectEvent

fields.name: from

fields.name: to

fields.name: block
fields.doc: The block.

fields.name: cause

fields.name: player

fields.name: source

fields.name: entity

shapes.name: BlockFlowEvent

fields.name: block
fields.doc: Where it flows from.

fields.name: to

fields.name: face

shapes.name: PistonEvent

fields.name: blocks

shapes.name: BlockRedstoneEvent
shapes.doc: A block's redstone power is changing.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: The block.

fields.name: from

fields.name: to

shapes.name: SignChangeEvent

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: The block.

fields.name: side

fields.name: lines

shapes.name: BlockStartBreakEvent
shapes.doc: A player started hitting a block.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: The block.

fields.name: item
fields.doc: What they're hitting it with, or `nil` for a bare hand.

fields.name: instant

shapes.name: BlockDropItemEvent

fields.name: player

fields.name: block

fields.name: items

fields.name: cause

shapes.name: ThunderChangeEvent

fields.name: world

fields.name: thundering

fields.name: cause
fields.doc: Why, as Minecraft names it: `"natural"`, `"command"`, `"sleep"`, `"plugin"` (a plugin or a script), `"unknown"`.

fields.name: world

fields.name: entity

fields.name: cause
fields.doc: Why, as Minecraft names it: `"weather"`, `"trident"`, `"command"`, `"spawner"` (a skeleton horse trap), `"custom"` (a plugin or a script), `"unknown"`.

fields.name: z

shapes.name: ChunkLoadEvent

fields.name: world
fields.doc: The world.

fields.name: x

fields.name: z

shapes.name: WorldEvent

fields.name: amount

shapes.name: PlayerPrepareGrindstoneEvent

fields.name: top

fields.name: bottom

fields.name: result
fields.doc: What the result slot shows, or `nil` for nothing. Writable: assign another item to make that the result, or `nil` for none.

fields.name: player

fields.name: flying
