shapes.name: CentityPathOptions
shapes.doc: How a centity walks where `centity:move_to` sends it. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: speed
fields.doc: How fast, in blocks a second: more than 0, at most 20. Default 4.3, a player's walk.

fields.name: fly
fields.doc: Flies there, through the air in any direction, rather than walking on the ground: no steps, drops or falling. Finding a way costs the server more. Default false.

fields.name: face
fields.doc: Turns it to face the way it goes, about its feet, a little each tick. Default true.

fields.name: width
fields.doc: How wide a gap it needs, in blocks: more than 0, at most 8. Default: its hitboxes' wider side, as they're placed when it sets off (1 without hitboxes). It's taken as square, whichever way it faces.

fields.name: height
fields.doc: How tall a gap it needs, in blocks: more than 0, at most 16. Default: its hitboxes' height (1 without hitboxes).

fields.name: step_height
fields.doc: Walking: how high a step it goes straight up, in blocks: at least 0. Default 1, a block, as a mob jumps one.

fields.name: max_drop
fields.doc: Walking: how far down it will drop off an edge, in blocks: at least 0. Default 3.

fields.name: range
fields.doc: How far from where it sets off it looks for a way, in blocks: more than 0, at most 128. A target further away than this is `false`. Default 48. One search looks at no more than 4096 places, so a long way round may only take it part of the way.

shapes.name: CentityPathEndEvent
shapes.doc: A centity stopped walking where `move_to` sent it.

fields.name: centity
fields.doc: The instance.

fields.name: reached
fields.doc: Whether it got there: to the end of its path, within 2 blocks of where it was sent (or of what it went after, which it stops short of); `false` when it gave up.

shapes.name: AnimationOptions
shapes.doc: How `centity:play_animation` plays an animation this time. The file says how it plays by default.

fields.name: speed
fields.doc: 1 is as authored (the default), 2 twice as fast, 0.5 half. Not negative.

fields.name: from_tick
fields.doc: Where in the clip to start, in ticks from its beginning. Default 0.

fields.name: loop
fields.doc: `true` loops it whatever its file says; `false` plays it through once (a `hold` clip still holds its last pose). Default: the file's `loop`.

fields.name: blend_ticks
fields.doc: Eases from the pose the nodes have now into the animation over this many ticks, instead of jumping to its first frame. Default 0.

shapes.name: TextStyle
shapes.doc: How a text display draws its text: what `node:display_text_style()` gives and `node:set_display_text_style` takes. Every field is optional; one left out is its default.

fields.name: background
fields.doc: `#AARRGGBB`, alpha first: `"#00000000"` is none at all. Default: Minecraft's translucent grey.

fields.name: opacity
fields.doc: The text's own opacity, 0 to 255. Default 255.

fields.name: shadow
fields.doc: A drop shadow under the text. Default false.

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc: How lines of different lengths line up. Default `"center"`.

fields.name: line_width
fields.doc: How wide a line gets, in pixels, before it wraps. Default 200.

fields.name: see_through
fields.doc: Drawn through blocks in front of it. Default false.

shapes.name: Brightness
shapes.doc: Fixed light levels a display is drawn with: `node:set_brightness`.

fields.name: block_light
fields.doc: Light from blocks (torches, lamps), 0 to 15. Required.

fields.name: sky_light
fields.doc: Light from the sky, 0 to 15. Required.

shapes.name: EntityFilter
shapes.doc: Which entities `world:entities` lists. Every key is optional; an entity is listed when it matches all of those given. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: Only this kind: `"minecraft:zombie"`.

fields.name: tag
fields.doc: Only entities with this scoreboard tag.

fields.name: near
fields.doc: Only entities within `radius` of this point. Needs `radius`.

fields.name: radius
fields.doc: How far from `near`, in blocks. Needs `near`.

fields.name: living
fields.doc: `true`: only living entities (mobs, animals, players); `false`: only the rest.

shapes.name: EntitySpawnOptions
shapes.doc: How `world:spawn_entity` sets up what it spawns, before anything (an `entity_spawn` handler included) sees it. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: custom_name
fields.doc: Its custom name, MiniMessage.

fields.name: tags
fields.doc: Scoreboard tags to give it.

fields.name: data
fields.doc: A table its `data()` table starts with: the same values a `data()` table may hold. Something that can't be saved is an error.

fields.name: velocity
fields.doc: How fast it starts moving, in blocks per tick.

shapes.name: EffectOptions
shapes.doc: How a status effect is given. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: amplifier
fields.doc: Its strength above the first: 0 is speed I, 1 speed II. Default 0.

fields.name: ambient
fields.doc: Fainter particles, as from a beacon. Default `false`.

fields.name: particles
fields.doc: Whether it shows particles. Default `true`.

fields.name: icon
fields.doc: Whether it shows an icon on their screen. Default `true`.

shapes.name: StatusEffect
shapes.doc: One status effect on a living entity: what `living:effects()` lists.

fields.name: effect
fields.doc: Its id: `"minecraft:speed"`.

fields.name: ticks
fields.doc: How long it has left; -1 for ever.

fields.name: amplifier
fields.doc: Its strength above the first: 0 is level I.

fields.name: ambient
fields.doc: Whether its particles are faint, as from a beacon.

fields.name: particles
fields.doc: Whether it shows particles.

fields.name: icon
fields.doc: Whether it shows an icon.

shapes.name: PathOptions
shapes.doc: How a mob walks where `move_to` sends it. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: speed
fields.doc: How fast, times its own walking speed (its `movement_speed` attribute): 1 walks, 1.5 hurries. More than 0. Default 1.

shapes.name: MobGoal
shapes.doc: One of a mob's goals: what `mob:goals` lists.

fields.name: key
fields.doc: Its key: `"minecraft:random_stroll"` for one of the game's, `"<namespace>:guard_post"` for one the project added, or another plugin's.

fields.name: priority
fields.doc: Its priority, the game's goals' too: smaller is more important. A goal takes its controls from running goals with a bigger number.

fields.name: controls
fields.doc: What it claims while it runs, so no less important goal claiming the same runs with it: `"move"`, `"look"`, `"jump"`, `"target"` (a targeting goal). Empty for a goal that claims none of these.

fields.name: running
fields.doc: Whether it runs now.

shapes.name: GoalDefinition
shapes.doc: A goal written in Lua, for `mob:add_goal`. Each callback gets the mob. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: priority
fields.doc: How important it is: smaller goes first. A goal takes its controls from running goals with a bigger number, and waits for those with a smaller one or the same. The game's goals use about 0 (swimming up in water) to 8 (looking about).

fields.name: controls
fields.doc: What it claims while it runs, so no less important goal claiming the same runs with it: `"move"` (it walks the mob), `"look"`, `"jump"`, or `"target"` alone (it picks what the mob fights). Default none: it runs alongside the goals that claim something, and one at a time with the others that claim nothing.

fields.name: should_start
fields.doc: Whether to start now, asked every tick or two while it isn't running. Default: always.

fields.name: should_continue
fields.doc: Whether to keep running, asked every tick or two while it runs. Default: what `should_start` says.

fields.name: start
fields.doc: It starts running.

fields.name: tick
fields.doc: While it runs: every tick or two, as the game updates its goals.

fields.name: stop
fields.doc: It stopped: `should_continue` said no, a more important goal took one of its controls, or it was removed while running.

shapes.name: GoalClearOptions
shapes.doc: Which goals `mob:clear_goals` leaves. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: keep
fields.doc: The keys of goals to keep, as `remove_goal` takes them: `{ "float" }` keeps `"minecraft:float"`, so a mob still swims.

shapes.name: AttributeModifier
shapes.doc: One modifier on an entity's attribute: what `living:attribute_modifiers` lists.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Its full id: `"<namespace>:slow_zone"` for one a script added, or the game's own (`"minecraft:sprinting"`), an item's, another plugin's.

fields.name: amount
fields.doc: How much.

fields.name: operation
fields.doc: How `amount` applies: added; added times the base value; or the total multiplied by `1 + amount`.

shapes.name: TitleOptions
shapes.doc: How long a title takes. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: fade_in
fields.doc: Ticks it takes to appear. Default 10.

fields.name: stay
fields.doc: Ticks it stays. Default 70.

fields.name: fade_out
fields.doc: Ticks it takes to go. Default 20.

shapes.name: EntityDamageEvent
shapes.doc: Something is hurting an entity: heard by the entity, then `nf.on("entity_damage")`.

fields.name: entity
fields.doc: Who is hurt.

fields.name: amount
fields.doc: How much, before armour: 2 is one heart. Writable: assign another to change it.

fields.name: cause
fields.doc: What hurt it, as Minecraft names it: `"entity_attack"`, `"projectile"`, `"fall"`, `"fire"`, `"lava"`, `"drowning"`, `"void"`, …

fields.name: attacker
fields.doc: Who did it, when someone did: for an arrow, whoever shot it.

shapes.name: EntityDeathEvent
shapes.doc: A living entity died: heard by it, then `nf.on("entity_death")`.

fields.name: entity
fields.doc: Who died. Its handle answers `nil` from now on.

fields.name: killer
fields.doc: Who killed it, when someone did.

fields.name: drops
fields.doc: What it drops. Writable: assign another list of items (or change this one) to drop those instead.

fields.name: experience
fields.doc: The experience it drops. Writable: assign another to change it.

shapes.name: EntityPathEndEvent
shapes.doc: A mob stopped walking where `move_to` sent it.

fields.name: entity
fields.doc: The mob.

fields.name: reached
fields.doc: Whether it got there, within 2 blocks; `false` when it gave up.

shapes.name: PlayerInteractEntityEvent
shapes.doc: A player right-clicked an entity: heard by the entity, then the player, then `nf.on("player_interact_entity")`.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who clicked.

fields.name: entity
fields.doc: What they clicked.

fields.name: hand
fields.doc: Which hand the click was with: the game asks for each hand in turn.

shapes.name: EntitySpawnEvent
shapes.doc: An entity is coming into a world: heard by the world, then `nf.on("entity_spawn")`.

fields.name: entity
fields.doc: What's coming. Its methods already work, so a handler can name it or tag it.

fields.name: world
fields.doc: The world it's coming into.

fields.name: cause
fields.doc: What caused it, as Minecraft names it: `"natural"`, `"spawner"`, `"breeding"`, `"command"`, `"custom"` (a plugin or a script), …

shapes.name: BanOptions
shapes.doc: How `player:ban` bans. Every key is optional; a key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: What they're told when they're kicked and when they try to join, as plain text. Default the server's own message.

fields.name: expires
fields.doc: When it runs out, as Unix time in milliseconds (like `nf.server.unix_time()`): a time already past is an error. Default never.

fields.name: source
fields.doc: Who banned them, as the ban list shows it. Default `"NetherForge"`.

shapes.name: AdvancementProgress
shapes.doc: How far a player is with an advancement, by its criteria's names as the advancement's own file calls them.

fields.name: done
fields.doc: The criteria they've met.

fields.name: remaining
fields.doc: The criteria left.

shapes.name: Item
shapes.doc: An item stack as a plain table: what `menu:item` returns and what `menu:set_item` takes. Only `kind` is required, or `item` instead. Read one, change a field and write it back, and nothing else about it changes: whatever the stack carries that these fields can't say (a book's pages, another plugin's data) rides along in `raw`, which you never write yourself. A field that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: The item type: `"minecraft:diamond_sword"`, or `"diamond_sword"`. Required unless `item` names a project item, whose kind it then is; an item read from the server always has it.

fields.name: item
fields.doc: The project item (`items/<id>/`) this stack is: `{ item = "ruby", count = 3 }`. Its file fills in every field the table leaves out (`nf.items.create` does the same), and the stack carries the item's namespaced id wherever it goes, so it's still a ruby in a chest, on the ground, or after a restart. A project item the project doesn't have is an error, and so is a `kind` that isn't the item's.

fields.name: count
fields.doc: 1 to 99. Defaults to 1.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Display name, MiniMessage. Not italic unless you say so.

fields.name: lore
fields.doc: Lines under the name, each MiniMessage.

fields.name: enchantments
fields.doc: Enchantment id → level: `{ ["minecraft:sharpness"] = 5 }`.

fields.name: glint
fields.doc: The enchanted shimmer without an enchantment, as menus use for "selected".

fields.name: hide_tooltip
fields.doc: No tooltip at all, for filler panes.

fields.name: damage
fields.doc: Durability used: 0 is pristine.

fields.name: item_model
fields.doc: `<pack>/<key>`: a look from one of the project's resource packs.

fields.name: tooltip_style
fields.doc: `<pack>/<key>`: a tooltip frame from one of the project's resource packs.

fields.name: equipment
fields.doc: Worn as armour or equipment, drawn as one of the project's resource packs' equipment looks: `{ asset = "gear/ruby", slot = "head" }`.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: `#RRGGBB`, for dyed leather, potions and maps.

fields.name: profile
fields.doc: Whose head, for a player head: a name or a UUID.

fields.name: max_stack_size
fields.doc: How many fit in one stack, 1 to 99, instead of the kind's own. More than 1 on an item that takes damage (a sword, armour) is an error.

fields.name: rarity
fields.doc: The colour of its name when it has no colour of its own: white, yellow, aqua or light purple.

fields.name: attribute_modifiers
fields.doc: What it changes about whoever wears or holds it: `{ { attribute = "minecraft:attack_damage", amount = 6, operation = "add_value", slot = "main_hand" } }`. These replace the kind's own (a sword's damage) rather than adding to them.

fields.name: can_break
fields.doc: Block kinds a player in adventure mode can break with it: `{ "minecraft:stone" }`.

fields.name: can_place_on
fields.doc: Block kinds a player in adventure mode can place it on.

fields.name: food
fields.doc: What eating it does. Any item with `food` can be eaten, even one that isn't food: `{ nutrition = 4, saturation = 2.4 }`.

fields.name: cooldown
fields.doc: A cooldown after using it (an ender pearl's): `{ seconds = 2 }`. Items with the same `group` share one.

fields.name: data
fields.doc: Your script's own data, saved on the stack itself (its persistent data container), so it goes wherever the item goes: tag a coin with `data = { coin = true }`. A table keyed by strings, holding what a `data()` table may: strings, numbers, booleans, tables of them, `Vec3`s, `Location`s, `Item` tables, and `Player` and `Centity` handles, which come back as the same types. Absent when the stack carries none. Anything else (a function, a `Menu` window) is an error, naming where it was.

fields.name: raw
fields.doc: Everything else the stack carries, opaque. Present only when the fields above don't say it all. Leave it alone: it's how a read-change-write keeps what you didn't change.

shapes.name: ItemAttributeModifier
shapes.doc: One of an item's `attribute_modifiers`: how much it changes one attribute of whoever wears or holds it.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: A namespaced id telling it apart from the item's other modifiers. Default `"<namespace>:<attribute>_<index>"` (the project's namespace, and its place in the list from 0), which is what you get back when it has that one.

fields.name: attribute
fields.doc: The attribute: `"minecraft:attack_damage"`, `"minecraft:movement_speed"`, `"minecraft:max_health"`, …

fields.name: amount
fields.doc: How much.

fields.name: operation
fields.doc: How `amount` applies: added; added times the base value; or the total multiplied by `1 + amount`.

fields.name: slot
fields.doc: Where the item has to be for it to count. Default `"any"`.

shapes.name: ItemFood
shapes.doc: What eating an item does: an `Item`'s `food`.

fields.name: nutrition
fields.doc: Hunger points it restores (a full bar is 20).

fields.name: saturation
fields.doc: Saturation it adds.

fields.name: can_always_eat
fields.doc: Whether it can be eaten when full. Default false.

fields.name: eat_seconds
fields.doc: How long eating it takes. Default 1.6.

shapes.name: ItemEquipment
shapes.doc: What an item looks like worn, and where: an `Item`'s `equipment` (the `equippable` component).

fields.name: asset
fields.doc: `<pack>/<key>`: an equipment look from one of the project's resource packs.

fields.name: slot
fields.doc: The slot it is worn in: `"body"` is a horse's or wolf's armour.

shapes.name: ItemCooldown
shapes.doc: A cooldown after using an item: an `Item`'s `cooldown`.

fields.name: seconds
fields.doc: How long, more than 0.

fields.name: group
fields.doc: A namespaced id: items in one group share a cooldown (`player:set_item_cooldown` takes it too). Default: the item's kind.

shapes.name: MenuOpenOptions
shapes.doc: What `player:open_menu` opens a window with.

fields.name: context
fields.doc: Anything at all, handed to the new window: its script reads it with `this:context()`, and every event on the window carries it as `event.context`. It's the very value, kept on the server, so a table can carry handles and functions. A shared menu has one window for everyone, so giving it a context is an error.

shapes.name: DialogOpenOptions
shapes.doc: What `player:open_dialog`, `dialog:open_for` and `dialog:ask` open a dialog with. Everything here is for this one opening: the dialog's file doesn't change, and the next opening starts from it again.

fields.name: context
fields.doc: Anything at all, handed back as `event.context` on every press (and on `close`) of this opening. Kept on the server for this player until the dialog leaves their screen, never sent to them, so it can carry handles and functions.

fields.name: values
fields.doc: What its inputs start at, by input key, instead of the file's `initial`: a string for a text input, the option's `id` for a `single_option`, a number within the range for a `number_range`, `true` or `false` for a `boolean`. An input the dialog doesn't have is an error.

fields.name: title
fields.doc: The title for this opening, MiniMessage, instead of the file's.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: Body text for this opening, MiniMessage, by the body element's `key`: a message's text, or an item's description. A key no body element of the dialog has is an error.

shapes.name: MenuEvent
shapes.doc: Someone opened or closed a menu window.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who.

fields.name: menu
fields.doc: The window.

fields.name: context
fields.doc: What the script that opened the window passed along (`player:open_menu(menu, { context = ... })`), the same as `menu:context()`: the very value, not a copy. `nil` when nothing was, and always for a shared window.

shapes.name: MenuClickEvent
shapes.doc: Someone clicked while a menu window was open. A click on one of the window's slots is heard by the slot, then the menu, then `nf.on("menu_click")`; a click anywhere else starts at the menu.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who clicked.

fields.name: menu
fields.doc: The window.

fields.name: target
fields.doc: The window's slot that was clicked, or `nil` for a click in the player's own inventory or outside both.

fields.name: index
fields.doc: The slot clicked, from 0: in the window when `in_menu` is true, and in the player's own inventory below it otherwise. `nil` for a click outside both.

fields.name: in_menu
fields.doc: Whether the click landed in the window rather than in the player's own inventory below it.

fields.name: click
fields.doc: What kind of click it was.

fields.name: hotbar_index
fields.doc: For `number_key`: the hotbar slot, 0 to 8.

fields.name: item
fields.doc: What was in the slot clicked.

fields.name: cursor_item
fields.doc: What the player was carrying on the cursor.

fields.name: context
fields.doc: What the script that opened the window passed along (`player:open_menu(menu, { context = ... })`), the same as `menu:context()`: the very value, not a copy. `nil` when nothing was, and always for a shared window.

shapes.name: MenuDragEvent
shapes.doc: Someone dragged a stack across slots of a menu window.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who dragged.

fields.name: menu
fields.doc: The window.

fields.name: indices
fields.doc: The window's slots the stack is spread over, from 0, in order.

fields.name: cursor_item
fields.doc: The stack being dragged.

fields.name: context
fields.doc: What the script that opened the window passed along (`player:open_menu(menu, { context = ... })`), the same as `menu:context()`: the very value, not a copy. `nil` when nothing was, and always for a shared window.

shapes.name: DialogPressEvent
shapes.doc: Someone pressed a dialog's button: heard by the button, then the dialog, then `nf.on("dialog_press")`.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who pressed it.

fields.name: dialog
fields.doc: The dialog.

fields.name: target
fields.doc: The button pressed.

fields.name: key
fields.doc: The button's `key`.

fields.name: values
fields.doc: Every input's answer, by its `key`: the text typed, the option's `id`, the slider's number, or a checkbox's `onTrue`/`onFalse` string (`"true"`/`"false"` unless the file says otherwise).

fields.name: context
fields.doc: What the script that opened the dialog passed along for this opening (`player:open_dialog(dialog, { context = ... })`): the very value, not a copy. It's kept on the server, never sent to the player, so it can be anything at all. `nil` when nothing was.

shapes.name: DialogEvent
shapes.doc: Someone left a dialog without pressing a button, or a script closed it.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who.

fields.name: dialog
fields.doc: The dialog.

fields.name: context
fields.doc: What the script that opened the dialog passed along for this opening (`player:open_dialog(dialog, { context = ... })`): the very value, not a copy. It's kept on the server, never sent to the player, so it can be anything at all. `nil` when nothing was.

shapes.name: ItemMatch
shapes.doc: A partial `Item` that picks stacks: a stack matches when every field given matches, so `{ kind = "minecraft:paper", name = "<gold>Ticket" }` finds gold tickets and nothing else. `kind` may be left out (any kind), and `data` matches as a subset: `{ data = { coin = true } }` finds coins whatever else they carry. `count` and `raw` have no place in a match; a field `Item` doesn't have is an error.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: The item type: `"minecraft:diamond_sword"`, or `"diamond_sword"`. Required unless `item` names a project item, whose kind it then is; an item read from the server always has it.

fields.name: item
fields.doc: The project item (`items/<id>/`) this stack is: `{ item = "ruby", count = 3 }`. Its file fills in every field the table leaves out (`nf.items.create` does the same), and the stack carries the item's namespaced id wherever it goes, so it's still a ruby in a chest, on the ground, or after a restart. A project item the project doesn't have is an error, and so is a `kind` that isn't the item's.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Display name, MiniMessage. Not italic unless you say so.

fields.name: lore
fields.doc: Lines under the name, each MiniMessage.

fields.name: enchantments
fields.doc: Enchantment id → level: `{ ["minecraft:sharpness"] = 5 }`.

fields.name: glint
fields.doc: The enchanted shimmer without an enchantment, as menus use for "selected".

fields.name: hide_tooltip
fields.doc: No tooltip at all, for filler panes.

fields.name: damage
fields.doc: Durability used: 0 is pristine.

fields.name: item_model
fields.doc: `<pack>/<key>`: a look from one of the project's resource packs.

fields.name: tooltip_style
fields.doc: `<pack>/<key>`: a tooltip frame from one of the project's resource packs.

fields.name: equipment
fields.doc: Worn as armour or equipment, drawn as one of the project's resource packs' equipment looks: `{ asset = "gear/ruby", slot = "head" }`.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: `#RRGGBB`, for dyed leather, potions and maps.

fields.name: profile
fields.doc: Whose head, for a player head: a name or a UUID.

fields.name: max_stack_size
fields.doc: How many fit in one stack, 1 to 99, instead of the kind's own. More than 1 on an item that takes damage (a sword, armour) is an error.

fields.name: rarity
fields.doc: The colour of its name when it has no colour of its own: white, yellow, aqua or light purple.

fields.name: attribute_modifiers
fields.doc: What it changes about whoever wears or holds it: `{ { attribute = "minecraft:attack_damage", amount = 6, operation = "add_value", slot = "main_hand" } }`. These replace the kind's own (a sword's damage) rather than adding to them.

fields.name: can_break
fields.doc: Block kinds a player in adventure mode can break with it: `{ "minecraft:stone" }`.

fields.name: can_place_on
fields.doc: Block kinds a player in adventure mode can place it on.

fields.name: food
fields.doc: What eating it does. Any item with `food` can be eaten, even one that isn't food: `{ nutrition = 4, saturation = 2.4 }`.

fields.name: cooldown
fields.doc: A cooldown after using it (an ender pearl's): `{ seconds = 2 }`. Items with the same `group` share one.

fields.name: data
fields.doc: Your script's own data, saved on the stack itself (its persistent data container), so it goes wherever the item goes: tag a coin with `data = { coin = true }`. A table keyed by strings, holding what a `data()` table may: strings, numbers, booleans, tables of them, `Vec3`s, `Location`s, `Item` tables, and `Player` and `Centity` handles, which come back as the same types. Absent when the stack carries none. Anything else (a function, a `Menu` window) is an error, naming where it was.

shapes.name: CommandDefinition
shapes.doc: How `nf.commands.register` describes a command: everything optional. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: One line for the server's help.

fields.name: permission
fields.doc: A permission node the sender needs. On Paper the command (or subcommand) doesn't exist for a player without it: not in tab completion, not when typed. The console has every permission.

fields.name: aliases
fields.doc: Other names for it.

fields.name: arguments
fields.doc: What comes after it, in order. Arguments with a `default` are optional and must come last; a `text` argument takes the rest of the line, so it must be the last one.

fields.name: subcommands
fields.doc: Words that can come next, each with its own arguments, permission and handler: `{ add = { ... }, remove = { ... } }`. Names are lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`. A subcommand wins over an argument when both could take the word.

fields.name: players_only
fields.doc: Refuses the console (and command blocks) with a message, so the handler can count on `event.player`. A subcommand under a `players_only` command is players-only too.

shapes.name: Subcommand
shapes.doc: A word after a command (or after another subcommand) with its own arguments and handler: `/shop give <player>`. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: One line for the server's help.

fields.name: permission
fields.doc: A permission node the sender needs. On Paper the command (or subcommand) doesn't exist for a player without it: not in tab completion, not when typed. The console has every permission.

fields.name: arguments
fields.doc: What comes after it, in order. Arguments with a `default` are optional and must come last; a `text` argument takes the rest of the line, so it must be the last one.

fields.name: subcommands
fields.doc: Words that can come next, each with its own arguments, permission and handler: `{ add = { ... }, remove = { ... } }`. Names are lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`. A subcommand wins over an argument when both could take the word.

fields.name: players_only
fields.doc: Refuses the console (and command blocks) with a message, so the handler can count on `event.player`. A subcommand under a `players_only` command is players-only too.

fields.name: handler
fields.doc: Runs when someone types it. A handler that errors is logged and whoever typed the command is told; the command stays.

shapes.name: CommandArgument
shapes.doc: One argument of a command. Its `type` decides what may be typed, what tab completion offers, the usage message, and the value the handler gets in `event.arguments[name]`. On Paper it's a real Brigadier argument, so the player's client checks and completes it as they type. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Its key in `event.arguments`, and what the usage message shows (`<amount>`). Letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit; unique within the command.

fields.name: type
fields.doc: What it takes, and what the handler gets: `"word"`: one word, a `string`. `"text"`: the rest of the line, spaces and all, a `string`. `"integer"`: a whole number, within `min` and `max` when given, a `integer`. `"number"`: any number, within `min` and `max` when given, a `number`. `"boolean"`: `true` or `false`, a `boolean`. `"choice"`: one of `choices`, as typed, a `string`. `"player"`: an online player by name, or a selector that picks exactly one (`@p`, `@s`), a `Player`. `"players"`: a name or a selector (`@a`, `@a[distance=..10]`) picking at least one player, a `Player[]`. `"entity"`: a selector that picks exactly one entity, an online player's name, or a loaded entity's UUID (a `Player` for a player), an `Entity`. `"entities"`: a selector, name or UUID picking at least one entity, an `Entity[]`. `"world"`: a loaded world by name, a `World`. `"position"`: three coordinates, each a number, `~` (relative to the sender) or `^` (local to where they look); whole numbers are block centres in x and z, as in vanilla commands, a `Vec3`. `"location"`: the same three coordinates, in the sender's world facing the way they face (the default world and no facing from the console), a `Location`. `"block_state"`: a block state like `oak_stairs[facing=east]`, given back in full with every property (`"minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=bottom,…]"`), a `string`. `"item"`: an item like `diamond_sword`, or with components on Paper (`diamond_sword[enchantments={sharpness:3}]`), an `Item`. `"centity"`: a live centity by its instance id (completed from the live ones), a `Centity`. `"centity_kind"`: one of the project's centities, by its folder name, a `string`. `"menu"`: one of the project's menus, by its id, a `string`. `"dialog"`: one of the project's dialogs, by its id, a `Dialog`.

fields.name: default
fields.doc: Makes it optional: the value the handler gets when it's left out. A value of the argument's type (a number for `integer`, a `Vec3` for `position`, one of `choices` for `choice`), or `false` for "nothing", the way to make a `player` or `item` argument optional: then `event.arguments.target or event.player`.

fields.name: min
fields.doc: The smallest value an `integer` or `number` argument takes.

fields.name: max
fields.doc: The largest value an `integer` or `number` argument takes.

fields.name: choices
fields.doc: What a `choice` argument takes: single words. Required for `choice`, and only for it.

fields.name: complete
fields.doc: Tab completion of its own, instead of what its type offers. Gets the event so far (`event.arguments` holds the arguments before this one) and what has been typed of this argument; returns the suggestions. NetherForge keeps those starting with `partial`. Runs in the module's scope, within its instruction budget, every time a player's client asks, so keep it cheap.

shapes.name: CommandEvent
shapes.doc: What a command handler, and an argument's `complete`, receives.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The command's name, as registered.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: What they typed to run it: the name, or one of its aliases.

fields.name: arguments
fields.doc: The arguments by name, typed by their declaration: a `Player` for a `player` argument, a `Vec3` for a `position`, an `integer` for an `integer`. An optional argument left out has its `default`.

fields.name: input
fields.doc: Everything typed after the command's name, subcommands included, as typed.

fields.name: sender
fields.doc: Who ran it, player or console. Answer them with `event.sender:send_message(text)`.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: The player who ran it, or `nil` from the console. Never `nil` in a `players_only` command.

shapes.name: WorldCreateOptions
shapes.doc: How `nf.worlds.create` makes a world. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: generator
fields.doc: Which of the game's own world types generates it: the usual (`"normal"`), the default superflat (`"flat"`), nothing at all (`"void"`, for maps built or placed by scripts), or one of the other vanilla world types (`"amplified"`, `"large_biomes"`). Default `"normal"`. Not with `terrain`, which is one of the project's instead. Only a `"normal"` environment takes it: a nether or an end always generates as the game's own.

fields.name: terrain
fields.doc: One of the project's terrains (`terrain/<id>.json`; `"acme:hills"` for a package's), which generates it in place of the game's own. Not with `generator`. Kept with the world, so it generates the same way when it's loaded again; a terrain the project changes later only shapes chunks generated afterwards. A world with a terrain is a `"normal"` environment.

fields.name: environment
fields.doc: Which kind of dimension: its sky, its light, whether water boils. Default `"normal"`.

fields.name: dimension_type
fields.doc: One of the project's dimension types (`dimension_types/<id>.json`; `"acme:deep"` for a package's): the world's build limits, light, sky and rules (beds, respawn anchors, piglins, raids) are its. Kept with the world, so it loads the same again. The server learns dimension types only as it starts: one it didn't start with (added or fixed since) is an error until it restarts. Default: the environment's own (the game's overworld, nether or end).

fields.name: seed
fields.doc: Its seed: a project generator makes the same world for the same seed. Default: a random one.

fields.name: structures
fields.doc: Whether villages, temples and the like generate. Default `true`.

fields.name: keep_spawn_loaded
fields.doc: Whether the chunks around its spawn stay loaded with nobody near. Default `false`.

shapes.name: WorldUnloadOptions
shapes.doc: How `world:unload` lets a world go. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: save
fields.doc: Whether it saves first. Default `true`; `false` throws away what changed since the last save (with `delete`, nothing is saved either way).

fields.name: delete
fields.doc: Whether its files are deleted afterwards, and the project forgets it. Default `false`.

fields.name: move_players_to
fields.doc: Which world the players in it go to, at its spawn. Default: the main world. To send them somewhere exact, teleport them before unloading.

shapes.name: BorderSizeOptions
shapes.doc: How `border:set_size` changes it. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: ticks
fields.doc: How long it takes to get there, moving steadily. Default 0: at once.

shapes.name: BorderDamage
shapes.doc: How a border hurts players outside it: what `border:damage()` gives and `border:set_damage` takes. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: amount
fields.doc: Damage each second for every block past `buffer` (half a heart is 1). The game starts at 0.2.

fields.name: buffer
fields.doc: How many blocks outside the border are safe. The game starts at 5.

shapes.name: BorderWarning
shapes.doc: When players' screens turn red as a border comes near: what `border:warning()` gives and `border:set_warning` takes. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: distance
fields.doc: Within this many blocks of it. The game starts at 5.

fields.name: ticks
fields.doc: When a shrinking border will reach them within this many ticks. The game starts at 300 (15 seconds).

shapes.name: StructureSaveOptions
shapes.doc: What `world:save_structure` keeps. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: entities
fields.doc: Whether the entities in the box are saved with the blocks (never players, and never what centities are drawn with). Default `false`.

shapes.name: StructurePlaceOptions
shapes.doc: How `world:place_structure` places one. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: rotation
fields.doc: How far it turns clockwise (seen from above) about its smallest corner, in degrees: 0, 90, 180 or 270 (any multiple of 90). Default 0.

fields.name: mirror
fields.doc: Whether it's mirrored first: `"left_right"` flips it along z, `"front_back"` along x. Default `"none"`.

fields.name: integrity
fields.doc: How much of it is placed, 0 to 1: each block is kept with this chance. Default 1: all of it.

fields.name: entities
fields.doc: Whether the entities saved with it are placed too. Default `true`.

shapes.name: BlockSetOptions
shapes.doc: How a block is changed. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: update
fields.doc: Whether its neighbours react (sand falls, redstone updates, water flows), as when a player places a block. Default `true`; `false` sets it quietly.

shapes.name: ParticleOptions
shapes.doc: How particles are spawned. Every key is optional; which ones a particle takes depends on its kind, and one it doesn't take is an error, as is any key that isn't one of these.

fields.name: count
fields.doc: How many, scattered around the position by `spread`. Default 1. With 0, one particle is sent moving along `spread` (a direction) at `speed`.

fields.name: spread
fields.doc: How far they scatter along each axis (a Gaussian spread), in blocks. Default none. With `count = 0`, the direction the one particle moves in.

fields.name: speed
fields.doc: How fast they move, for particles that move. Default 0.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: `"#rrggbb"`: dust, dust that changes colour, and coloured particles. Default white.

fields.name: to_color
fields.doc: `"#rrggbb"`: what dust that changes colour fades to. Default white.

fields.name: size
fields.doc: How big dust is, 0.01 to 4. Default 1.

fields.name: block_state
fields.doc: Which block block particles are made of: `"minecraft:stone"`. Required for those.

fields.name: item
fields.doc: Which item item particles show. Required for those.

fields.name: viewers
fields.doc: Only these players see them (those near enough). Default: everyone near enough.

fields.name: force
fields.doc: Show them even to players who turned particles down, and from up to 128 blocks away. Default `false`.

shapes.name: SoundOptions
shapes.doc: How a sound plays. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: volume
fields.doc: How loud, from 0. Default 1. Above 1 it carries further rather than getting louder: 16 blocks per 1.

fields.name: pitch
fields.doc: How high, 0.5 (an octave down) to 2 (an octave up). Default 1.

fields.name: category
fields.doc: Which of the player's volume sliders it follows. Default `"master"`.

shapes.name: WeatherOptions
shapes.doc: How weather set with `world:set_weather` lasts. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: ticks
fields.doc: How long it lasts before the game picks again (at least 1). Leave it out for a random length, as the game chooses.

shapes.name: ExplosionOptions
shapes.doc: How an explosion behaves. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: fire
fields.doc: Whether it sets fires. Default `false`.

fields.name: break_blocks
fields.doc: Whether it breaks blocks. Default `true`.

shapes.name: BiomeSearchOptions
shapes.doc: Where `world:locate_biome` looks. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: near
fields.doc: Where it looks from, in this world. Default the world's spawn.

fields.name: radius
fields.doc: How far it looks, in blocks across: 1 to 6400. Default 6400, as `/locate biome`.

shapes.name: LightningOptions
shapes.doc: How lightning strikes. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: effect_only
fields.doc: Only the flash and the thunder: no fire, no damage. Default `false`.

shapes.name: RaycastOptions
shapes.doc: What a ray can hit. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: blocks
fields.doc: Whether blocks stop it. Default `true`.

fields.name: entities
fields.doc: Whether entities (players included) stop it, by their hitboxes. Default `true`.

fields.name: ignore
fields.doc: Entities it goes through: the one it's cast from, usually. Default none.

fields.name: centities
fields.doc: Whether centities' hitboxes stop it. Default `true`.

fields.name: fluids
fields.doc: Whether water and lava stop it, as solid blocks. Default `false`: it goes through them.

shapes.name: RaycastHit
shapes.doc: What `world:raycast` hit: where, and what. Exactly one of `block`, `entity` and `centity` is set.

fields.name: position
fields.doc: Where the ray met it, in the world.

fields.name: normal
fields.doc: The unit direction straight out of the face it hit, in the world.

fields.name: distance
fields.doc: How far along the ray that is, in blocks.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: The block it hit, or `nil`.

fields.name: entity
fields.doc: The entity it hit, or `nil`.

fields.name: centity
fields.doc: The centity whose hitbox it hit, or `nil`.

fields.name: node
fields.doc: Which node of `centity` it hit (its hitbox), or `nil` for anything else.

shapes.name: BossBarOptions
shapes.doc: What `nf.bossbars.create` makes a bar with. Every key is optional; a key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: text
fields.doc: What it says, MiniMessage. Default none.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: Default `"pink"`, the way vanilla bars start.

fields.name: style
fields.doc: One bar, or split into notches. Default `"progress"`, one bar.

fields.name: progress
fields.doc: How full, 0 to 1. Default 1.

shapes.name: LootContext
shapes.doc: What `nf.loot.roll` and `nf.loot.fill` roll with: who and what the roll is for, which the table's conditions ask about. Every key is optional; a key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: The player behind the roll: who killed the mob, broke the block or opened the chest. A `player` condition passes only with one. Default none.

fields.name: tool
fields.doc: What the player killed or broke it with, for `tool` and `enchantment` conditions. Default none: those conditions don't pass.

fields.name: luck
fields.doc: The roll's luck: more `bonusRolls`, and each entry's weight shifted by its `quality`. Default 0.

fields.name: looted
fields.doc: The entity whose loot this is, which a game table for a mob needs. Default none.

fields.name: location
fields.doc: Where a game table is rolled. Default the player's place, else the looted entity's.

fields.name: seed
fields.doc: Rolls with this seed give the same items every time, on the server and in the editor. Default a new one each roll.

shapes.name: ProjectBlockPlaceEvent
shapes.doc: A block is about to be placed.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who is placing it, or `nil` for a script.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: Where it goes: what is there now is replaced, so `block:custom()` is `nil` until it has been placed (`this:id()` says which block is being placed).

fields.name: item
fields.doc: The stack placing it, or `nil` for a script.

shapes.name: ProjectBlockClickEvent
shapes.doc: A block was clicked.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who clicked.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: The block.

fields.name: click
fields.doc: Which button: the left (hit) or right (use).

fields.name: face
fields.doc: Which face of the block was clicked.

fields.name: item
fields.doc: What's in the hand the click was with, or `nil` for an empty hand.

fields.name: hand
fields.doc: Which hand: the game asks for each hand in turn.

shapes.name: ProjectBlockTickEvent
shapes.doc: A block ticked.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: The block that ticked.

shapes.name: TeamOptions
shapes.doc: What `nf.teams.create` makes a team with. Every key is optional; a key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: display_name
fields.doc: What it's called where Minecraft names a team, MiniMessage. Default its name.

fields.name: prefix
fields.doc: What goes before each member's name, MiniMessage. Default none.

fields.name: suffix
fields.doc: What goes after each member's name, MiniMessage. Default none.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: The colour of members' names and glow. Default none.

fields.name: friendly_fire
fields.doc: Whether members can hurt each other. Default `true`.

fields.name: see_invisible_teammates
fields.doc: Whether members see each other while invisible. Default `true`.

fields.name: nametags
fields.doc: `"always"` (the default), `"never"`, `"hide_for_other_teams"` (only teammates see them) or `"hide_for_own_team"` (only players outside the team see them).

fields.name: collision
fields.doc: `"always"` (the default), `"never"`, `"push_other_teams"` (members pass through each other) or `"push_own_team"` (members push only each other).

shapes.name: ScheduleOptions
shapes.doc: What a schedule is called and what to do about a run the server missed. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: A name for the schedule, which what it last ran is kept under, so it's known across restarts. Lowercase letters, digits and `_` (starting with a letter or digit, at most 64 characters), and no two of a package's live schedules share one. Default none: the schedule is forgotten when it stops.

fields.name: catch_up
fields.doc: Run once when the script starts if a run was missed since the schedule last ran (the server was off over its time). Needs an `id`; a schedule seen for the first time has missed nothing. Default `false`: a missed run is skipped.

shapes.name: DatabaseStatement
shapes.doc: One statement of `db:transaction`.

fields.name: sql
fields.doc: One SQL statement in the database's own dialect (SQLite's for the package's own database; MySQL's or PostgreSQL's for a connection the server owner set up), with `?` where a value goes: the values come in `params`, never inside the text, so a name a player typed can't become SQL. A second statement after a `;` is an error: use `db:transaction` for several. On PostgreSQL a literal `?` (the JSON operators) is written `??`.

fields.name: params
fields.doc: The values for the `?`s, in order: `{ player_name, 5 }`. Each is a `string`, `number`, `integer` or `boolean` (stored as 1 or 0); a hole in the list (`{ 1, nil, 3 }`) is SQL `NULL`, and so are the last `?`s when the list is shorter (Lua can't tell `{ name, nil }` from `{ name }`). Any other kind of value is an error, and more values than `?`s fails the statement.

shapes.name: DatabaseResult
shapes.doc: What `db:execute` (and each statement of `db:transaction`) did.

fields.name: changes
fields.doc: How many rows it inserted, updated or deleted.

fields.name: last_insert_id
fields.doc: On the package's own database, the `rowid` of the last row it inserted (the new row's `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`), or `nil` when nothing was ever inserted. On a MySQL connection, the `AUTO_INCREMENT` key the statement generated, or `nil` when it generated none. On PostgreSQL always `nil`: ask for the key with `INSERT ... RETURNING id` through `db:query`.

shapes.name: HttpRequestOptions
shapes.doc: What `nf.http.request` takes.

fields.name: url
fields.doc: An `http://` or `https://` URL, without a user name or password in it (send credentials in a header). Its host must be one the calling package declares in `requires`.

fields.name: method
fields.doc: The HTTP method; `"GET"` when left out.

fields.name: headers
fields.doc: Request headers by name. `Host`, `Content-Length`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Connection`, `Upgrade` and the like are set by the server and refused here. A `User-Agent` of `NetherForge` is sent unless you give one. `Authorization`, `Cookie` and `Proxy-Authorization` are dropped when a redirect leads to another host.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: The request body, as text (UTF-8). Its size is limited by `http.max-request-bytes` in the server's `config.yml`. A `GET`, `HEAD` or `OPTIONS` can't have one.

shapes.name: HttpResponse
shapes.doc: What `nf.http.request` gives.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: The status code: `200`, `404`.

fields.name: headers
fields.doc: The response headers by name in lowercase (`response.headers["content-type"]`); a header sent more than once is its values joined with `, `.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: The body as text, decoded by the charset the response names (UTF-8 when it names none), so a response that isn't text (an image) doesn't survive. Its size is limited by `http.max-response-bytes` in the server's `config.yml`.

fields.name: url
fields.doc: The URL the response came from: the request's own, or where its redirects ended.

shapes.name: ParticlePlayOptions
shapes.doc: How `nf.particles.play` plays an effect. Every key is optional; a key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: viewers
fields.doc: Only these players see it (still only those within range). Players who leave drop out. Default: everyone in range.

fields.name: scale
fields.doc: Multiplies its distances: shape sizes, offsets, spreads and speeds (not dust sizes). More than 0, at most 16. Default 1.

fields.name: loop
fields.doc: Whether it starts again after its last tick, until it's stopped. Default: what its file says.

fields.name: follow
fields.doc: Follow this from the start, as `effect:follow` does. Each tick, before it spawns anything, the effect moves to the target: its position (a node's `world_position()`), facing the target's yaw (a node's centity's), pitch 0. When the target stops existing (a removed centity, a player who left, an entity that died or was removed, a centity or entity whose chunk unloaded) the effect ends with reason `"target_gone"`. `location_or_position` is still needed: it's where the effect is if the target is already gone, which ends it on its first tick.

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: With `follow`: where the effect sits from the target, as for `effect:follow`. Without `follow` it's an error.

shapes.name: EffectEndEvent
shapes.doc: A particle effect ended.

fields.name: effect
fields.doc: The effect.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Why: it played to its end; `stop()` was called; what it followed went; its file was deleted; or the script that played it unloaded (a reload, its centity removed, the server stopping).

shapes.name: CutscenePlayOptions
shapes.doc: How `nf.cutscenes.play` plays a cutscene. Every key is optional; a key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: origin
fields.doc: Where the path's coordinates are measured from: every camera position is added to it (the path is moved, not turned). A `Location` also says which world the cutscene is in (its `yaw` and `pitch` are not used); a `Vec3` is in the player's world. Default: the path's coordinates are the world's, in the player's world.

fields.name: skippable
fields.doc: Whether the player may end it early by sneaking (reason `"skipped"`). Default: what the cutscene's file says, which defaults to `false`.

shapes.name: CutsceneEndEvent
shapes.doc: A cutscene ended.

fields.name: cutscene
fields.doc: The cutscene.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who was watching.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Why: it played to its end; `stop()` was called; the player sneaked, in a skippable one; another cutscene was played for the player; the player left the server; or the script that played it unloaded (a reload, the server stopping).

shapes.name: CutsceneCueEvent
shapes.doc: A cutscene reached a named cue.

fields.name: cutscene
fields.doc: The cutscene.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who is watching.

fields.name: cue
fields.doc: The cue's `event` name in the cutscene's file.

shapes.name: TimeOptions
shapes.doc: How `nf.time.format` and `nf.time.parse` read a clock time. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: zone
fields.doc: Which time zone the clock time is in: an IANA name like `"Europe/London"` or `"America/New_York"`, `"UTC"`, or an offset like `"+02:00"`. Default the server owner's zone (`schedules.time-zone` in `config.yml`, the server's own by default), the one `nf.schedule` runs in. A zone the server doesn't know is an error.

shapes.name: NoiseOptions
shapes.doc: Which noise `nf.random.noise2` and `noise3` give. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: seed
fields.doc: Which noise: each seed is a different pattern. Default 0.

fields.name: scale
fields.doc: What the coordinates are multiplied by first: smaller is smoother and wider (0.05 changes over about 20 blocks). Default 1.

shapes.name: RaisedEvent
shapes.doc: What `nf.test.raise` gives back.

fields.name: cancelled
fields.doc: Whether a handler called `event:cancel()` (always `false` for an event that can't be cancelled).

fields.name: event
fields.doc: The payload as the handlers left it: a writable field they assigned (`message`) holds what they set.

commandArguments.name: text
commandArguments.doc: the rest of the line, spaces and all

commandArguments.name: integer
commandArguments.doc: a whole number, within `min` and `max` when given

commandArguments.name: number
commandArguments.doc: any number, within `min` and `max` when given

commandArguments.name: player
commandArguments.doc: an online player by name, or a selector that picks exactly one (`@p`, `@s`)

commandArguments.name: players
commandArguments.doc: a name or a selector (`@a`, `@a[distance=..10]`) picking at least one player

commandArguments.name: entity
commandArguments.doc: a selector that picks exactly one entity, an online player's name, or a loaded entity's UUID (a `Player` for a player)

commandArguments.name: entities
commandArguments.doc: a selector, name or UUID picking at least one entity

commandArguments.name: position
commandArguments.doc: three coordinates, each a number, `~` (relative to the sender) or `^` (local to where they look); whole numbers are block centres in x and z, as in vanilla commands

commandArguments.name: location
commandArguments.doc: the same three coordinates, in the sender's world facing the way they face (the default world and no facing from the console)

commandArguments.name: block_state
commandArguments.doc: a block state like `oak_stairs[facing=east]`, given back in full with every property (`"minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=bottom,…]"`)

commandArguments.name: item
commandArguments.doc: an item like `diamond_sword`, or with components on Paper (`diamond_sword[enchantments={sharpness:3}]`)

commandArguments.name: centity
commandArguments.doc: a live centity by its instance id (completed from the live ones)

commandArguments.name: centity_kind
commandArguments.doc: one of the project's centities, by its folder name

commandArguments.name: menu
